content.title: JSON-LD from the shared page model

body:
JSON-LD from the shared page model
When you add structured data to a Theme, use the JSON-LD Gazette supplies with the page. It comes from the same PageProjection as the HTML, so the article, publisher and relationships come from the content you are rendering. The Theme chooses where to embed that data.
Set machine = { json_ld = true } in the existing brand publication binding. Gazette then supplies the template's json_ld value and writes the site's site.jsonld file. Embed the page value with the JSON script encoder:
{% if json_ld is defined %}
<script type="application/ld+json">
  {{ json_ld | json_script }}
</script>
{% endif %}

json_script encodes the supplied value for a script element. Use it instead of interpolating raw JSON; it needs no additional safe filter. The filter handles encoding, while Gazette's page model determines what the data says.
Important

Local builds can include drafts. Check the selected pages before exposing their output. Producing JSON-LD does not publish the page or guarantee that a search engine will index it or show a rich result.
For the publisher's setup, follow Help readers find the work.
Read an emitted article graph
The first-publication tutorial contains an article, “Keep the observation with its context”, inside the Field Notes collection. Enable JSON-LD in that publication and render the article. This excerpt keeps its identities and breadcrumb relationship; other properties are omitted:
{
  "@context": {
    "@version": 1.1,
    "@vocab": "https://schema.org/",
    "url": {
      "@id": "https://schema.org/url",
      "@type": "@id"
    }
  },
  "@id": "https://field-notes.example/keep-the-context/#article",
  "@type": "Article",
  "identifier": "content:keep-the-context",
  "url": "https://field-notes.example/keep-the-context/",
  "mainEntityOfPage": {
    "@id": "https://field-notes.example/keep-the-context/",
    "@type": "WebPage",
    "name": "Keep the observation with its context",
    "url": "https://field-notes.example/keep-the-context/",
    "breadcrumb": [
      {
        "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
        "numberOfItems": 2,
        "itemListElement": [
          {
            "@type": "ListItem",
            "position": 1,
            "name": "Field Notes",
            "item": { "@id": "https://field-notes.example/" }
          },
          {
            "@type": "ListItem",
            "position": 2,
            "name": "Keep the observation with its context",
            "item": { "@id": "https://field-notes.example/keep-the-context/" }
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Start with the article's identifier: content:keep-the-context is the key from its source. Its url comes from the resolved page route. In this example the serving and canonical addresses coincide. Local-link previews use their loopback routes; syndicated copies keep a separate reference to the original page.
Next, follow mainEntityOfPage. The article and the WebPage carrying it share a URL here but have distinct public identities: the article uses the canonical address plus #article, while its page uses the canonical address. The article holds the content key, lifecycle, language and keywords; the page holds only its name, address and place, so the same facts are not stated twice. This lets the breadcrumb name the page without treating the article itself as a WebPage. The BreadcrumbList starts at Field Notes and ends at that presentation page. Gazette takes its positions from the collection structure, not from path segments or alphabetical order.
When debugging a Theme, compare the page model's json_ld with the JSON decoded from that page's application/ld+json script. They should describe the same value. For site.jsonld, compare the corresponding discovery/listing entry in pages[id].json_ld: that entry can omit relationships present on the direct page. The tutorial remains draft content for local learning, so its direct page graph alone is no reason to include it in a public index.
Identities and vocabulary
Public page values, generated listings and site.jsonld use Schema.org terms with a local JSON-LD 1.1 context. Gazette includes that context instead of fetching one. The public serializer selects supported publication facts explicitly; it does not rename internal evidence, provenance or operational state into superficially similar standard properties.
A content key stays a literal identifier. Routed works use canonical public IRIs: an article uses its canonical page address plus #article, and its presenting WebPage uses the canonical address. Other pages, collections, journeys and generated listings use their canonical page addresses. These identities stay public in local previews while serving url fields may use loopback addresses. Breadcrumbs, article presentation pages, linked works and public ItemLists use the same identities. Unrouted works retain document-local blank nodes; equal blank-node labels across separate documents do not establish shared identity. A principal with a configured website uses that website's canonical address plus #person or #organization, so every page and site names the same person or organisation; give each principal of a kind its own website. A principal without a website, and each scoped taxonomy term, keeps a document-local blank node. Route aliases do not become sameAs.
Each document describes the page's own work once. Every other mention of a work, whether in isPartOf, hasPart, subjectOf, a journey or a listing, is a reference with its identity, content key, type, name and serving url; its keywords, lifecycle and language stay on its own page. A breadcrumb item carries the name shown in the trail and the target's @id. Empty relationships are omitted rather than written as empty arrays.
Titles supply names. Publisher, author and rights-holder fields come from their resolved declarations, with each role kept separate. Supply the principal's kind and name where needed; Gazette will not invent them from its key. The same applies to contacts, social links, dates, offers, licences and rights.
A principal's configured website supplies Person.url or Organization.url through its public canonical_url, including in preview. Configured same_as entries become sameAs references with @id values. Gazette neither discovers these entries from social profiles, aliases or publisher roles nor verifies them remotely. A Theme's navigation can still use the separate serving url to keep a preview link local.
How page fields map to JSON-LD
Use this table to trace a public property back to the page model. Private inspection includes the complete structure. Public aggregate output follows the discovery rules, filtering ineligible relationship endpoints, including breadcrumbs.
A filtered journey keeps each remaining member's original one-based position and counts only the members it lists. If any declaration behind a project relationship is ineligible, that relationship is omitted from aggregate about/mentions. Filtering this output leaves authored prose links and the underlying graph intact.
Resolved input	JSON-LD property	What to expect	
Content family	Article → Article; collection/journey or explicitly configured listing → CollectionPage; other pages → WebPage	An extension key does not create a Schema.org type or make its page an article.	
Title, lifecycle, language and retained body text	name, article-only headline, creativeWorkStatus, optional inLanguage, text	Article, BlogPosting and TechArticle reuse the article title as headline, with no new identity. Language uses the page's explicit value or publication default; unresolved language stays absent. text carries the body, not a generated summary.	
Root description and authored dates	description, datePublished, dateModified	The description stays plain text. Dates retain XML Schema date or dateTime types. Missing values stay absent, date-only values stay date-only, and shallow linked records receive no extra description or dates.	
Explicit body-summary text	abstract	The same retained prefix used by Theme and search, separate from description. An absent summary stays absent; HTML and the summary marker are excluded.	
Content licence	license with the exact URI as @id	Uses the content field, without falling back to a repository licence, fetching terms or granting publication permission.	
Site terms of use	usageInfo with the configured terms address as @id	Appears on each page's own node when the publication declares terms. It never fills an absent content license; a page's explicit licence stays alongside it.	
Site publisher	publisher with the declared Person or Organization type, optional name and configured website	Uses the exact publisher principal through the same profile projection as attributions. Publishing a site does not make the principal its author or rights holder; a site address does not become an undeclared organisation website.	
Utility-page subtype and explicit subject	AboutPage with an optional principal mainEntity, or WebPage with a distinct Service mainEntity	Uses the declared subject. An About page without a subject invents no mainEntity; existing project and brand relationships remain intact. Principal identity comes from the existing catalog. Service identity, name, provider and optional description are explicit; page titles, publishers, dates and lifecycle never fill missing service facts. Existing listing and journey ItemList identities remain unchanged.	
Scoped attributions	author, copyrightHolder	Principal kind and optional name come from the referenced person or organisation. Each role keeps its declared principals. Eligible published content uses the same site author default as its byline; a missing author does not fall back to the publisher or a guessed name.	
Direct subject and mentions	about, mentions	The explicit project kind supplies its type; omission remains Thing. Project entities use their explicit public IRI or canonical landing plus #entity. Configured internal reading destinations enter subjectOf only when their resolved relationship is About this project, with the target’s actual title, type and work identity. A Mentions index may itself declare About; its navigation label is not its relationship.	
Editorial residence	isPartOf	Keeps the direct collection or sole containing journey as a reference. Array-shaped output does not permit extra memberships; a page with neither omits the property.	
Children and editorial links	hasPart, relatedLink	Children are references with resolved serving URLs; a page without children or FAQ answers omits hasPart. A related page need not share membership or subject matter.	
Journey members	mainEntity → ItemList with positioned ListItem values	Keeps traversal order, original one-based position, exact title/type and resolved URL. A member without a route keeps its identity without a guessed link.	
Structural breadcrumb paths	breadcrumb → one BreadcrumbList per path	Positions start at one and the last item is the page itself. Each ListItem carries the trail name and the target @id. A path holding only the page itself is omitted. Missing routes stay missing.	
Literal keywords and classification bindings	keywords → strings and DefinedTerm values with inDefinedTermSet	Each term keeps its exact taxonomy identity and label; equal keys in different taxonomies remain distinct. The native view retains the taxonomy language constraint. A label does not create a subject relationship.	
Authored image occurrences	image → ImageObject values	Each occurrence keeps its resolved contentUrl, alt text as description and optional title as name. An explicitly bound figure caption supplies caption from its admitted reading text. Images inside components explicitly declared presentation_only are excluded. No image is guessed from a stylesheet, icon or unreferenced asset.	
Validated FAQ components	hasPart → FAQPage, ordered Question values and acceptedAnswer	Keeps the exact question text and admitted rich answer body, without changing the containing page type or its listing identity.	
Compiler callers select this public view with page.json_ld().public() or by applying .public() to a discovery/listing JSON-LD selection. Generated listing views provide ListingPage::public_json_ld(). These borrowed serializers retain the caller's output limits. The application uses them for templates and the site graph.
The existing page.json_ld() remains a native inspection view, including Gazette's technical namespace and complete relationship origins, evidence, provenance, project state, scoped taxonomy language, role order, primary flags and rendering coordinates. The complete asset inventory remains in the page inspection model. Public output omits those technical fields without deleting or changing the underlying facts. Source provenance and relationship evidence do not become isBasedOn or citation; availability does not become an Offer. A generic project's repository and licence remain native metadata and visible resource links, rather than falsely typing the project as software or applying CreativeWork properties to an unknown kind of thing.
Journey and listing ItemList entries use explicit positions and counts, so array ordering is not their only record of editorial order.
creativeWorkStatus carries textual work status. Publication and modification dates can be Date or DateTime values. Gazette keeps that distinction through typed values; it does not turn a date into a midnight timestamp. The accepted inputs and missing-value rules are in authored chronology.
Explicit project subjects
Declare project.kind on the owning landing or inline catalog record. The finite mapping is software-application → SoftwareApplication, software-source-code → SoftwareSourceCode, creative-work → CreativeWork, collection → Collection, project → Project, and research-project → ResearchProject. Project and ResearchProject describe organizational undertakings, not their papers, applications or source code. A collection is distinct from the CollectionPage presenting it. Omission emits Thing; filenames, repositories, page families and themes never supply a project kind.
The optional project.identity is a public HTTP(S) entity IRI. It preserves an explicit fragment, rejects credentials and local/private endpoints, and must not collide with another project or a routed work/page. Without it, the declared landing supplies its canonical public address plus #entity. Without either anchor, the subject keeps a document-local identity and its declared type; neither its name nor a URL is invented. Kind, lifecycle, visibility and availability remain independent. Only an explicitly software-source-code subject emits its repository as codeRepository; an application is not silently made identical to its source repository.
subjectOf means a work about the subject. Internal learning and article-index links are resolved against the captured graph and remain shallow, deduplicated references. Mentions-only targets keep their visible navigation links without becoming subjectOf. A configured code-documentation URL that exactly matches a validated provider page for the same project becomes a shallow WebPage reference with its public URL and available provider title. The page's physical or virtual storage form does not imply a more specific semantic type. Preview navigation keeps its local address separately. Unknown destinations retain bare IRI references; titles are never inferred from a route or project name, and incomplete provider catalogs are rejected rather than used to supply partial project metadata. Cycles do not recursively expand pages. The native inspection graph keeps its own identity scheme and relationship evidence.
Rendering, scope and failure
Breadcrumbs belong to a WebPage. An article therefore links to its presentation page through mainEntityOfPage, and that page carries the breadcrumbs under its canonical public identity. Other page families and containers carry breadcrumb directly. Breadcrumb and neighbour references use the same distinction throughout the graph.
For a syndicated article, mainEntityOfPage instead identifies the original page and its canonical URL. The copy keeps its own serving URL and publisher; its breadcrumbs, publisher and attributions are not copied onto the original's page record. See syndicated bodies.
Each BreadcrumbList keeps the path's endpoints, names and configured URLs, with explicit integer positions. The native view additionally identifies the direct container without choosing a primary path. An endpoint without a route keeps its local identity but has no URL. Collection, child, editorial-related and journey-member records likewise keep their resolved serving URLs. Ranked recommendations remain suggestions rather than becoming authored relationships or Schema.org subject claims.
The site file's @graph contains the discovery/listing values for the selected site's discoverable authored pages, followed by its generated taxonomy and listing pages. Authored pages are ordered by their resolved serving URLs. Aliases and linked foreign pages do not gain their own top-level records, though related records can appear inside a local document. Check the selected content and disclosure policy separately from this local discovery filtering. Turning JSON-LD off removes both the page field and site.jsonld; search, sitemap and llms.txt have their own settings.
Page-context, whole-file and inventory limits still apply. A missing required value, a collision or an exhausted limit fails the render rather than returning a truncated graph or substitute JSON. Building these outputs adds no wall-clock value, native path or mutable remote observation to artifact identity.

body:
Links and crossings
A crossing exists because a thought often continues in another inquiry: a link to another configured publication lets the reader follow it there without losing the argument they came from. Use Gazette's resolved link attributes to style a link that crosses from one publication to another. Gazette resolves links for the whole configured publication set. The Theme can show a destination site's visual identity while the reader stays on the page that contains the link.
How a link is classified
Destination kind	What Gazette resolved	
internal-native	A link on this publication, including a root-relative /path/	
cross-site	An address on another configured publication	
external	An address outside the configured publications	
resource	A compiled asset or download for the site	
Gazette checks declared routes, aliases and mirrors. A crossing can name another site without matching a page there. In that case the link has the destination site's information but no destination page. Gazette never requests the URL to find the page.
What a link carries
Attribute	What a Theme reads	
data-gazette-link	Stable ID for this occurrence of the link	
data-gazette-destination-kind	One of the four destination kinds	
data-gazette-destination-content	The target page's content ID, if Gazette found a page	
data-gazette-destination-site	The destination site ID, if configured	
data-gazette-destination-relationships	Existing related, collection, collection-member, journey or journey-member relationships	
data-gazette-destination-theme	The destination site's Theme package	
data-gazette-destination-palette	The destination site's palette, if configured	
An attribute appears only when Gazette has the value. Navigation entries, search records and graph nodes get the same destination Theme and palette. Read those fields to style the link. The Theme reference describes the full presentation data.
Links do not make collections, journeys or related-page declarations. The content model defines how those relationships are authored.
Writing links in site content
Link to a page in the configured publication set by domain, route and optional fragment:
Read the [[site:example.org/research/paper/#results|paper's results]].

The route can be a page's address or alias. Gazette stops the build when the site is missing or ambiguous, or the route or fragment is missing. A local preview uses the local serving address when available. A public build uses the public address. Use this syntax for page links only. Inside a table, follow links in tables so the separator remains part of the link.
Use ordinary Markdown for external URLs, such as [background](https://elsewhere.example/paper/). An absolute URL stays as written unless a preview link map points its base at a local server. Use public URLs or publication links rather than paths on your machine: a machine-local path exposes that location and does not give readers a working destination on the live site.
Authored content and article notes reject relative links to Markdown files, such as ../guide.md. Encoded or differently cased .md and .markdown suffixes follow the same rule. Repository manuals and mounted native documentation keep the relative-file contract described below.
Declare lasting relationships by ID in the frontmatter arrays before their tables:
+++
related = ["content:research-paper"]
collections = ["collection:research"]
projects = [{ project = "project:engine", kind = "about" }]

[content]
id = "content:commentary"
site = "site:example"
title = "A commentary on the paper"
lifecycle = "published"

[content.structure]
kind = "page"
family = { kind = "article" }
+++

Writing links in project documentation
Within a developer manual, use a relative link such as ./install.md or ./install.md#what-a-build-needs. Gazette rewrites it to the destination's configured page address. It stops assembly if the page or heading is missing. See Mintlify manual inputs for what can be a destination.
To reach product help, use its public URL. A preview link map can point it at the local publication. For an author’s example, see Connect publications.
What a crossing never does
A crossing does not copy the target page, add its site to the build or verify that its content is current, approved or reachable. Give it the same target size, focus, keyboard behavior and timing as other links. Use routing for redirects and aliases, including mirrors served on another site.
A citation download uses the same asset path and serving URL rules as a body link. The site build must include an asset referenced only in content.citation too. Gazette serves a .bib or PDF file as supplied without validating its contents. It does not fetch or verify external destinations.

Render publications locally
Render one or more sites from the same workspace and read the output inventory before you write anything. Start with a compiled workspace that names the sites, their content sources and Themes. The render includes drafts and archived pages unless the recipe supplies a release candidate.
I need to…	Start here	
Build several sites from one capture	Local site sets	
Inspect the model or scan the generated files	Inspect a local build	
Configure Markdown, discovery rules or static files	Prepare inputs for the renderer	
Change the Theme, resource handling or templates	Prepare templates and browser resources	
Read search records, machine files or the site graph	Read the generated site files	
Open the site in a browser or watch files	Local publication preview	
Write an existing configured output directory	Output materialization	
Use build::render_publication for one in-memory site. For several sites, the Rust SDK supplies build::acquire_publications and build::render_publications. build::stage_publication or the single-site command’s --output-parent writes a fresh private stage. Rendering grants no permission to release the site.
Local site sets
For a workspace on disk, keep its usual choices in gazette.toml:
[build]
sites = ["site:one", "site:other"]
local_drafts = "include"
corpus_bytes = 536870912
math = true

gazette render-sites --local --workspace-root /absolute/path/to/configuration-root --allow-execute

--workspace selects a different root-relative configuration document. The default is gazette.toml. --allow-execute permits this call's configured math process; the workspace cannot grant that permission. Omit it for a build that needs no native math execution. Rendering remains in memory.
Use a JSON request when the invocation needs explicit site options or a caller-owned configuration buffer. Save the following as render.json, replacing the absolute workspace root and the site IDs. Omitting sites selects [build].sites; an explicit list overrides it.
{
  "format": "gazette-local-publication-set/1",
  "workspace": {
    "kind": "local",
    "root": "/absolute/path/to/configuration-root",
    "workspace": "gazette.toml"
  },
  "sites": [
    {"site": "site:one", "model_output": "model.json"},
    {"site": "site:other", "model_output": "model.json", "graph": {"output": "graph/index.html"}}
  ]
}

Run the build without writing a stage. This workspace enables math, so permit the configured typesetter for this invocation:
gazette render-sites --local --allow-execute < render.json

Read the inventory and check the status of each site. gazette check build --local runs the same build with the same request, result and failure rules. Use it when the goal is validation. Neither command creates a stage or release record, approves output or deploys it. Use plain gazette check to check the selected workspace and its pages and check --publication to inspect the resolved model without running a Theme.
Name the workspace and sites
The tagged workspace input is either the explicit local document set shown above, or {"kind":"supplied","source":"...exact TOML..."} for a caller-owned buffer. The local root must be absolute and the workspace path root-relative; Gazette reads only that root document and its exact non-recursive include set. It never searches the current directory, ancestors or siblings. Site options name reserved output paths; the selected Theme manifest owns exact page, alias and graph entries. Unknown fields/versions, duplicate object members and empty, duplicate or over-limit site selections fail before native acquisition. Cross-links never add render targets. Configured foreign content still participates in the shared semantic graph, even when its publication is not in the requested output set.
Set the year, model file or candidate
An optional request-level render_year is a positive calendar year in 1..=9999, independent from article publication/modification dates. An explicit value wins over a boundary default. The direct CLI render and preview commands capture the current UTC year once when no command default is supplied; --render-year supplies a reproducible command default. The MCP boundary also captures the current UTC year once; an explicit recipe value takes precedence there as well. Rust SDK callers supply their own value: the compiler and renderer do not read a clock. The same exact value reaches page metadata, generated listing metadata and graph presentation metadata, and participates in build cache identity. An omitted SDK value remains omitted.
model_output is optional. Omit it when the site does not need a standalone JSON model artifact, for example {"site":"site:one"}. The shared model still feeds Theme rendering and every selected machine output. Gazette does not invent a destination for the omitted artifact; render evidence records a model path only when one was selected. Selecting a path retains the ordinary collision checks and changes the build-cache identity. The single-site render-site command has the same behavior when --model-output is omitted.
An optional selection object supplies one complete content/asset disposition map for the whole captured corpus, as described in closed candidates. It is not a site-local filter or publication approval. Omission retains private unfiltered rendering; explicit null, unknown fields, repeated keys or malformed identities/paths fail before acquisition. Candidate completeness and relationship closure are checked against the captured model before any site program runs.
Allow the math or diagram program
For the author’s setup and a first formula, return to Typeset mathematics.
The workspace chooses the math typesetter or DOT renderer and its exact source or executable pins. [build].math selects math generation; --math true or --math false overrides it for one CLI call. The recipe also accepts math and allow_execute. Selection and execution permission are separate.
Math defaults are a 2 MiB request, a 30-second deadline, 4,096 formulas and 64 MiB aggregate output. Per-formula and per-fragment limits still apply. A math_generation object selects math explicitly and can override individual defaults; {"math_generation":{"allow_execute":true}} is enough to use them. The following example deliberately chooses smaller limits and also enables diagrams:
{
  "math_generation": {
    "allow_execute": true,
    "max_input_bytes": 1048576,
    "timeout_ms": 30000,
    "formulas": 64,
    "output_bytes": 1048576
  },
  "diagram_generation": {
    "allow_execute": true,
    "max_input_bytes": 1048576,
    "timeout_ms": 30000,
    "diagrams": 16,
    "output_bytes": 1048576,
    "diagnostic_bytes": 16384
  }
}

Add only the required field to the complete recipe, rather than submitting this fragment alone. Omitted math selection follows [build].math, then defaults off; omitted diagram_generation stays off. math: false conflicts with an explicit math_generation object. Selecting a renderer in the workspace does not grant execution permission, and permission to read sources or open preview listeners does not grant it either. The Markdown reference explains the retained typesetting result; page resources describes DOT resource binding. The current named fields and bounds also appear in the native recipe schema at MCP render_sites's recipe_json.contentSchema.
Acquisition runs the selected program once and retains its input/output binding; rendering consumes that result without rerunning it. In development preview a later source capture may need a new invocation. These native processes are not sandboxed: their filesystem, network or other effects are separate from Gazette's in-memory rendering. Inspect failed or interrupted execution before deciding whether to retry.
Read results for every site
Gazette compiles the workspace, captures the files needed by the requested sites and resolves one content model. The sites share those immutable input bytes. Each site's Theme and resources render against that model without reopening files. Sites have independent output paths, so each can produce index.html. A collision within a site still fails.
Field	What the private result tells you	
status	local_set_rendered when all sites succeeded, otherwise local_set_incomplete	
sites	Every requested site. Each has rendered with its inventory and render details, or failed with its original error code and message.	
compilation, sources	One copy of the shared configuration, Git pins and captured tree identities	
source_bytes	Actual retained payload sizes: captured_total counts each source key once, shared_content is the common graph input, and sites gives each site's input footprint and additional presentation bytes. Site footprints overlap; their sum is not a disk-read total. missing_sources identifies captures whose sizes remain unknown.	
selection	The complete candidate decision, including exclusions, or null for an unfiltered render. It appears even if every site failed.	
source_failures	The errors for all presentation-only sources that failed, including shared inputs. A site's error uses its first failed source in key order.	
The CLI prints the complete structured result and exits unsuccessfully if any site failed. It keeps successful siblings in the result. Keep the report private because it can include paths and diagnostics. It is separate from the emitted files and release records.
Size the request, input and output limits
Limit	What it counts	
--max-source-bytes	Entire JSON request before decoding, 64 KiB by default	
Acquisition defaults	Up to 128 requested sites and 256 different source keys under one source budget	
--max-corpus-bytes	Aggregate authored files and opaque assets before parsing; invocation override, then [build].corpus_bytes, then 16 MiB	
--max-total-output-bytes	Combined output, 1 GiB by default	
--max-total-output-entries	Combined output, 100,000 entries by default	
Gazette reads content sources before presentation-only sources, in stable order in each group. A source used by both counts as shared content and is read once. Failed sources hold no payload and are not retried. Successful captures still count against the budget. The budget counts bytes kept, not all attempted filesystem reads or Git work. Each attempt has its own read limits.
render-site, render-sites, MCP and preview resolve the same workspace corpus setting. It also reaches math/diagram acquisition and preview rebuilds. Use --max-corpus-bytes 67108864 to override it for one CLI call, including with a smaller ceiling. It does not change acquisition, per-document, parser, output or transport limits.
Per-site output ceilings are separate. Sites render in key order and can use the remaining combined allowance. A failed site returns no partial tree. Insertion order in the request cannot decide which site gets a remaining allowance. These limits count bytes and entries, without measuring CPU time or exact allocator use.
Render several sites from Rust
Rust callers use build::acquire_publications and build::render_publications with explicit set limits and exactly matching option keys. PublicationSetRenderOptions combines those site recipes with the optional compiler-owned selection. The result retains the actual immutable per-site trees, not only its inspection report. Single-site rendering uses the same acquisition, metadata, compiler and output owners. Acquired site entries are explicit success/failure values. Successful views share one immutable packet; source failures do not produce a partially valid view. Later SDK staging still protects every selected source root, including failed captures. An unresolved root can therefore block staging without undoing a successful in-memory render; missing input is not permission to write there.
Distinguish shared and per-site failures
Gazette performs no output staging, database writes, listening, Git mutation or deployment in this command. Separately permitted native generators can have their own effects, as described above. Shared configuration, required content acquisition and complete content syntax/semantic errors still stop the whole operation before rendering. A failed presentation-only source instead fails each dependent site while unaffected sites continue. Without candidate selection, if all sites fail acquisition the report keeps their exact failures and shared captured-input evidence without parsing content, calling renderers or claiming valid semantics. With selection, shared syntax, semantics and candidate closure are still checked from the retained required content; failed presentation cannot bypass them. Unfiltered output remains draft-inclusive; candidates reject included drafts and retain published/archived distinctions. The result does not authorize publication or record release-set settlement.
Continue by task
                 
Inspect a local build
Inspect a local build. Inspect parsed content, review pages before templating, or scan the generated files.

Review pages before running the Theme.
     
Prepare inputs for the renderer
Prepare inputs for the renderer. Bind authored content, Markdown and static files so the renderer reads the files you intend it to use.
       
Prepare templates and browser resources
Prepare templates and browser resources. Choose the Theme templates, resources, capabilities and heading data that the renderer uses.
     
Read the generated site files
Read the generated site files. Find the graph, discovery files, Markdown copies and search records produced from the shared page model.

Find the discovery files.

Read the search records.

Authoring language server
Gazette meets each actor where it works, with the same publication model behind every mode: a person writing in an editor arrives through the language server, an agent helping in Claude Code or Codex through the MCP server and its skill, and a build or integration through the command line and SDKs.
Open the publication folder containing gazette.toml. In Claude Code, load the Gazette plugin; it names the local executable and supplies the native discovery settings. In VS Code, use the editor integration. Neither path requires a generated list of every article. The plugin's actual Claude language-server demonstration is still under qualification; the protocol below describes the implemented server contract.
Start gazette lsp to add Gazette diagnostics, navigation and completions to an editor. One process analyses one workspace, even when it contains one site. It uses framed Language Server Protocol over standard input and output, with analysis from the shared application and Rust SDK. The session tracks unsaved edits. It does not build or publish a site.
If you are…	Start here	
Writing in VS Code	Write with feedback	
Connecting Claude Code	Gazette agent plugin	
Building the VS Code extension	VS Code integration	
Implementing another client	Initialize the session, then send changes and track versions	
Adding a feature to an existing client	Diagnostics and symbols, current context or privacy and limits	
Explicit initialization
For configuration-driven selection, new-page discovery and repair of invalid native configuration, use editor source discovery. The fixed selections below remain supported; their shared version, query and transport contracts also apply to discovered sources.
Send initialize with ordinary LSP capabilities and one of two explicit initializationOptions shapes. The supplied-buffer form is:
{
  "workspace": {
    "uri": "untitled:workspace.toml",
    "path": "workspace.toml",
    "text": "principals=[{id='owner:one',kind='person'}]\nsites=[{id='site:one',publisher='owner:one',deployable=false}]\n"
  },
  "workspace_documents": null,
  "documents": [
    {
      "uri": "untitled:article.md",
      "path": "article.md",
      "text": "+++\n[content]\nid='content:one'\nsite='site:one'\ntitle='Example'\nlifecycle='draft'\n[content.structure]\nkind='page'\nfamily={kind='article'}\n+++\n# Example\n"
    }
  ]
}

Use workspace_documents: null for one supplied workspace buffer. For a modular workspace, put the root in workspace and its included TOML files in workspace_documents, using the same {uri,path,text} form for each. The array must match the root's non-recursive includes. Gazette does not discover extra files.
Give each document a role and a logical path. The URI identifies the document for the protocol. Gazette never opens it or infers a role from the URI, suffix or editor language. Duplicate paths or URIs, invalid logical paths, unknown fields and input above the limits reject initialization. Single-buffer and modular initialization are separate choices. A failure does not switch modes.
Supply only the configured text you want to analyse. This session does not capture all of a publication's assets. Plain project Markdown needs its configured workspace binding for semantic checks. Having a heading does not make a file part of the publication.
Check the server capabilities during initialization. The server advertises full-text synchronization, UTF-16 positions, document symbols, workspace-symbol search, identity hover, typed replacement of workspace references, reviewable diagnostic fixes and experimental.gazette.authoring = "0.1.0". It supplies links and navigation for within-workspace TOML, configured Markdown documents, headings and footnotes. The VS Code client checks these capabilities. Each folder session is separate, so an editor cannot assume documents in another process can be queried.
Let the server read named files
To have the server read the files, specify the workspace root and every input role. For a single directory, set rootUri or use one workspaceFolders entry. Send:
{
  "native_selection": {
    "allow_read": true,
    "workspace": "workspace.toml",
    "documents": ["content/article.md"],
    "manuals": [{"source": "source:manual", "path": "docs/index.md"}],
    "page_inputs": ["content/article/diagram.svg"],
    "package_baselines": [
      {"kind": "theme", "package": "theme:base", "path": "themes/base/theme.toml"}
    ]
  }
}

Set allow_read: true before asking the server to open files. If you use both root fields, they must identify the same absolute file: directory. This form supports at most one workspace folder. Gazette loads the root document, its non-recursive includes and the named regular files. It never scans a directory, follows symlinks, guesses roles from suffixes or reads from the current directory. A failed read does not switch to supplied buffers.
For explicitly distributed editor sources, use a rooted selection instead:
{
  "native_selection": {
    "allow_read": true,
    "roots": [
      {"id": "workspace", "uri": "file:///work/publication"},
      {"id": "content", "uri": "file:///work/owner-content"}
    ],
    "workspace": {"root": "workspace", "entry": "gazette.toml", "path": "gazette.toml"},
    "workspace_documents": [
      {"root": "workspace", "entry": "config/sites.toml", "path": "config/sites.toml"}
    ],
    "documents": [
      {"root": "content", "entry": "blog/example/index.md", "path": "authored/owner/blog/example/index.md"}
    ],
    "manuals": [],
    "page_inputs": [],
    "package_baselines": []
  }
}

Each root must identify an opened workspaceFolders entry. If present, rootUri must name the configuration root. Put configuration modules under that root, using their relative entries as logical paths. This editor form opens the named configuration files even if they contain errors so the editor can show them. The compiler then checks the required include list. The single-directory form reads that list through the strict loader.
Other locators give both an entry to read and a logical compiler path. Neither creates a public address or editorial relationship. Gazette refuses duplicate physical files across roles, unknown roots and conflicting ownership of nested folders. Give each manual its configured source key and each package manifest its typed package identity.
Both forms use one combined source/entry budget across roots. Configuration and package manifests use the TOML size ceiling; authored text uses the content ceiling. Opaque page inputs keep their bytes without becoming text buffers. Initialization sends locators within the same frame limit. Reads across roots are not an atomic snapshot.
The SDK builds the session from the files it read. The physical entry and its root determine the file URI. When an editor closes a buffer, the server returns to the original baseline or the latest acknowledged save. It does not read the file again. Permission to read these files does not allow a build or publication.
Check Theme templates through the CLI or MCP
Gazette 0.1 uses Theme manifests for component completion and hover. It does not serve the Tera templates named by those manifests as LSP documents. Use the CLI or MCP template compiler to check the complete Theme and its virtual template namespace. LSP does not scan template directories or infer roles from filenames, suffixes or language IDs.
Current editor context and transport handoff
gazette/authoringContext accepts {generation, textDocument: {uri}, position} with a standard UTF-16 position. It returns current compiler-owned fields and schema facts, native diagnostics, cursor assistance, identity/composition and page-package context. Source digest and open version bind the result. Optional semantic views explicitly distinguish available, inapplicable and unavailable current evidence. The tolerant field outline never replaces strict compilation. Schema errors in a configuration document retain that document's own path and range throughout the compiler, SDK and LSP; they cannot acquire a sibling's span. Semantic failure still refuses compilation. Unambiguous typed source facts remain available for repair: a uniquely occurring unresolved reference keeps its exact owner and can receive reviewed replacement proposals across modules. Repeated or ambiguous occurrences do not acquire an invented source location.
gazette/editorSnapshot returns a complete manifest of the current retained selection: generation, roles, logical paths, current and saved-baseline digests, byte counts and open versions. baseline_sha256 identifies saved text; a non-null version alone does not mean the text is unsaved. gazette/editorSource accepts {generation, document, offset, length} and returns at most 65,536 bytes as base64 with the same generation, document and offset. Offsets are byte coordinates and may divide a UTF-8 character; decode text only after reassembly and complete digest verification. A generation change rejects subsequent chunks. Opaque companions preserve their byte role.
These requests perform no native read or write. For native workspace discovery, the snapshot also includes native_selection: the workspace directory, configuration path, explicit manual selections and hashes of the saved configuration and machine binding. The editorSnapshot.nativeContextFormat capability advertises gazette-editor-context/2. A client transfers text only for sources whose current and baseline digests differ, retaining the complete manifest, clean open versions and opaque file observations. Export and MCP inspection use the same SDK reconstruction owner. The receiving caller must separately permit native reads; the exported selection grants no permission. Reconstruction checks saved baselines, replays unsaved configuration before content, and refuses changed membership, roles, hashes or observations. File-size observations do not establish asset contents, and reads across files are not atomic.
Explicit supplied-buffer selections retain the self-contained gazette-editor-context/1 format, including captured opaque inputs. A client can also reproduce those supplied inputs through authoring_start and replay open versions through authoring_open_document. Native discovery refuses an older server without the compact descriptor instead of copying the entire saved corpus. LSP and MCP remain separate sessions over one SDK analysis owner. A manifest is not a build, publication or permission receipt.
Baselines, overlays and generations
The SDK session holds the source baseline, full-text edits, versions and generation. LSP checks URIs and request shapes and converts locations to UTF-16. MCP uses the same SDK with UTF-8 byte offsets. Its handle limit and expiry apply to MCP sessions only.
Editor event	What Gazette does	
initialized	Analyse the captured baseline and publish diagnostics.	
didOpen	Start an overlay for a URI in the configured session.	
didChange	Accept one complete replacement with a strictly increasing integer version. Consecutive changes for the same URI may be combined before analysis.	
didSave	Compare the supplied saved text with the open overlay. If it matches, make it the baseline and advance the generation when the baseline changed. It reads no file.	
Close	Remove the overlay and analyse the original or acknowledged saved baseline. To see external file changes, restart with a fresh read.	
The server logs and ignores duplicate opens, unopened or out-of-session changes, malformed notifications and incremental edits. A full replacement above the session's byte limit is also ignored. None advances the version or generation or stops the server from handling another valid request.
An accepted edit reruns analysis across the whole configured session. For example, an open included TOML file supplies its current declarations, and editing a collection can produce a diagnostic on an unchanged article. The diagnostic uses the article's version and digest with the new generation. An invalid current parse replaces the earlier successful result for diagnostics, navigation and validation. Completion can separately use the preceding workspace parse as described below.
The reader can accept frames while one worker runs SDK analysis. The worker keeps the latest pending change. Requests and open/close events preserve their order relative to changes. If a newer contiguous edit is already queued, Gazette discards the older result. A computation already under way can finish, but it cannot publish an obsolete or partial result.
Scheduler setting	Limit	
Input channel and backlog	64 messages each	
Change notifications in one analysis batch	64	
First batching delay	4 ms	
Later batching delay	A quarter of the most recent analysis duration, between 2 and 40 ms	
Batching controls how long the worker waits for changes before starting. It does not bound the total editor response time. The scheduler test queues 64 changes and checks that diagnostics reach the latest version without one update per keystroke. It does not use a machine-specific timing threshold.
Diagnostics and symbols
Native errors remain application-owned. The SDK's borrowed projection retains codes, logical fields/endpoints, all matching declaration origins and exact path/digest binding. The LSP adds only editor ranges, versions and generation. The same retained Markdown analysis reports source-only renderability failures for raw HTML before Theme rendering. Nested footnotes and references inside image labels use the same emitted-footnote closure as rendering. Backlink counts describe emitted references rather than unused source occurrences. This diagnostic preview neither selects a Theme/component renderer nor changes publication admission or build validity.
Checked UTF-8 spans become UTF-16 ranges, including CRLF and non-BMP characters.
data.location preserves the native full-file span and its precision. A construct range is not an exact token or permission to edit it.
Missing locations use a required LSP document range while retaining a null source location. Logical fields are not converted to guessed field spans.
Selection-wide failures are explicitly marked; repeating one on selected documents does not blame those files individually.
Complete-result exhaustion fails explicitly rather than dropping findings.
A final gazette/analysisPublished notification carries generation and structural validity after that generation's diagnostic notifications. Sequential stream delivery is not atomic client application of the set. An interrupted stream must not be treated as a completed generation.
textDocument/documentSymbol uses shared workspace_symbols for the selected workspace and heading_symbols for Markdown. Workspace declarations are flat Object symbols named by their native identity, with the original TOML scalar construct as both range and selectionRange. Markdown headings retain the shared allocator's body coordinates checked against exact full source. Neither role invents whole-section ranges or rename tokens. Invalid current syntax or ambiguous declarations refuse workspace symbols; an unrelated corpus syntax failure does not erase a valid workspace index. Corpus failure cannot return previous headings. Structural help does not imply a valid publication.
Find a symbol in the workspace
workspace/symbol uses the SDK's single selected-source symbol search. Its required query is a string; empty selects all symbols. Matching uses Unicode lowercase substring comparison, not identity normalization, fuzzy ranking or linguistic case folding. Results are complete current workspace declarations and Markdown headings, ordered by logical path and native construct. There is no disk search.
The server advertises workspaceSymbolProvider: true and returns standard SymbolInformation: Object declarations and Namespace headings with each actual selected URI and checked UTF-16 range. Native generation, source digest, path and overlay version are checked before projection. The ranges describe constructs, not rename tokens. A changed overlay changes the result; close restores the exact selected baseline. Invalid current selected syntax or exhausted result bounds refuses the whole search instead of returning stale or partial matches. Lazy resolution and partial-work delivery are not advertised. Use the VS Code source setup to exercise symbol search in the editor.
Workspace declaration and reference navigation
The existing definition/reference methods also consume the compiler's retained workspace association index. The selected workspace's exact UTF-8 source identity is checked before LSP converts its native construct ranges to UTF-16. Only typed workspace references recognized by that compiler owner participate; equal strings in names, comments or other unrelated fields are not references.
In supplied-buffer mode, declarations and references belong to that one workspace buffer. In modular mode, navigation spans the root and its exact admitted set of included TOML documents: a reference in an include can lead to a declaration in the root or another selected include. The compiler identifies each definition and reference's actual document, source digest and span; LSP maps that document to its selected URI and converts positions in the matching buffer. It does not discover unselected modules, read native files during navigation or guess targets from equal strings. Markdown-link, footnote and field-origin queries retain their separate scopes described below.
Invalid current workspace syntax or semantics refuses navigation instead of reusing an earlier index. Valid workspace navigation remains available during an independently invalid selected Markdown corpus. Accepted overlays and close use the same shared Session lifecycle as Markdown navigation.
Current workspace field origins
The discoverable custom request gazette/origin accepts {generation, query}. Use the generation from gazette/analysisPublished; stale generations are refused. query is either {kind:"field", query:<FieldQuery>} or {kind:"composition", query:<CompositionOriginQuery>}, reusing the native compiler query contracts. Native key/index paths remain string/integer arrays.
The response is {native, range}. native binds the selected document, logical path, generation and nullable overlay version to the compiler's exact source digest, UTF-8 byte span and (for composition) winning declaration layer. range only projects that span to checked LSP UTF-16 positions in the same current buffer. No field-location or inheritance resolver exists in the server. The capability is advertised at experimental.gazette.origin.
Origin queries reparse the bounded current workspace using the existing native parser/resolver. They perform no source I/O or publication effects and never substitute a previous successful result. Invalid current workspace, missing identity, absent explicit field, stale generation and query/ result exhaustion are distinct refusals. Unrelated Markdown failure does not hide a valid workspace origin. Closing an overlay restores only its retained baseline. authoring_origin supplies the same native result through MCP.
When changing origin queries, run the SDK origin tests and the protocol suites:
cargo test --locked -p gazette-sdk --test authoring_origins
cargo test --locked -p gazette-lsp --test protocol origin
cargo test --locked -p gazette-mcp --lib authoring::origin

Workspace identity hover
textDocument/hover uses the same current native association as definition and reference navigation. A declaration or recognized reference returns Resolved <native kind>: <identity> with its original occurrence range. The server chooses the first supported format in the client's textDocument.hover.contentFormat preference list. An absent or empty list uses plaintext; Markdown is used only when offered. Opaque identities, paths and values remain literal in either format, and Markdown escaping counts toward the complete response limit. The application's workspace_identity result retains source identity, occurrence precision and the original declaration symbol; LSP only presents these facts. A field can also show its description, whether it is required, the values it accepts and any named choices from the shared schema. Unrecognized text returns no hover. Help describes the current configuration; it does not establish a valid publication.
Page-package authoring remains compiler-owned. Within an authored page's resources[].inputs[] and resources[].build.entry values, completion proposes only paths retained by that page's resolved resource declarations and includes their proven output routes in completion data. Standard definition navigation follows an exact declared input or entry to its explicitly selected retained companion URI; the zero position means the opaque companion has no fabricated editable source span. The generation-bound gazette/pagePackage request accepts { "generation", "document" }, where document is a selected document or opaque page-input URI, and returns the retained owner/source/companion URIs plus compiler-validated resource programs. Unhandled companions never receive an invented compiled destination.
Resolved documentation builds are target-preflighted without acquisition or effects. Workspace diagnostics retain ordered manual navigation, configured routes, exact source identities/selections, and generated references as distinct items. documentation_validation_incomplete is informational and means final route/anchor closure belongs to target assembly but the editor session lacks the complete retained manual/reference trees. Documentation field provenance remains available through gazette/origin using the native brand field path; the LSP does not parse Mintlify configuration or implement a second anchor validator.
For a site declaration or typed site reference, the same native identity result also borrows the compiler's effective composition. Hover appends a bounded JSON view, fenced as code only for Markdown clients, showing its Theme, palette and capability selections, including each winning workspace/site layer. Disabled capabilities stay visible; a site Theme replacement does not acquire the default Theme's omitted palette. Neither LSP nor MCP recomputes inheritance or maintains another configuration catalog. These are desired selections, not verified provider availability or build readiness. Origins remain logical declarations, not invented edit ranges.
Label length is checked before formatting, and the complete result is bounded before delivery. Invalid current workspace analysis refuses the query, never substituting an older identity. Accepted edits and close follow the same selected Session lifecycle; unrelated invalid Markdown does not remove valid workspace help. MCP exposes this exact native fact through authoring_hover, including precision that standard LSP ranges cannot express and the same site composition object.
Typed reference replacement and repair
textDocument/completion projects the shared native reference queries. For workspace references, complete_reference includes unresolved keys. The compiler verifies the native TOML string scalar and its decoded identity; the field's declared namespace and current unambiguous declarations supply the complete candidate set in source order. Each candidate reuses its declaration's original valid quoted literal, including escapes, rather than introducing another TOML encoder. Names, declarations, arbitrary strings and comments return null.
The edit replaces the entire scalar, not its decoded interior. Each item retains the exact preimage, source digest, path, editor version and session generation in data; LSP alone converts native byte ranges to UTF-16. The shared response and complete protocol result have independent byte bounds; exhaustion returns no partial list. Invalid syntax and ambiguous declarations offer no repair subset. Unresolved references retain current diagnostics while permitting proposals from the same typed parse. These current-source queries never substitute an older model or admit a partial workspace; the separate interrupted-reference fallback below does not change their contract. The shared result carries the field's namespace and a nullable current target. These are typed proposals, not proof that replacement satisfies every cross-field constraint. Applying clients must keep the current preimage/version and validate the changed workspace. Gazette performs no source writes. The VS Code bridge rejects in-flight results after buffer, version, ownership or session changes. MCP exposes the same result through authoring_complete_reference with its exact generation guard. Standard LSP completion requires a single-line replacement range, so multiline reference scalars are explicitly refused by LSP while their native exact-span proposals remain available through SDK/MCP. Replacement text requests asIs insertion rather than automatic reindentation. Schema-derived missing-key and closed-literal completion is separately available for workspace TOML and explicit authored TOML frontmatter. The compiler recovers current syntax against the actual Rust/Serde declaration schema; LSP owns only UTF-16 projection and exact edits. Plain Markdown, body positions and open-ended string vocabularies do not acquire invented candidates. General free-text prefix completion remains unsupported. Structured *.landing.yaml sources participate in selected-set parsing and resolved cross-document references. Original component and direct arguments scalars can show the winning Theme template and argument schema. Exact tokens can receive component names, unused schema keys and closed literal proposals. Normalized Markdown body text has no exact inline edit coordinates. Escaped and folded YAML may expose a containing construct for inspection without an edit.
Authored reference help also covers editorial collection, journey and member scalars, authored site and attribution-principal scalars, and non-containing related-content references. Editorial candidates respect the field's target kind and the declaring site's identity. Current declaration literals and source locations supply replacements; the graph still validates residence and cycles after an edit. Related-content candidates include resolved site-specific legal outputs, not their owner-held source identity. If that derived namespace cannot be established, completion refuses rather than presenting an incomplete set.
AST-recognized [[site:...|label]] links have destination-only completion, including incomplete or unresolved selectors. Candidates come from selected publication pages and their proved headings and article-owned notes anchors. Code, image labels and unrelated same-word text acquire no symbolic edit. Exact source preimages, candidate definition evidence and complete-result bounds remain shared with SDK/MCP; LSP only converts the range to UTF-16.
Selected notes.md belongs in editable documents, not opaque page_inputs. It retains its article's identity and requires no independent page frontmatter. Exactly selected legal-source bindings receive the reduced native legal schema, reported as legal_source_frontmatter, rather than invented site or page fields. Sound scalar assistance can survive incomplete neighboring TOML; this does not make the document valid for publication. Symbolic candidates are publication targets, not evidence of Mintlify manual-link compatibility.
Completing an interrupted workspace reference
While a workspace reference is being edited, completion can use its last parsed scalar if the current parser cannot supply candidates. For example, deleting the closing quote in publisher='owner:one' still lets the editor suggest the declared principals. The SDK keeps at most one previous workspace analysis and the edited source, within the existing retained-source byte limit. Current diagnostics continue to show the syntax error.
This fallback requires every byte outside that known scalar to remain unchanged. A declaration or field change makes the fallback unavailable. Editing another document, saving, closing, changed native membership or unavailable native sources discards the retained parse. Native discovery can retain it only when the selected roles and current inputs are identical. The edit range, source digest, preimage and editor version describe the current buffer; candidate definition positions from the earlier parse are omitted. Results identify their prior source and generation and set isIncomplete so the editor asks again as typing continues. Multiline LSP replacements and exhausted response bounds still fail. Quick fixes, hover, navigation, validation and stateless MCP queries never use this fallback.
Reviewable diagnostic repairs
textDocument/codeAction advertises only quickfix. It offers the same exact source-bound replacement proposals as completion when the requested range has a byte-for-byte current Gazette diagnostic. The server recomputes that diagnostic from the selected session; stale, altered, non-Gazette or unassisted diagnostics produce no action. Each returned edit names the current editor version when one is open and retains the session generation, source digest and preimage in its proposal data.
Actions are deliberately titled as review proposals, are never preferred and contain no command. Gazette does not apply them, save files, run a formatter or claim the replacement satisfies every cross-field constraint. The client shows the versioned edit for review; accepted text must return through ordinary didChange analysis before diagnostics can clear. There is no fix-all action and no second TOML or Markdown parser in the language server.
Heading and footnote source navigation
Heading links use the same allocated anchor index and strict fragment decoder as publication compilation. A recognized navigational link with no path, such as #section or ?view=local#section, resolves to its emitted heading. Querying that heading returns the complete recognized local reference set. Duplicate automatic slugs and explicit IDs therefore agree with the rendered page; the editor does not slugify text or reverse-map generated HTML.
Images, external links and root-relative links do not become heading associations. Relative document paths use the selected-document association described below, not a same-document fallback. Valid footnote or continuation DOM anchors do not masquerade as heading declarations. Native source occurrences omitted from rendered output remain source-navigation evidence. A malformed or missing local fragment refuses the document's heading-reference result rather than returning a partial list. Structural heading symbols remain independently available; this query is not full publication-link validation.
The shared source_navigation operation compares heading/link and footnote occurrences by their native containing ranges. A footnote reference in a heading selects the note; a fragment link inside a footnote selects the heading. Equal ranges with different targets fail as ambiguous. An independently valid footnote association remains available when heading-link evidence cannot be produced.
textDocument/definition and textDocument/references resolve recognized Markdown footnote occurrences through the shared authoring SDK. The compiler exposes the existing native definition/reference facts; the application retains their bounded document-local associations. Neither the LSP nor VS Code parses labels, invents case-folding rules, reverse-maps HTML IDs or joins equal labels across files. This includes source occurrences omitted from rendered output.
Queries require the exact current selected source and checked UTF-16 positions. The application binds its answer to the logical path and whole-source digest, and lifts body coordinates through the original frontmatter boundary. If a reference occurs within a definition, the smallest containing native occurrence wins. More than one matching native definition fails as ambiguous; undefined footnote-like ordinary text does not acquire an invented target. Unused native definitions remain queryable even when they have no references.
Definition returns one standard location or null; references returns the complete logical-path/source-ordered set and honors includeDeclaration. These are native construct ranges, not exact label-edit or rename ranges. The SDK preserves precision; standard LSP locations carry the range only. They authorize no source changes.
Accepted overlays rerun these same facts. Failed current corpus syntax refuses Markdown navigation rather than returning an earlier map; workspace or content-policy errors may still permit explicitly structural source help. Invalid positions, surrogate interiors, unselected URIs and malformed request shapes are rejected. The source projection is bounded across the whole selection before copying; URI amplification and complete response encoding are separately bounded by the server. No partial reference list is returned on exhaustion.
Follow links between configured documents
Explicit relative Markdown links resolve only to exact logical paths in the selected source set. The compiler shares publication path decoding and anchor allocation: encoded filenames/fragments and confined ./.. segments work, without extension guesses, directory-index lookup, disk reads or URI inference. A fragment selects its existing heading; a fragmentless link selects the target's whole Markdown body, excluding frontmatter. Valid nonheading DOM anchors do not invent heading definitions. Images, external/root-relative links and unselected targets do not create associations.
Each definition and reference retains its own selected path, complete source digest and native location. Reverse references include the complete selected incoming set plus local heading links. Footnotes remain document-local. Invalid selected target fragments or malformed/escaping relative paths refuse complete cross-document evidence instead of returning a partial or older target; an independently valid footnote can still resolve. Target overlays immediately rebind unchanged incoming links, and close restores the captured baseline.
The Rust SDK navigation tests cover selected-document source/anchor joins, exclusions, overlays, stale-source refusal, failed targets and complete-result bounds. After changing client presentation, test source navigation in VS Code.
Open a source link
Resolved publication and document references also project through standard textDocument/documentLink. The compiler's existing source associations own the link range, target source and heading coordinates. The LSP maps that exact selected target to its client URI; it does not interpret a site URL as a filesystem path. Link data retains the current generation and both source identities. Failed current resolution refuses the result rather than returning a successful stale subset. Normal page ownership belongs to gazette/authoringContext and gazette/pagePackage, not the Problems list. Unhandled companions still produce their actionable warning.
Inline heading-link completion
Standard completion also projects Analysis::complete_heading for a selected Markdown document. The candidates are the exact emitted headings and URL-ready fragments used by publication rendering, including duplicate-heading suffixes and explicit IDs. They are not an editor-maintained slug catalog. An unresolved fragment can be repaired from current heading facts without borrowing an older successful link-resolution result.
The initial edit profile is a provider-recognized emitted inline link whose literal suffix is ](#fragment), including an empty #. The decoded destination must match those exact source bytes. Only that destination is replaced; labels, framing, line endings and other content are preserved. Images, external links, reference-style links, titles and escaped/entity destination spellings receive no inferred edit. This is not incomplete-Markdown parsing or cross-document completion. Native containing ranges alone never justify token replacement.
The proposal binds the complete current source digest and exact preimage. LSP adds the session generation, overlay version and checked UTF-16 edit range; MCP exposes the same native proposal through authoring_complete_heading. Complete native and transport bounds refuse instead of truncating the candidate set. The existing VS Code completion guard protects current source/version and retired sessions. Selecting a suggestion edits an editor buffer only; ordinary native reanalysis follows, without file writes or publication permission.
Theme component authoring
Standard completion and hover also project the shared SDK's selected-Theme component facts. Supplied initialization selects typed theme or plugin package identity alongside its unique file identity, logical path and exact manifest text. The workspace remains the sole owner of its source/manifest binding; native selection supplies exact permitted locators instead of text. Gazette never infers a Theme from presentation.toml, scans a folder or opens a configured repository path. Two source bindings may therefore use the same manifest filename without losing their distinct identity.
The application joins an authored document to its configured content source, site, effective composition, Theme source and Theme identity once. The compiler's retained directive header lexer and Components validator remain the sole name/argument owners. Completion replaces either the exact component-name slot with the complete selected-Theme catalog, or an exact property-name/closed-literal slot inside that component's TOML argument table with candidates from its native Draft 2020-12 schema. The LSP projects checked UTF-8 spans to UTF-16 edits, including non-BMP text before the slot. Hover shows the exact component name and selected template, with its argument contract as JSON, fenced as code only for Markdown clients. For structured YAML landings, hover also explains that child sections may use components from the effective Theme or ordinary groups with a heading, nonempty body or child section. Completion on an exact child component name shows the selected catalog. Markdown normalized from YAML body scalars does not supply editable ranges. Manifest or document overlays advance the same authoring generation, so changed or closed buffers cannot reuse older component facts.
MCP exposes the same UTF-8 source-bound result through authoring_component_assistance; LSP alone converts its exact byte span to UTF-16. The VS Code extension selects only explicitly configured native files and forwards these standard completion/hover results unchanged. It contains no component parser, argument-schema interpreter or catalog.
No general free-text prefix completion, formatting, fix-all action, workspace-folder mutation or notebook synchronization is advertised. The bounded quick-fix action above is the only code-action profile. Unsupported requests receive method-not-found; unknown extension notifications have no effect. Shutdown followed by exit is required for clean termination.
Bounds and privacy
Defaults: 8 KiB headers; 1 MiB incoming JSON; 2 MiB outgoing JSON and complete diagnostic set; 256 total diagnostics. Selected-source defaults come from the SDK session: 4,096 documents including the workspace, 1 MiB total URI identity bytes and 16 MiB retained baseline-plus-overlay bytes plus the optional prior completion source, matching the default complete corpus budget and including opaque authoring inputs. Identifier, logical-path and text bounds precede selection retention; a refused edit cannot partially mutate a session. Shared workspace parsing defaults remain 64 KiB source, 10,000 nodes and depth 64; content and heading limits come from authoring::Limits. Source navigation defaults to 16,384 retained workspace declaration/reference occurrences, footnote occurrences, heading links, exact inline completion-slot records and selected-document references, and 4 MiB of native association keys/strings across the complete selected set. Query results use only these bounded retained facts.
Framing checks length before body allocation. The duplicate-safe SDK JSON decoder precedes native protocol types. Projection budgets precede retained diagnostic rows; the complete encoded set and each outgoing frame are separately bounded. Native stream failure may interrupt a write and is never clean success. These are bounded operations under the shared execution model, not a process sandbox.
Source text, URIs, identities and diagnostics may be private. They travel only over the selected editor process connection. No telemetry or provider access is performed.
To check protocol changes, run the LSP protocol suite, CLI integration suite and shared-session suite:
cargo test --locked -p gazette-lsp --test protocol
cargo test --locked -p gazette-launcher --test lsp_cli
cargo test --locked -p gazette-sdk --test authoring_session

These cover framing, process startup, editor overlays and failed analysis. Continue with VS Code setup to inspect the result in an editor.
Current editor contract
The sections above define the versioned selected-source contract. The LSP and VS Code client project the shared compiler/SDK facts; they do not implement a second publication model. A current failure cannot borrow an older successful analysis, and an edit proposal still requires an exact current source preimage.
Rename, formatting, fix-all, automatic file writes, notebook synchronization and native build/release effects are outside this protocol. Synchronous SDK analysis already running cannot be interrupted. Generated-source ranges are exact only where the SDK retains an exact origin. For the client implementation and separate editor-host checks, continue with VS Code integration and the client checks.

Markdown
Gazette uses Comrak 0.54.0 to parse publication Markdown and developer manuals. Gazette then resolves the headings, links, components and resources that depend on its publication model.
Source profile	What it parses	
publication (default)	Tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes, heading attributes and GitHub alerts	
publication-math	Everything above, plus inline and displayed mathematics	
Set markdown_profile = "publication-math" on the content binding to parse equations. An attached notebook uses its own source's profile. The editor uses the workspace profile for a bound file and ordinary Markdown for an unbound file. To turn equations into rendered output, follow Typeset mathematics or pass generator options to the renderer.
Headings
Add a heading ID or class using the Markdown adapter's attribute syntax. Quote IDs containing Unicode or punctuation outside the bare form, such as # Heading {#"café" .wide}. The DOM ID is café, and the link fragment is #caf%C3%A9. Malformed attributes remain heading text. Recognized attributes other than IDs and classes fail. Gazette supports one attribute grammar.
Code blocks
Name a language on a fenced code block to highlight its syntax:
```rust
let message = "Hello, reader";
```

Website HTML uses Syntect 5.3.0 with the two-face 0.5.2+bat-0.26.1 syntax bundle, including TypeScript and TOML. The pure-Rust regex profile supplies the supported definitions; excluded or unrecognized syntaxes use plain text. Recognized language names and extensions produce nested span elements with syntax- classes; for example, keyword.control becomes class="syntax-keyword syntax-control". The existing pre and code elements retain their attributes, including language-rust. Themes supply colours and code-panel presentation; the engine emits no inline styles.
