Page packages and page-local resources
Give a publication page its own stylesheet, browser module, font or image. Gazette compiles the declared files and passes their URLs to the Theme in presentation.resources. The template still needs to include the stylesheet or script.
This applies to pages rendered by a Theme, including product help. Use the Mintlify documentation target for the repository’s developer manuals and API reference.
Declare a page resource
Framed authored pages and framed project-native documentation can declare resources from their existing content source. The following declarations assume those files exist in that selected source. They are frontmatter fragments, alongside the page's complete [content] declaration.
Put resource tables at the frontmatter root, alongside [content]:
[[resources]]
inputs = ["main.scss", "_tokens.scss"]
build = { kind = "stylesheet", entry = "main.scss" }
output = "/assets/article.css"

[[resources]]
inputs = ["main.ts", "dep.ts"]
build = { kind = "browser-module", entry = "main.ts" }
output = "/assets/article.js"

[[resources]]
inputs = ["type/article.woff2"]
build = { kind = "woff2-font", entry = "type/article.woff2" }
output = "/assets/type/article.woff2"

[content]
# The page's existing required structural fields follow here.

Build the site to produce /assets/article.css, /assets/article.js and /assets/type/article.woff2. Each declaration owns its own output path. The publication build uses the same adapters as site-level resources. See browser resources for supported inputs. TypeScript erasure removes types without checking them.
Consume the resolved resources in a Theme
The owning page and its aliases receive presentation.resources, an ordered list of kind, url, output, sha256 and bytes. Use url in markup; Gazette has already applied the publication's public or local-preview base. output is the site-relative output path. Other pages receive their own list, empty when they have no page resources.
{% for resource in presentation.resources %}
  {% if resource.kind == "stylesheet" %}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ resource.url }}">
  {% elif resource.kind == "browser-module" %}
  <script type="module" src="{{ resource.url }}"></script>
  {% endif %}
{% endfor %}

The Theme places this loop where its document structure needs the resources. Theme and page JSON receive the same resolved values. Page resources remain separate from the complete top-level resources map, presentation.theme_resources and presentation.capabilities provider outcomes. presentation.theme_resources contains required Theme resources in requirement order, followed by resources explicitly selected with use = "site". Dependency-only resources are not executable roots.
Keep page companions with their owner
A framed guide/index.md or guide/index.markdown owns the retained companions beneath guide/. A standalone guide.md does not claim a sibling directory. Gazette classifies companions as notebooks, programs, stylesheets, WOFF2 font candidates, supported static assets or unhandled inputs.
An article may also own one unframed sibling notes.md, including when its bundle is the selected source root. Notes share the article's identity and have no independent route or search record. Other Markdown beneath a leaf package is refused. See article notes for rendering and anchor behavior.
Authoring interfaces can select notes as editable documents. Other companions can be supplied as opaque page inputs, which do not accept text overlays. The compiler resolves ownership once; SDK, LSP, MCP and VS Code show that result. Unhandled companions appear in authoring diagnostics and prevent a successful publication build when they remain unconsumed.
Compiled companions require an explicit page route. Without a resource declaration, a leaf package admits one top-level non-test JavaScript/TypeScript program entry and one top-level non-partial CSS/Sass/SCSS stylesheet entry. More than one candidate of either kind requires explicit declarations. Nested files, TypeScript declarations, tests and Sass partials remain inputs, not standalone public outputs. Notebooks and static files retain their own format and asset rules.
Bind inputs and dependencies
Name inputs relative to the captured source. Do not use the page's address, corpus prefix or public URL. The entry must be in the unique input set. Imports stay within that set and the supported resource profile. Gazette preserves resource order and treats input lists as sets. Output name, kind, execution order and owner come from declarations, not filenames.
Use build.imports to map a browser module's import aliases to workspace libraries. Gazette emits each library once at its configured URL. The page's other files still come from its own source. The alias does not read another source or activate a capability.
The Theme and site model receive the same module graph. A Theme can serialize its import map and render each page's supplied modulepreload dependencies. Neither adds a script that runs the module. Gazette does not invent priorities, timestamps or a separate preload manifest. Plain Markdown without frontmatter cannot declare page resources.
Validate the complete output
Stylesheets may carry references, mapping each actual decoded CSS URL to its checked site-output path. References resolve from the emitted stylesheet, not its source file or owning page. They may target selected static assets or compiled resources. Missing or out-of-site targets fail before staging; no dependency is fetched or selected implicitly.
Page resources share the site's inventory with pages, aliases, static assets, site resources and machine outputs. Conflicting claims fail even when their bytes match. Missing inputs, invalid recipes and undeclared imports reject the site. Use the retained publication build path: rendering a bare Theme page cannot silently omit its declared resources.
Only actual compiler dependencies consume the corresponding opaque inputs. Listing an unused notebook or arbitrary file in inputs does not make it compiled; other unhandled companions still fail the build. Resource declarations and their encoded text consume the authored graph bounds. Site and page resources also share metadata and emitted-byte limits before the complete site inventory check. These bound records and bytes, not adapter CPU or all intermediate allocations.
Private page_resources evidence records each page's source, recipe, dependencies, compiler and output identities. Native source coordinates do not enter the public resource list. Later rebuilds use their captured bytes rather than reopening a source during rendering. Local rendering remains draft-inclusive and separate from disclosure review or release.
WOFF2 fonts
The 0.1 font profile admits WOFF2 only. A font recipe must select exactly one retained file and performs complete WOFF2 decompression plus required head, maxp and name table parsing through the pinned decoder/parser pair. TrueType- and CFF-flavored single fonts are admitted; collections and unknown flavors are refused. Output preserves the exact retained WOFF2 bytes, while private evidence binds both encoded and reconstructed SFNT identities. No system font lookup, live filesystem read, network provider, automatic suffix admission or font subsetting occurs.
@font-face is a closed stylesheet profile rather than a general opaque-at-rule escape. It requires exactly one family and one source descriptor. A URL-backed face requires one URL with explicit format(woff2). A local fallback face may instead list 1–16 literal local() font names, each nonempty and control-free after decoding, with both its decoded name and the CSS parser’s serialized name (including any quotes or escapes) bounded to 256 UTF-8 bytes. Local names remain browser font lookups: they add no retained URL, font-byte evidence or installation claim. Generic family keywords, mixed local/URL lists, multiple URL candidates, technology hints, unknown descriptors and duplicates are refused. Optional style, weight, stretch and Unicode-range descriptors may appear once. The profile also admits one font-display value from auto, block, swap, fallback or optional; one finite nonnegative percentage for size-adjust; and either normal or one finite nonnegative percentage for each of ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override. No expression, unit substitution or duplicate spelling is accepted. The URL is resolved relative to the emitted stylesheet and must identify the emitted font resource; queries, fragments, cross-site, escaping and missing targets remain invalid under the existing complete output-reference closure. Preview serves the producer-declared resource as font/woff2; a filename alone never grants that declaration.
Supply a Theme file from a shared source
A workspace may supply a Theme resource's already declared logical input from another configured source through design_inputs and theme_packages.resource_inputs. The workspace example defines the exact alias, source and entry mapping. The Theme manifest still owns the resource recipe and complete input list; workspace composition independently selects its output and use. Merely declaring an alias emits nothing and grants no native read permission.
Package-local and mounted inputs share one virtual resource-input tree. For example, a Theme-local Sass entry can import a declared mounted token partial at its logical path without copying the token source into the Theme repository. Existing resource adapters consume retained bytes from that tree, with the same input, dependency, compiler and output checks as local inputs. Their public resource records and serving URLs remain unchanged.
The selected Theme/dependency closure brings its mounted source keys into the normal bounded acquisition, once per exact source key. Missing or nonregular inputs, undeclared targets and package-local/mounted ambiguity refuse metadata; no fallback file search or successful partial resource is returned. Compilation and retained replay never reopen those native sources. The private resource evidence preserves each logical input's original alias, source key, entry and exact retained identities rather than treating the virtual path as native provenance.
Shared inputs apply to Theme resource recipes, not page companions, template mounts or Mintlify inputs. Page-local resources continue to use their owning content source.
For a mounted dot-image recipe, the existing explicit diagram-acquisition path resolves the single declared input to its original retained source and entry. It requires the same pinned dot_renderer executable and execution permission as local DOT, validates the generated PNG and retains its exact input/output binding. Resource rendering checks those retained bytes, then expresses input identity and dependency paths in the virtual resource namespace; it does not confuse those paths with native provenance, reread the source or execute Graphviz again. The executable pin alone does not make the generator's libraries, plugins, fonts or other ambient dependencies hermetic.
Captured image transformations
For placing a figure in an article and continuing the writing, return to Figures, notes and notebooks.
Image recipes use that same input, compilation, output and evidence path. They do not expose a Tera filesystem function or create another asset namespace:
[[resources]]
inputs = ["photos/source.png"]
output = "/assets/thumbnail.png"
build = { kind = "raster-image", entry = "photos/source.png", input_format = "png", apply_orientation = true, resize = { operation = "fit", width = 640, height = 480 }, encoding = { format = "png" } }

input_format is png, jpeg or single-image webp, independent of the filename. resize selects scale (exact width/height), fit-width, fit-height, fit (bounded without upscaling), or fill (center-cropped exact width/height). The fixed raster-adapter profile uses Lanczos3. Orientation is applied before resizing only when selected. Output uses eight-bit channels; PNG and lossless WebP preserve transformed alpha. Use encoding = { format = "webp" } for lossless eight-bit WebP output. With unchanged dimensions and no crop, WebP preserves every decoded eight-bit RGBA channel, including RGB beneath zero alpha; resize or orientation remains an explicit transformation. Higher-depth input is quantized by this explicit profile, not preserved at its original depth. JPEG uses an explicit quality in 1–100 and background RGB triplet, for example encoding = { format = "jpeg", quality = 85, background = [255, 255, 255] }.
The shared public resource kind is png-image, jpeg-image or webp-image. Theme chooses how to present its URL and supply authored alternative text; Gazette does not invent captions or image meaning. Both page resources and site-selected resources carry image geometry in the same public resource projection: source is the stored pixel size, oriented is its size after selected orientation handling, and output is the actual encoded size. Each has width and height. The raster adapter decodes the final encoded artifact to check its output dimensions; renderers do not reread images or guess dimensions from a resize request. Theme can set intrinsic HTML dimensions from resource.image.output.width and .height; JSON receives those same facts. Scripts, styles and fonts omit image. Preview and disclosure dispatch use the generated representation, even for an extensionless or misleadingly named output. Private evidence retains the exact recipe, source hash, compiler profile and output hash.
The raster adapter consumes only retained bytes and uses the maintained image library for transformations. Resource input/output ceilings apply alongside resource::Limits.raster pixel/buffer ceilings. These are bounded operations, not a process-wide allocation sandbox. Sampling is premultiplied-alpha in encoded channel space, not an ICC/color-managed transform. Re-encoding does not grant disclosure approval; the existing output review remains separate. Animation, video, other raster codecs, automatic responsive variants, colour-profile transformation, wide-gamut output and browser/color-management qualification are not supplied by this PNG/JPEG/WebP profile.
Bind an original image to its compiled rendition
Add rendition = true beside inputs, build and output on a page raster resource. Markdown and images.default, light and dark continue to reference the original retained source. The native reference resolver maps that recipe’s entry to its compiled output for this page, preserving query strings, fragments and public/local serving bases. Only one rendition may bind an original per page; additional variants remain ordinary resources unless explicitly selected as responsive candidates. Scripts are not searched and rewritten for matching strings.
The public resource projection exposes rendition_of, the original image’s resolved serving URL, alongside the derived url and verified image.output dimensions. A browser component can use that mapping without private paths or output-suffix guesses. Independently selected originals remain available for their other uses. After resource compilation, image occurrences carry intrinsic dimensions, and native Markdown HTML emits width/height attributes with that aspect ratio. An authored display width takes effect in the initial HTML, with height scaled proportionally and rounded to a positive integer; without verified dimensions only the declared width is emitted. The verified raster display dimensions remain separate in intrinsic. Ordinary retained PNG, JPEG and WebP images also receive native dimensions when the bounded decoder verifies their pixels and display orientation. Inspection keeps stored width and height unchanged; its optional display extent accounts for orientation. Missing orientation metadata means the stored extent applies; unrecognised orientation metadata leaves display geometry unknown. Failed inspection leaves the image transport unchanged and supplies no invented dimensions.
Supply responsive image sizes
Keep the full fallback as rendition = true, add smaller outputs with responsive = true, and declare the image's intended layout in images.sizes:
[[resources]]
rendition = true
inputs = ["portrait.png"]
output = "/images/portrait.webp"
build = { kind = "raster-image", entry = "portrait.png", input_format = "png", apply_orientation = true, resize = { operation = "fit-width", width = 1600 }, encoding = { format = "webp" } }

[[resources]]
responsive = true
inputs = ["portrait.png"]
output = "/images/portrait-small.webp"
build = { kind = "raster-image", entry = "portrait.png", input_format = "png", apply_orientation = true, resize = { operation = "fit-width", width = 640 }, encoding = { format = "webp" } }

[[images]]
default = "portrait.png"
sizes = "(max-width: 48rem) 100vw, 50vw"

Markdown keeps referencing portrait.png. Native HTML receives srcset with the verified output widths and the declared sizes; src remains the full fallback. The browser chooses a candidate for its viewport and display density. Gazette does not infer layout from filenames, container classes or an image's position on the page. sizes accepts at most 1,024 bytes of literal ASCII layout syntax; the browser evaluates its media conditions and lengths.
Each original admits up to 16 additional candidates. They must share the fallback's original, input format and orientation setting, using fit-width, fit-height or fit throughout. Cropped fill and distorted scale recipes cannot form a responsive group. Integer rounding during proportional resizing is expected: descriptors use independently decoded output widths, including when a fit bound produces a narrower image than requested. Duplicate output widths fail. Missing fallback, missing verified geometry, missing sizes on a declared responsive image, and sizes without any responsive candidates also fail. Responsive occurrences may retain a query string but cannot select an image fragment.
The image model exposes responsive.sizes and responsive.default, with responsive.light and responsive.dark when those modes are declared. Each candidate is {url, width}, ordered by increasing pixel width and including the mode's fallback. Existing destination and variants keep the full fallback URLs for image expansion. Native HTML also emits a declared dark mode as a picture source ahead of the default img, with the dark candidates and the same sizes, so the browser chooses the dark rendition before any script runs; the source's media follows the Theme's starting colour mode. A Theme changing display mode updates that source's media, or the image's srcset, sizes and src where there is no source, from the same image record; it does not derive another filename. Page resources expose responsive_of for additional candidates and retain the unique rendition_of on the fallback. Both identify the original's serving URL, using the selected public or local base.
Static SVG images
The separate svg-image recipe admits exactly one retained UTF-8 SVG and emits its exact bytes. It is an inert static-image profile, not a general XML, HTML or SVG application runtime:
[[resources]]
inputs = ["marks/icon.svg"]
output = "/assets/icon.svg"
build = { kind = "svg-image", entry = "marks/icon.svg" }

The root must be an unprefixed svg element with the exact SVG default namespace. XML declarations, DTDs, processing instructions, prefixed elements, script, style, foreignObject, inline style, event attributes, embedded data, prefixed attributes and external references are rejected. href may name only a local fragment. Parsing is bounded by the same retained-input/output limits plus finite event, nesting, name, attribute and value ceilings. The adapter neither fetches dependencies nor rewrites markup.
This profile is suitable for an explicitly selected site icon or ordinary Theme image. A link-preview role remains PNG/JPEG because social-preview consumers do not provide a portable SVG contract. The SVG profile does not support animation or active content; accessibility and publication review still depend on the selected image and presentation.
Inline SVG figures
An image declaration can opt into inline rendering while retaining its external SVG file:
[[images]]
default = "figure.svg"
inline = true
width = 480

The SVG must already be an automatic leaf-page companion or an explicit svg-image page resource. Inline rendering adds stricter validation; it does not make arbitrary SVG or raw HTML admissible. Unsupported content fails with a diagnostic instead of being silently removed. The emitted external resource retains its original bytes. A declared width sizes the inline SVG before scripts run, preserving its intrinsic viewport ratio, or its view-box ratio when intrinsic dimensions are absent. Theme CSS can constrain that width to the available column. Image renditions explains occurrence identity, the hidden image fallback and viewer integration.
The first inline profile supports exactly svg, g, title, desc, path, text, tspan, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline and polygon. Names are case-sensitive, the single root declares xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", and nested SVG roots or alternate namespaces are refused. It admits geometry and transforms, fill/stroke and their presentation attributes, opacity, font family/size/weight/style, text anchoring and spacing, viewBox, dimensions and aspect ratio. id, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and role="img" supply accessible descriptions. IDs must be unique ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, at most 256 bytes; accessibility references must resolve inside the same SVG. Each occurrence receives its own generated ID prefix, including repeated figures and notebook cells.
Live typography and colours can use currentColor or CSS variables such as font-family="var(--type-family-reading, sans-serif)" and fill="var(--color-ink, #292722)". Variables accept one --token and an optional simple fallback without nested functions. Presentation values use ASCII letters, digits, whitespace and - _ # % . , ( ) +; supported value functions are var, rgb, rgba, hsl, hsla, translate, scale, rotate, matrix, skewX and skewY. CSS escapes, style attributes/elements, classes, events, scripts, foreign content, links, paint URLs, embedded media, filters and animation are not part of this profile. XML declarations, DTDs, processing instructions, CDATA and unknown entities are refused. Text and attribute entities are decoded, validated and safely re-escaped; comments are omitted from the canonical inline markup.
Admission limits retained input to one MiB, 100,000 decoded events, 64 nested elements, 64 attributes per element and 64 KiB per attribute value. The enclosing Markdown plan and final output enforce their own byte limits. Inline rendering does not fetch files, execute code, infer captions or change image ownership.
Explicit variants can be composed with a stylesheet resource, for example:
.illustration {
  background-image: image-set("thumbnail.png" 1x type("image/png"),
                             "thumbnail-dense.jpg" 2x type("image/jpeg"));
}

Declare both raster recipes and the stylesheet using the existing resource settings. Relative URLs resolve from the stylesheet's emitted route, not its source folder. Every candidate must exist in the final output, even one a browser might skip because of its resolution or type hint. The same checked references reach Theme and the model; a missing candidate refuses the build before staging. Gazette preserves the native CSS rather than choosing a device-dependent image. Variant generation remains explicit; the browser chooses among the emitted candidates. The syntax follows the CSS Images image-set definition.
Resource caching
Multi-site SDK rendering shares a session-local resource cache; watch keeps it across generations. A hit requires the same complete input tree, recipe, selected module URLs and effective limits. Each site still resolves its own output and URL, and the application checks dependency and adapter evidence before using the result. Acquisition, semantic resolution, Theme rendering and output closure still run.
The default cache holds at most 128 successful requests and 32 MiB of logical payload: keys, output, dependency/reference strings and compiler profiles. It evicts oldest entries first and bypasses oversized results. ResourceCacheLimits can change those allowances; zero disables retention. Container overhead and returned copies are additional memory. Cache hits do not change artifact identity.
The persistent whole-site cache is separate. It stores an already completed output tree under its source, configuration, Theme/template, tool and semantic identities. A warm whole-site hit can bypass rendering. A clean cache write must revalidate the complete plan under the same adapters, options and limits. Neither cache grants publication approval or bypasses the relevant output and release checks.
External SVG layout
The existing SVG validator records root viewport geometry for both explicit svg-image resources and automatic leaf-page companions. The public svg evidence is separate from raster image geometry. Positive finite absolute root width and height establish the ratio; otherwise a valid viewBox may establish it. View-box offsets do not change the ratio. Percentage and automatic lengths do not establish intrinsic dimensions.
Native image HTML uses a known natural width or the authored display width and reserves the proportional height before scripts run. A view-box ratio alone does not invent a natural pixel size. For both rasters and SVGs, fragment-selected views and mode variants with unverified or differing ratios receive no borrowed geometry. Exact SVG bytes and the existing admission policy remain unchanged.

Configured policy checks
Run a checker you configure against a candidate review or against the complete rendered files. Gazette runs the command and checks that its response refers to the supplied inputs. Your checker decides what passes. Use output disclosure checks for Gazette's built-in string, path, endpoint and format scans.
Call these operations from the Rust application or SDK. A checker result is one input to a release decision. Gazette does not decide the applicable rights, privacy rules or publisher approval.
Configure and allow a checker
The workspace declaration accepts one optional root-level command:
[policy_check]
program = '/absolute/path/to/checker'
directory = '/absolute/path/to/workspace'
arguments = []
environment = { MODE = 'candidate-review' }

The executable and directory can use absolute native paths, workspace-relative paths or the existing machine roots. Mark path arguments explicitly as { path = 'machine:checker/check.py' }; string arguments remain literal values. Machine-bound program binding explains the shared math/checker declaration and the captured machine file. Native execution receives absolute program and directory paths. Gazette neither searches PATH nor inherits the parent environment; omitted arguments/environment are empty. Environment names use ASCII letters, digits and underscores, without a leading digit. Keep secrets out of configuration. Command text rejects NULs and is limited to 64 KiB across both paths, all arguments and environment keys/values; at most 256 arguments and 64 environment entries are supported.
Parsing this configuration performs no filesystem access or execution. A missing checker does not disable ordinary standalone local publication work. An explicit request to run a checker with none configured returns policy_unconfigured, never an invented successful check.
An independently selected executable can also be pinned in that same command:
[policy_check.executable]
bytes = 12345 # Exact file length, not an input/output budget.
sha256 = '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef'

Replace these illustrative values with the approved executable's exact length and SHA-256. Pinning is optional for ordinary local execution; it is never inferred from the file being checked. A selected pin requires a nonempty regular file of at most 256 MiB. The native runner opens it without following the final symlink, checks its complete bytes and file/path identity before spawning, retains that handle, and rechecks it after the child is reaped before returning success. The same guard applies to bounded stdout capture. A mismatch before spawn returns process_executable with not-started custody; a failed final check returns process_executable_changed with reaped custody and no captured stdout. Permission refusal still precedes executable reads. Original transport failures retain their original failure/custody evidence; they do not establish a verified executable lifetime or authorize retry.
These paired observations require trusted local namespace control. Native spawn still uses a path: this is not protection against a hostile replace-and-restore race, executable-image attestation or a sandbox. Pinning a script does not pin its interpreter; pinning an interpreter does not pin scripts, libraries, imports, policy sources or remote inputs. Those remain separately selected dependencies.
Rust callers use build::check_policy(&selected, process::Options, ReviewLimits). allow_execute defaults to false and must be acknowledged for every call. Review the trusted-code model before enabling it. Gazette selects the command from the checked object's own retained workspace, not from a second SDK/CLI command declaration. Permission and option validation precede projection or process creation.
Read the checker input and process limits
Gazette writes a compact gazette-candidate-policy/1 JSON envelope to stdin, then closes stdin. Its review is the complete {sha256, request}. Its response is either null or the original matched response. The invocation digest covers the whole envelope. A one-site check and a set check serialize it the same way. The program's stdout cannot add meaning to the source.
The checker must understand this input. Gazette does not infer rules from the executable or add arguments.
Operation	What Gazette reads or limits	
Exit-only check	Discards stdout and stderr. Uses the process result.	
Candidate or output response check	Captures stdout up to the configured limit and validates the response. Discards stderr.	
Complete stdin	16 MiB by default, with a supported maximum of 64 MiB. Review creation has its own limits. Oversized input fails without sending a prefix.	
Write stdin and wait for the child	One deadline after spawn, 30 seconds by default. Accepted range is 1 millisecond to 5 minutes.	
After failure	Attempts to terminate the direct child and allows another 100 milliseconds to reap it.	
The adapter runs on Unix. Other hosts refuse before spawn. Gazette does not promise that process creation can be interrupted. The result tells whether the child never started, was reaped or may still be running. If inspection fails, do not signal an unverified PID. An embedding application must leave child reaping and status handling to Gazette.
The configured program can read files, use the network or launch other processes. Its directory, cleared environment and timeout do not sandbox it. A failed run does not establish that descendants stopped or that no effects occurred. Inspect before retrying.
Checker-originated candidate response
The local preparation recipe can select candidate_policies for exactly every requested site. Each value is a CandidatePolicyRequirement: {policy: {id, revision, source_sha256}, command_sha256}. These are independent expectations, not values learned from stdout. This mode requires candidate_check, the configured checker with an executable pin, and the retained policy_source described below. It cannot be combined with imported review_responses and never falls back to exit-only checking.
Before the first checker runs, Gazette constructs every selected review and bounded request, matches the complete command digest and verifies the selected policy's actual captured bytes. The candidate envelope carries response: null, the independent requirement and exact policy_source. Invocations then run in stable site-key order, before any Theme or resource compilation. Policy bytes remain opaque to Gazette; their presence and digest do not establish policy-owner authority.
The checker must return the existing strict gazette-review-response/1 response on stdout. Its request_sha256 binds the inner review's exact digest; the invocation digest separately binds the entire stdin envelope. Normal exit zero and complete matching against the independently selected policy and every review occurrence are required. Any hold/exclude decision, malformed or incomplete response, changed binding or exhausted bound refuses the candidate phase without filtering or rendering. Per-response byte/decision limits and aggregate response-byte limits remain separate from request limits.
The private check retains the original matched stdout, its observed digest, review, requirement and policy source. Unlike an imported response, that stdout digest is an observation of the actual capture, not an independently supplied expectation. If a later site's candidate check fails, completed_responses preserves earlier successful sites' original matched responses alongside their completed invocations. The shared failure report retains the failing capture's digest, byte count and exit/custody evidence without exposing its raw stdout. It does not authorize retry.
Historical inspection independently reconstructs the original candidate envelope with response: null, verifies its invocation digest and retained policy file/tree binding, and reapplies the shared response matcher using the retained independent policy requirement. It neither reruns the checker nor substitutes current local policy bytes. matched-unverified and all-allow decisions establish no evaluator authenticity, evidence validity, freshness, rights or publication approval.
Check the actual rendered bytes
Select an opaque policy document through the existing pinned source declarations:
[policy_source]
source = 'source:publication-policy'
entry = 'policy.json'

The source key must be declared and a checker must be selected. Publication acquisition captures this source as a shared required input, not a Theme manifest or authored document. Its regular-file bytes must be nonempty and at most 1 MiB; the complete checker request retains its separate transport ceiling. Gazette does not interpret the document's policy language. A missing file, exhausted bound or mismatch with an independently required policy digest returns policy_source before checker execution and before staging in local preparation. There is no live reread or fallback after capture.
build::check_output_policy(&rendered, process::Options, requirement) checks the complete immutable PublicationRender, independently of any earlier candidate check. The same native execution owner is used; no source, Theme or generated directory is reopened, and no rerender or filesystem export occurs.
Its compact JSON stdin has the following transport fields:
Field	Retained value	
format	gazette-output-policy/1, distinct from candidate-review input	
repository_source_provenance	Embedded repository source provenance, not executable, feature or toolchain attestation	
mode	local; this request never represents an already certified publication	
acquisition	Existing site/configuration/source inspection evidence	
selection	Complete candidate intent, including exclusions, or null for unfiltered output	
candidate_check	The retained preceding check, including its invocation, exact review and optional original matched response, or null; never approval	
disclosure	Exact required disclosure report during preparation checking; absent in standalone diagnostic output checking	
preview_urls	Exact preview URL projection, or null when absent	
render	Existing Theme, page, asset and resource render evidence	
inventory	Complete output inventory, including directories and structural identity	
media_types	Producer-declared formats, including extensionless output paths	
files_base64	Every regular-file path and its exact bytes in standard padded Base64	
policy_source	When selected: exact {binding: {source, entry}, tree, sha256, document_base64} from retained acquisition	
Media declarations use html, json, json-ld, xml, rss, atom, text, javascript, css, png and jpeg. These identify producer representations, not HTTP headers or guessed file extensions; transport adapters retain their own MIME projection.
Binary and hidden files are not filtered, guessed as UTF-8 or replaced by hashes. Payload encoding streams through the bounded JSON writer without an intermediate encoded copy of each file. The stdin ceiling covers the entire wire representation, including Base64 expansion and provenance; exceeding it prevents process creation. The request is an Engine transport, not a schema for any owner's policy judgments.
Stream complete output without a Base64 copy
Select policy_output_transport = "framed-v2" at the workspace root when the checker implements this protocol. Omission or "inline-v1" preserves the JSON envelope above. Candidate-review input remains JSON. The same SDK and preparation operations honor the selected output transport; an embedder without segmented native capture refuses it instead of falling back.
The stream contains, in order:
The ASCII bytes gazette-output-policy/2\n, ending with one line-feed byte.
An unsigned 64-bit big-endian metadata length, then exactly that many UTF-8 JSON bytes.
For each file in inventory.entries order, an unsigned 64-bit big-endian file length followed by its exact raw bytes. Directories have no frame.
EOF immediately after the final file.
The header retains the fields above, uses format: "gazette-output-policy/2" and omits files_base64 entirely. Every directory and file remains in the inventory. Entries have unique, lexical UTF-8 relative paths with explicit directory parents. A directory is {path, kind: "directory"}; a file is {path, kind: "file", bytes, sha256}. The inventory also carries total_bytes and its gazette.inventory.v1 identity. The native inventory identity defines its length-framed encoding; neither filesystem paths nor timestamps enter it.
The checker must reject duplicate or invalid inventory entries, a wrong inventory identity or total, missing or extra frames, mismatched file lengths or SHA-256 values, truncation and trailing bytes. It must finish checking every member and EOF before returning an allow response. gazette-output-response/1 remains the response format; request_sha256 hashes every transmitted byte, including the magic, lengths, metadata and file payloads, rather than the header alone.
The metadata retains the caller's max_input_bytes ceiling: 16 MiB by default and at most 64 MiB. The framed profile separately supports at most 10,000 inventory entries, 64 MiB per file and 512 MiB of aggregate raw file bytes, matching the native source defaults. Framing adds eight bytes per file plus the magic and metadata-length prefix. The producer retains a bounded metadata buffer and borrowed file segments; it does not allocate the concatenated request or another Base64 copy. A checker can preserve whole-file analysis while retaining one bounded file at a time. These are explicit logical budgets, not a process-wide memory guarantee.
Input delivery, selected output capture, EOF and child exit share the existing deadline. Permission, command and executable-pin checks remain mandatory, including pin verification after execution. No publication tree is exported or reopened, and no source or output member is excluded to meet a limit.
A normal zero exit is necessary for OutputPolicyCheck. With no requirement, this is exit-only evidence and response is null. Its receipt contains output-policy-check-passed-unverified, invocation digests and the structural output identity. candidate_check_sha256 binds the exact private candidate-check object delivered to the output checker, or is null when absent. During preparation checking it also includes disclosure_sha256, the digest of the exact serialized report delivered in the request. Standalone diagnostic checking has no disclosure report or disclosure digest. Rust callers can borrow the exact checked render through rendered(); serialized receipts contain neither that render nor its file payloads. Changing any delivered output, selection or evidence changes the request identity. Per-site checks do not settle a multi-site release set.
Independently bound output response
Some(&OutputPolicyRequirement) additionally requires an explicitly pinned executable, the exact compact-JSON command digest, an independently selected ReviewPolicy (id, revision, source_sha256) and a complete stdout allowance response_bytes from 1 byte through 64 MiB. Command mismatch refuses before staging in local preparation. This mode also requires policy_source; Gazette hashes the actual retained file and matches ReviewPolicy.source_sha256 before execution. A missing checker or policy source never falls back to exit-only mode. The pin covers the executable, not interpreter scripts, imports or policy-source authenticity; their qualification remains with the selecting owner.
The checker must return one closed, named JSON object:
{
  "format": "gazette-output-response/1",
  "request_sha256": "<SHA-256 of exact stdin bytes>",
  "policy": {"id": "policy:site", "revision": "revision:selected", "source_sha256": "<policy-source SHA-256>"},
  "outcome": "allow",
  "evidence": ["evidence:policy-check"]
}

Policy identities, revision identifiers and evidence references are complete namespace:local keys. Revisions are strings, not numbers.
Expected response coordinates are not added to stdin for the checker to echo. The actual selected document is delivered; its own content may declare policy identity or revision, which the checker must interpret and evaluate independently. Early candidate checking is optional and its policy is never copied into this requirement. Gazette matches the actual output-request digest and the checker's reported policy against the independent requirement. Evidence references must be nonempty and unique; their existence or validity is not inferred. Hold, exclude, nonzero exit, malformed/duplicate/positional JSON and output overflow fail without modifying the rendered tree or proceeding to Git preparation.
The private response retains the exact original stdout text, its digest and the requirement under checker-reported-policy-matched-unverified. The same matcher verifies retained preparation history. Native failures retain the original capture and invocation; CLI/MCP diagnostics report its digest, byte count, exit and direct-child custody without exposing raw private stdout. Failure after staging preserves that stage's original receipt and never retries the checker. Complete capture is bounded by the native execution deadline; an overflow or incomplete pipe yields no purported complete response.
The private output-check evidence retains the selected policy document once, or an explicit null when none was selected. Historical inspection rechecks its canonical Base64, actual digest and exact file/tree coordinates against the original preparation's source inventory before matching the recorded response. Neither a new local file nor a different historical expectation rewrites that retained input. Source integrity is not source-owner authentication or approval.
This is matched checker-reported evidence, not authenticated policy approval. The delivered request binds output, provenance and disclosure, but does not independently qualify the Engine binary, scanner, checker dependencies or policy owner. Those acceptance obligations remain separate.
Required preparation checks
build::check_preparation(&rendered, &disclosure_policy, process_options, disclosure_limits, requirement) joins the required disclosure scan and optional workspace checker over one immutable selected render. It first rejects preview or missing publication selection, validates the required policy and performs its bounded scan. Findings, unsupported decoding or exhausted scan bounds prevent checker execution. When a checker is configured, it receives that same report together with the complete output request above; the existing request digest covers the report as well as the output and provenance.
The returned PreparationChecks privately retains the exact report and optional OutputPolicyCheck. Its disclosure() and policy() accessors expose those actual results, not replaceable inputs. A generic workspace with no checker retains the required scan with policy() == None; it does not manufacture a passing invocation. An arbitrary diagnostic report cannot be supplied in place of the required scan, and a standalone OutputPolicyCheck cannot be promoted into this combined result.
build::record_preparation_check(&checks, request, options) records the retained results against the original staging intent. It neither rescans output nor invokes the checker. The durable disclosure bytes must match the report delivered to the checker, and the stored invocation binds their exact digest. A changed policy requires a new scan and, when configured, a new checker invocation; recording cannot append a new scan to an old invocation. Immutable-history conflicts remain explicit.
Read the checker result
A normal zero exit after complete stdin delivery returns a PolicyCheck with policy-check-passed-unverified. The private result contains the request and command digests, the review and any matched response. Nonzero or abnormal exit returns policy_rejected with the same invocation coordinates. A transport failure records its phase and whether the child was reaped. A response-producing candidate check also requires a complete all-allow match. When the exit or response fails, Gazette keeps the capture and invocation for inspection.
The command digest covers the bound native paths and arguments, literal arguments, environment and the executable pin when present. Independent candidate/output requirements compare this resolved native command, never the portable declaration; a machine relocation can therefore require a new independently selected command digest. A successful pinned check records the executable byte checks before and after the process. It does not verify dependencies or what the program did with stdin. An output check binds the rendered bytes and, during preparation, the required disclosure report. A passing invocation cannot supply rights, approval, a certificate or a release token.
For a custom checker, test an allowed result, an explicit rejection, malformed output and a process timeout. Gazette's process and publication tests cover the transport; your checker needs examples that express your publication's actual rules.

Local publication preview
Embed a local publication server, supervise it as a process or serve files your application has already rendered. Gazette reports which addresses are listening and lets your host stop them. In watch mode, readers continue to get the last complete build while the next one runs.
For the author’s setup, see Your first publication. Preview serves from memory and leaves the publication’s output directory and release journal untouched. Configured generation programs need execution permission separately from reading files and opening listeners. Documentation generation also needs an explicit private staging parent, as described below. Review the trusted-code model before granting that permission.
Choose an entrypoint and URL mode
Your host needs	Use	
Serve until the host requests stop, with callbacks for state changes	preview::runner::run, demonstrated below	
Keep serving while the host handles other work	preview::session::Session; background ownership	
Serve output the host has already acquired and rendered	preview::bind, or reserve/render/attach for local URLs; borrowed lifecycle	
Supervise Gazette as a subprocess	gazette preview-sites; process input and shutdown	
Choose the URL mode independently of watch mode:
Local links
Set local_urls: true in runner options, or pass --local-urls to the CLI. Gazette reserves the loopback sockets first, then renders links with those actual addresses. Aliases, search, feeds, sitemaps, structured data and resources use the same route model. Object and feed identities do not change.
Public links
Keep the configured canonical addresses, redirects and cross-site links. This is useful when checking how output will link after delivery. Following a link or loading an absolute resource can contact a public host.
Both modes keep the publication's deployment path prefix. Publications outside the preview keep their public addresses. Literal external URLs in program bytes are not rewritten, and the local server does not restrict your browser's network access.
Embed the shared runner
Your application supplies a parsed build::LocalPublicationRecipe, an exact site-to-SocketAddr map and a way to request stop. The recipe is the gazette-local-publication-set/1 input, with the selected workspace and sites. Parse its bytes with build::LocalPublicationRecipe::parse_json, supplying the request-byte and site-count bounds. Configuration and content must already satisfy the normal rendering prerequisites; the helper does not create a publication.
This complete helper uses pinned acquisition and developer-local URLs. Pass one loopback address for every selected site; port zero asks the OS to allocate a port. The caller's status writer is private because runtime observations include input and output identities. Its stop predicate can read a host-owned cancellation flag.
use std::{collections::BTreeMap, io::Write, net::SocketAddr};
use gazette_sdk::{build::LocalPublicationRecipe, preview, workspace::Key};
use preview::{runner, watch};

pub fn serve_preview(
    recipe: &LocalPublicationRecipe,
    listeners: BTreeMap<Key, SocketAddr>,
    status: &mut impl Write,
    mut should_stop: impl FnMut() -> bool,
) -> Result<(), runner::Error> {
    let options = runner::Options {
        local_urls: true,
        listeners: preview::Options {
            allow_listeners: true,
            ..Default::default()
        },
        ..Default::default()
    };

    runner::run(
        recipe,
        listeners,
        options,
        |event| {
            if let runner::Event::Ready { state } = &event {
                for (site, bound) in &state.sites {
                    writeln!(status, "{site}: {}", bound.url)?;
                }
            }
            writeln!(status, "{event:?}")
        },
        || Ok(if should_stop() {
            watch::Control::Stop
        } else {
            watch::Control::Continue
        }),
    )
}

Use the reported URLs only after Ready: successful entry into the operation is not listener readiness. All selected listeners and the initial complete generation must be available before that event. The runner serves while it checks the stop predicate at native checkpoints; a stop request does not interrupt in-progress capture, compilation or HTTP work. When the runner returns successfully, its listeners have been released. A source, rendering, listener or status-delivery failure returns an error instead of a smaller successful preview set.
The defaults keep acquisition pinned. To adopt working-tree changes under the same bindings, select runner::Mode::Development { interval }; the watch contract explains stale output and recovery.
Shared runner and background ownership
Use preview::session::Session when your host needs to keep doing other work while serving the preview. One worker owns its recipe, captured sources, rendered files and local sockets.
Start the session
Call Session::start(recipe, addresses, options, limits). The result is a running worker, not a ready server. A startup failure is reported separately.
Wait for readiness
Use inspect() for the current Snapshot, or poll(after, maximum) for events. Start the event cursor at zero and save the returned next cursor. Wait for Event::Ready before opening the reported URLs.
Polling does not drive the server. You can repeat a cursor after losing a response. If old events have been overwritten, the result reports a gap while keeping the latest state and terminal outcome.
Stop and join the worker
Call request_stop(), wait until Snapshot.finished, then call try_finish() to obtain the terminal result. It returns None while the worker is active. A Closed callback alone does not prove that the worker has finished.
Dropping the session requests a stop but does not wait for it. Use the explicit sequence when your host needs confirmation that serving ended. The MCP preview operations use this same lifetime.
Direct command
Use --workspace-root /absolute/path/to/workspace to load the configured build directly, or pass one compact gazette-local-publication-set/1 JSON request as the first line on stdin. Use the same recipe as render-sites. Escape the TOML newlines inside a supplied source value. For a workspace on disk, name its absolute root and root-relative manifest. The CLI checks the line's byte count before parsing or reading sources.
gazette preview-sites --local --allow-listeners \
  --listen site:one=127.0.0.1:0 --local-urls

The workspace supplies the corpus limit and math selection through [build]. --max-corpus-bytes and --math true|false override them; --allow-execute separately permits configured math and share-card generation. A share-card recipe requires explicitly pinned Node and browser bindings; no browser is selected implicitly. Each watch generation uses the settings resolved at startup. Repeat --listen for each site. Port zero asks the OS to choose the port. With --local-urls, the build uses those assigned addresses, including during share-card capture. Otherwise links use the public configuration. Read the actual URL mode and addresses in the ready result.
Add --plan to see which sites, loopback endpoints and effects the request calls for before it runs. The plan contains no local paths. source_reads is once in pinned mode and repeated in watch mode. Other fields distinguish derived-state and output writes, listeners, loopback/outbound network, Git reads and writes, release approval consumption and configured programs. The SDK checks the same plan during execution. Plan mode does not read configured sources, start programs, listen, write or contact a remote.
Keep stdin open after the initial request, or from startup when using --workspace-root. Any additional byte or EOF asks the server to stop. A closed input file causes immediate shutdown after startup. Wait for readiness before using the addresses and for the close result to confirm the listeners were released. If the CLI cannot write its result, it fails. See --help for input, rendering, header and deadline limits.
The command makes these effects explicit before execution:
Effect	Behavior	
Source reads	Exact configured source acquisition; --watch repeatedly captures disclosed working bytes while verifying unchanged Git baseline bindings	
In-memory compilation	Shared content, Theme, resource and machine-output pipeline	
Local network	Explicit loopback listeners and responses to connecting clients	
Gazette output stages and journal writes	None	
Gazette outbound platform/integration calls	None	
Configured math/diagram programs	Only when separately selected and permitted; their effects are not sandboxed	
Git mutation, signing, release consumption or deployment	None	
gazette production-preview is a narrower process entrypoint: it requires --registry unconfigured and --artifact fresh-render, fixes pinned capture and configured public links, and uses the same recipe and runtime. It does not accept local URLs, watch mode, registry reconciliation or retained prepared artifacts. It performs the reads, compilation and listening described above, including any separately permitted math or diagram generation. Gazette does not stage output, mutate Git, prepare a release, consume release authority or deploy from this command.
Shared operation and lifecycle
Rust callers first use build::acquire_publications and build::render_publications, then pass the retained result, an exact site-to- socket map and explicit preview::Options to preview::bind. Import preview::PreviewSession for the session operations.
For developer-local URLs, use preview::reserve after acquisition, then preview::render with that reservation and the normal render options, and finally preview::attach. Import preview::PreviewReservation to inspect the held addresses and typed local bases. Reservation has no serving API: the same sockets remain owned throughout compilation and attachment, including OS-assigned ports. There is no probe/rebind window. Failed rendering or attachment requires dropping the reservation; the CLI does this automatically without announcing readiness.
The pure multi-site render options expose the same explicit preview_urls map; it must exactly match the selected sites, use literal HTTP loopback addresses with nonzero effective ports, and preserve configured path prefixes. This is projection input, not proof that a listener is held. The SDK preview path supplies the map from its reservation; attachment checks exact equality. Ordinary bind refuses developer-local output because it cannot reacquire the original session.
The map belongs to this session's private evidence and sockets. It never enters the workspace or SQLite registry, so another preview or a later production render cannot inherit it, including after cancellation, panic or process exit. Durable staging preparation refuses developer-local output before any writer, journal or filesystem action.
Every requested render must have succeeded. Binding a smaller successful subset is refused, including when only one site failed.
Every site has one explicit loopback address. Port zero requests an OS-assigned port; the session's addresses() reports the actual bound set and urls() projects usable local entry URLs with their configured path prefixes.
All listeners are held before readiness. Failure on a later bind releases earlier sockets without claiming a reduced ready set.
poll() accepts at most one connection and performs bounded request/response work. An idle result permits a short caller wait. Client disconnection or timeout is distinct from response completion; listener failure terminates the set instead of silently losing a site.
For a directly borrowed HTTP session, close() or drop releases its sockets. This differs from the background handle, whose drop requests stop rather than proving closure.
The output is immutable for each borrowed generation lifetime. Source or Theme changes after acquisition do not change those bytes. A fresh input capture and complete render are needed to install a different generation.
Development watch and rebuild
Select runner::Mode::Development { interval } in Rust or --watch in the CLI to recapture working-tree changes. Either URL mode is supported. The initial workspace, site recipes, source roots, commits, parent gitlinks, Theme selections and listener addresses stay fixed; changing those bindings requires a new run. The CLI retains the configuration resolved from its initial request or --workspace-root; configuration changes require a restart.
The configured checkout baseline must still exist and match the declared HEAD and parent/child pins, while working files beneath the selected roots may differ. These captures are development observations, including when their bytes match the baseline. They cannot enter verified-source materialization or durable publication preparation. Pinned acquisition instead requires byte equality with the baseline.
Each --watch-interval-ms interval (default 500, allowed 100–3600000) performs a fresh confined capture of the exact configured source universe, including the shared Theme, explicitly enabled plugin packages and the content needed for cross-site relationships. Capture and Git metadata remain subject to the normal per-source and aggregate ceilings. Polling compares retained tree identities, not mtimes or event labels: same-byte saves and bursts coalesce, while additions, deletions, renames and atomic saves become actual capture changes. No machine-wide scan or native watcher installation is involved. Changes during capture remain subject to the reader's consistency checks; this is not an atomic cross-repository snapshot.
Changed inputs run through the same complete semantic, Theme, resource and machine output compiler. The SDK keeps one bounded resource cache for the watch session, so unchanged resource requests can reuse compiled bytes after fresh acquisition. The exact retained input tree (including unused declared prerequisites), recipe, selected module URLs and every effective compilation limit form the key. Compiler- adapter replacement starts a new cache. No error is cached; every reused artifact still passes the application's dependency, geometry, reference and output checks. Every requested site must succeed before replacing the generation. Listener reservations stay held during acquisition and compilation. A scoped transport worker serves the previous complete generation while that bounded work runs; compilers and their session-local caches remain on the calling thread. The worker is joined before the complete output set changes, including on failure or unwind. Per-request transport limits still apply. This does not provide per-browser multi-request snapshot isolation: requests on either side of a successful replacement can observe different generations.
The private control stream reports:
ready: initial complete generation attached to actual listeners.
changed: a new complete generation installed on the same sockets (the Rust observer's Event::Rebuilt).
rebuild_failed: the old generation remains served but is explicitly stale.
recovered: fresh acquisition again matches the previously retained generation; its generation number does not falsely advance.
closed: the session's listeners are released.
Observer/report-delivery or listener failure terminates the run; a later build failure instead keeps the last complete generation and reports the reason. Source and Theme changes that arrive during a build are acquired on a subsequent poll. No browser auto-refresh script is injected; refresh the browser after a successful rebuild. Live configuration rebinding and browser live reload remain separate work.
For direct watch-loop integration, preview::watch::run accepts its fixed Request, bounded Options and an observer returning Control::Continue or Control::Stop. Its Event::Poll is a quiet cancellation checkpoint, not a progress notification. This application-owned loop uses the normal build adapters and retains each generation's exact source and render evidence without copying payloads or self-referential borrows.
Include generated documentation in discovery
Imported reference pages join search and reading outputs without running a generator. For a configured generated reference, preview-sites --documentation-generation-parent /absolute/private/stages --allow-execute selects an existing staging parent and permits its pinned tools to run. The parent must be separate from all captured source and configuration roots. The rendering guide explains the complete source limits, including an explicit entry ceiling for builds that need more than the default.
The CLI emits original documentation results before Ready, and the served state retains the same results. Failed rendering or output delivery does not erase stages already created; inspect the recorded paths before retrying. Documentation results have their own bounded capacity, separate from the preview state’s metadata limit. A lost output pipe returns failure and preserves the complete evidence on stderr.
SDK hosts selecting generation use preview::runner::run_with_documentation_delivery and consume its DocumentationDelivery callback, including original native failure custody, before returning from that callback. The ordinary runner::run entry refuses this selection. Background preview::session::Session also refuses it before creating a worker, with preview_documentation_custody_unavailable; use the synchronous callback entry for this case. In watch mode, unchanged captured documentation inputs reuse their generated catalog. Changed inputs regenerate it; an unchanged failed attempt retains and replays its original failure instead of running the tools again.
Developer-local documentation links
Run Gazette's publication preview and Mintlify's documentation preview as two separate servers. Each reports its own local address. To make links from the publication open that local documentation server, a publication recipe can supply preview_link_bases, a private JSON object mapping exact public bases to literal HTTP loopback bases with the same mount path. Use the documentation server's actual held address, for example:
{"https://docs.example/": "http://127.0.0.1:43000/"}

The publication operation requires developer-local preview_urls; the preview runner derives those site URLs from its reserved listeners. Ordinary hyperlinks to those selected publications use the same local bases as identity references. The additional map projects documentation hyperlinks and configured Docs resource actions at the URL-binding boundary, preserving the remaining path, query and fragment. An owned documentation destination without a selected local provider refuses the local render instead of silently linking to its public host. Unrelated external addresses, canonical/source identities, code examples and raw text stay unchanged; this requires no new authoring syntax.
The CLI can add this mapping without editing the saved request:
cat "$GAZETTE_REQUEST" - | "$GAZETTE" preview-sites \
  --local --allow-listeners --local-urls --watch \
  --listen site:field-notes=127.0.0.1:0 \
  --preview-link-bases-json '{"https://docs.field-notes.example/":"http://127.0.0.1:3909/"}'

Use the documentation server's actual address. The flag requires --local-urls. It adds the map to the native preview request; it does not change the saved request or article. Conflicting maps, duplicate keys and non-loopback destinations fail before serving.
For the reciprocal direction, the Mintlify target accepts the same native map while assembling a private preview. Use the actual Gazette listener address for that return link. Both outputs retain the selected map in their private evidence. No override is written into the workspace or registry, and durable preparation or maintained-output replacement refuses an output carrying this local projection. A fresh ordinary assembly/render without the map retains public links and refuses loopback hyperlinks in page and manual prose; code examples remain literal.
Requests the preview server accepts
The HTTP adapter uses a pinned native request parser and the existing RoutePath codec to map validated paths to exact retained files. Directory indexes require an actual retained index.html; missing files do not fall back to another page or native directory. Request handling cannot open symlinks, special files or changed disk entries.
Requests and connection lifetime
Requests require HTTP/1.1, GET or HEAD and exactly one Host matching the actual socket address reported at startup. DNS names are not accepted as equivalent hosts. The profile rejects request bodies, transfer encodings, upgrades and unsupported request forms. It closes each connection after one response and does not process pipelined follow-up requests. It does not promise to detect bytes that arrive after that response has begun.
A valid local page navigation with no retained output returns an HTML 404. It links to Home at the selected mount when present, and to Search when the selected search page was emitted. HEAD sends the same headers without a body. Missing resources and refused requests keep the plain response. The recovery page is assembled when the preview attaches a complete output.
Response compression
Preview negotiates gzip through Accept-Encoding for text, JSON, XML, feeds, manifests and SVG. It compresses bodies of at least 1 KiB when doing so saves bytes; when the client explicitly refuses identity encoding, smaller text can also use gzip. Quality values, wildcard preferences and explicit refusals are respected. If neither available representation is acceptable, preview returns an empty 406 response. Malformed encoding preferences return 400.
GET and HEAD use the same negotiated Content-Length and Content-Encoding; HEAD sends no body. Responses carry Vary: Accept-Encoding and retain Cache-Control: no-store, so a changed preview never depends on an older browser cache. Encoding happens within the response deadline with a bounded temporary buffer; it changes neither the retained source bytes nor their identity. Images, fonts and video remain unencoded, and video range offsets still refer to their original bytes.
This describes the local preview. A deployment host must negotiate its own compression and caching; Gazette does not establish those settings by emitting a compressed sidecar file.
Response formats and media ranges
Header byte/count ceilings apply before unbounded retention. Request and response timeouts are total deadlines for each phase; trickling bytes does not renew them. Generated pages, resources, feeds and machine outputs retain their producer-declared media types even when their configured paths have no extension or a misleading suffix. The transport does not sniff their bytes or reconstruct formats from filenames. Untyped static assets use a bounded filename mapping; unknown types remain non-sniffable binary data. Retained .mp4 and .webm files use video/mp4 and video/webm respectively, and advertise Accept-Ranges: bytes. GET supports one closed, open-ended or suffix byte range, slicing borrowed bytes without copying. A valid unsatisfiable range returns 416 and Content-Range: bytes */length; malformed, unknown-unit or multipart ranges return the complete representation. HEAD ignores Range; If-Range receives the full representation because preview has no validators. Duplicate Range headers and ranges on other media remain refused. Range handling does not validate the media container. Responses are non-cacheable and supply no permissive CORS policy. The local server provides neither authentication nor process isolation.
What preview can and cannot do
Preview success establishes local serving of the selected retained generation. Release, disclosure checks and browser interaction assessment have their own owners; preview does not replace them. Render and acquisition bounds still apply alongside the HTTP limits above. Use only content and scripts trusted for execution in the selected local browser.
The SDK runner, background session and borrowed session expose the implementation entrypoints. The MCP contract defines its process-local handle and result-delivery rules over the same runtime.
When changing preview behavior, check the SDK session lifecycle, MCP handle lifecycle and CLI server behavior:
cargo test --locked -p gazette-sdk --test preview
cargo test --locked -p gazette-mcp --lib preview
cargo test --locked -p gazette-launcher --test preview_mcp
cargo test --locked -p gazette-launcher --test publication_render preview
