Recovery without guessing
Inspect an interrupted operation before you repeat it. A process exit or a missing reply leaves open whether the operation wrote files or pushed to a remote.
Keep the original request and result
Save the request, any result returned, the journal and the output path. You need these to identify the same operation after restarting.
Inspect the destination
For a push, read the remote refs. For a local write, inspect the destination or journal. Do not repeat a write or push to find out whether the first one worked.
Continue from the state you can verify
Compare the observed state with the original request. If you cannot determine what happened, preserve both and stop before making another change.
Gazette uses an ordinary approved Git push. GitHub Pages or Mintlify may then build from GitHub. The destination does not need a Gazette receiver or recovery script.
Local output
render-site, documentation assembly and preparation write to fresh staging locations. To update a configured destination, use the output writer. When staging reports leftover files or completed private output, keep the path it reports. Inspect the directory before deciding whether to keep or remove it. Use a fresh directory for the next build.
SQLite store
Use inspect-store to read metadata without acquiring a writer. It does not create or upgrade a database. SQLite coordination-file maintenance needs separate permission even when the SQL is read-only. Check journal compatibility before using another executable version.
Use backup-store to create a verified copy and verify-backup to compare it with the manifest digest you stored separately. prepare-store-restore creates and checks a separate copy. It does not replace or open the live journal for writing. Keep the original store, backup, manifest and restore result until you have verified that the intended replacement is live. An old snapshot must never make a used authorization valid again or allow a second effect.
Release transaction
Find the approval, its lease and consumption, the attempt, and its reconciliation separately in the journal:
inspect-release-authorization
inspect-release-leases
inspect-release-consumption
inspect-release-attempts
inspect-release-reconciliations

Use recovery-session to inspect the interrupted transaction. It cannot dispatch or retry a release. Read the remote refs in the original request, record what the remote returned and reconcile the already consumed authorization. If bytes, destinations or preconditions have changed, obtain a new approval.
What the remote shows	What you can record in settlement mode	
The intended change happened	The release took effect	
The original state is intact and no change happened	The release had no effect	
The remote conflicts with both states	Keep the conflict for review	
There is not enough information to tell	Keep the interruption unresolved	
For an interrupted receive-pack, observe-interrupted only records the observation. It cannot settle or seal the consumed release even if the current refs look conclusive. Provider build and served-site observations follow Git read-back and cannot change its result.
Find the command inputs
Use CLI help or the live MCP catalog that VS Code uses. Keep local paths, journal coordinates and approval data in your private request.
gazette recovery-session --help
gazette observe-release-targets --help
gazette record-release-observation --help
gazette inspect-release-reconciliations --help

These commands inspect or record recovery state. Publishing still requires approval from the publisher.

Releasing
Release the generated files the publishers approved. The ordinary path prepares the complete output for review, records the publisher’s explicit confirmation of its digest, and pushes each target with that publisher’s selected credential. Gazette retains the exact intent, attempts and independent read-back needed to inspect an interrupted push. Signed authorization remains an optional mode.
GitHub Pages or Mintlify may build and serve a site after the push. Gazette needs no receiver service or scripts on the destination. Verify the push and the served pages as separate steps.
The chain
Step	Command or operation	What it leaves behind	
Prepare	gazette prepare-sites	For each site: a retained stage, its disclosure and output checks, and a verified local Git commit on an independent deployment worktree	
Inspect	gazette inspect-release-preparations	Confirms the whole prepared set is complete and consistent; certifies nothing	
Hold a writer	gazette release-session (open)	One anchored journal writer at a known generation	
Review	release-session operation review	The complete verified set, its publisher scopes, owner credentials and confirmation digest; no approval is granted	
Confirm	The publisher reviews the output	Explicit confirmation of the exact digest returned for review	
Register	release-session operation register_reviewed	The original confirmed bytes, held in custody	
Consume	release-session operation consume_reviewed	One intent per target, recorded once; the approval can never be used again	
Dispatch	release-session operation dispatch_reviewed	One attempt per target: a durable start, the push, and its result	
Read back	gazette observe-release-targets, gazette record-release-observation	What each destination actually holds	
Settle	release-session operation reconcile	A settlement per release, appended to its history	
gazette mcp offers the same session as open_release_session, operate_release_session and close_release_session.
Preparing
Pass one private JSON request to gazette prepare-sites. It contains the workspace, journal, expected journal header, decisions about which content to include, disclosure rules, candidate check and each site's render and stage settings. Supply required nullable fields explicitly. Use the recipe schema for optional fields.
Gazette checks the complete request before reading sources. It refuses unfiltered, preview and development output. It captures the inputs once, renders the set, then prepares the sites in order. For each site it scans for private values and runs the configured output checker over the bytes to be delivered. A refusal keeps the stage and stops before Git.
Each deploy commit uses a separate worktree and an explicit parent, with no remotes, hooks or linked worktrees. Gazette reads the commit back before reporting it. The publication’s repository supplies its Git destination on main; an explicit destination = { kind = "git", remote, branch } overrides those coordinates. With neither field, the site has no delivery target. deployable remains the release eligibility switch; configuring a repository does not grant release approval.
If any site fails, the report marks the set incomplete, lists the sites already prepared and names the failed phase. Previous work stays in place. Inspect it before continuing instead of submitting the same request as a new attempt.
Set up configured output repositories
gazette materialize-sites --checkouts /absolute/private/checkouts.json can prepare each configured output repository before the existing journal-owned output write. MCP materialize_sites accepts the same optional checkouts object. It must contain exactly the rendered site set, keyed by site ID. The retained workspace supplies each remote and branch, including the repository → main default; the setup request does not repeat a destination.
Each entry contains git, expected, history, read and options. git selects the absolute native executable, empty private isolation directory and optional explicit credential helper. expected selects the local state: {"state":"missing"}, {"state":"unborn"}, or {"state":"commit","oid":"…"}. history selects an independently observed remote parent: {"kind":"acquire","expected":"…","root":"/absolute/private/new-history.git","allow_acquire":true} fetches into a fresh bare repository; {"kind":"retained","expected":"…","source":{"kind":"bare","path":"/absolute/private/history.git"}} uses complete retained history. {"kind":"unborn"} requires a qualified native observation of absence; a silent or failed HTTPS advertisement cannot establish that state. read carries separate read/network permissions and process bounds. options carries separate allow_initialize, allow_update and repository admission limits. All permissions default to denied.
Acquisition checks the expected branch before fetching, verifies the complete local commit/tree/blob ancestry, and reads the remote ref independently afterward. Native storage is admitted against a size limit after fetching; that limit is not a hard cap on bytes written by the Git process. Process deadlines and captured-output limits remain separate. Failure retains the selected local history path and its possible effects; Gazette never substitutes a root commit or retries acquisition automatically.
Output setup creates missing metadata or adopts only a strictly empty independent repository, preserving an existing .git directory’s identity. It records the configured branch, origin tracking and the parent’s index without checking remote files out over generated or unrelated files. An existing configured branch must match the selected local commit and can advance only to a verified descendant. Detached preparation worktrees remain separate. Pending materialization history, unsafe configuration, unrelated refs, divergence or a changed root identity refuses setup. If a later site fails, the result retains the completed metadata prefix; generated output is written only after the original complete-set output planner succeeds. Keep the request and result for inspection instead of rerunning a partly completed setup.
Build a local preparation request
Preparation uses the shared SDK build::LocalPreparationRecipe. To discover its exact JSON shape through MCP, find prepare_sites in the paginated tools/list response. Its inputSchema.properties.recipe_json.contentSchema is generated from that recipe's Rust owner. The outer input schema separately describes native permissions and limits. Tool discovery explains discovery; the declaration-schema CLI does not expose this recipe.
A one-site caller can construct the request below from its own retained inputs. Work in a private directory and supply these files:
File	Value it supplies	
workspace.toml	A complete one-file workspace with absolute configured source locations and the selected site/destination.	
expected-header.json	The exact {schema_version, journal_id, journal_epoch, writer_fence} observed for the existing journal; do not predict a successor generation.	
coordinator.json	The independently retained {anchor_root, binding} from enrollment; explicit JSON null selects an ordinary unguarded writer. Release work uses the enrolled selection described in Store.	
disclosure.json	The actual private prohibition policy, with all six classes; see required checks. Example or empty rules cannot stand in for those values.	
commit-metadata.json	Explicit parent, author, committer and message. Each author/committer has name, email, nonnegative Unix seconds and offset_minutes. This example requires parent: null; an existing parent also needs a selected native parent_source.	
preparation-id.txt	A new, caller-selected 64-character lowercase SHA-256 identity, retained with this request before invoking preparation. Reuse is inspected, never treated as a fresh attempt.	
Save this as make-preparation.py, substitute your own absolute journal/stage roots and exact site identity, and run it once to write preparation.json:
import json
from pathlib import Path

def unique_object(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate JSON key: {key}")
        result[key] = value
    return result

def read_json(name):
    return json.loads(Path(name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=unique_object)

metadata = read_json("commit-metadata.json")
if metadata["parent"] is not None:
    raise ValueError("This example selects a root commit; supply a parent source for history")

request = {
    "workspace": {"kind": "supplied", "source": Path("workspace.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")},
    "journal": "/absolute/private/journal",
    "expected_header": read_json("expected-header.json"),
    "coordinator": read_json("coordinator.json"),
    "disclosure": read_json("disclosure.json"),
    "candidate_check": None,
    "sites": [{
        "render": {"site": "site:notes", "model_output": "model.json", "graph": None},
        "stage_parent": "/absolute/private/stages",
        "stage_name": "notes-candidate",
        "preparation_id": Path("preparation-id.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip(),
        "metadata": metadata,
        "parent_source": None,
    }],
}
with Path("preparation.json").open("x", encoding="utf-8") as output:
    json.dump(request, output, ensure_ascii=False)
    output.write("\n")

This example supplies one complete TOML buffer. For a modular workspace.kind = "local" request, include its complete native limits object as shown in the discovered recipe schema; preparation requires the serialized named shape, including those nested defaults.
The stage parent must already exist, be private and be separate from the source, journal and history roots. The workspace must select deployable output and its explicit destination. candidate_check: null selects no pre-render checker; it does not create a passing review. A configured output checker still runs over the rendered bytes. To require candidate responses or a qualified output policy, use the policy-check selections and the exact recipe schema rather than adding an unchecked approval field.
For an enrolled local preparation, the corresponding command is:
gazette prepare-sites --local --allow-read --create-stage \
  --record-preparation --advance-writer-generation --reserve-local-coordination \
  --write-coordinator-anchor --allow-coordination-files --initialize-worktree \
  < preparation.json > preparation-result.json

A configured checker also needs --allow-policy-execution. That permission runs its selected command with native effects; it is not a process sandbox. Review gazette prepare-sites --help for independent input, output and process limits. This command creates local stages, journal records and Git objects; it neither signs nor pushes. Retain both input and output even when the command fails.
On success, status is local-preparations-complete-not-certified, and sites contains the preparation receipts. not-started means preparation did not begin; candidate-failed and render-failed preserve the earlier checker/render evidence. An incomplete report contains requested, completed and the failed site/phase. Inspect that completed prefix and any later stage, stage_residue, journal or Git effect coordinates before continuing. A missing response cannot establish which phases ran. inspect-release-preparations reads the exact preparation selection; recovery explains interrupted custody. Do not regenerate the request with new IDs to hide uncertain effects.
Closed candidates
Omit selection to include all non-draft content and its required retained assets. Gazette derives one complete selection from the captured corpus before checking or rendering it. Preparation uses this default even when no candidate checker is selected. Ordinary local previews retain their configured draft policy.
To override that default, supply complete content and assets decision maps over the captured corpus. Each decision is include or exclude; asset keys use the captured logical path. For example, a corpus containing exactly one page and no assets can select:
{"content":{"content:notes":"include"},"assets":{}}

That override is complete only for that corpus. Missing, extra or conflicting decisions, included drafts and relationships to excluded required endpoints refuse the candidate. Selecting content does not approve its release. The retained review inventory provides the source surfaces to review; the compiler checks candidate closure before rendering. Preview output and unfiltered local inspection remain separate from a preparation candidate.
Reviewing and confirming
Open gazette release-session before requesting approval. The returned readiness names the actual held journal generation; keep that session open through registration, consumption and dispatch. The CLI accepts one JSON operation per line. MCP exposes the same operations through operate_release_session; discover its schema for the complete field and limit definitions.
The open request’s optional reviewed selection contains workspace, optional sites, credentials, allow_read and supplied-document limits. The workspace uses the same supplied or local shape as preparation. Local configuration capture requires allow_read: true. Omitting sites selects the workspace’s configured build set; an explicit ordered set is fixed for the lifetime, never reduced to the sites that succeeded. Every selected site must be deployable and have a destination. Each distinct publisher needs one credential selection: {publisher, owner, credential: {helper, allow_credentials}}. The helper is an absolute executable path, with separate permission to invoke it for HTTPS. The owner label records the operator’s selection; it does not establish provider-account membership. The ordinary git selection supplies the executable and isolation directory with credentials: null; reviewed operations route each target through its own publisher’s credential.
Send review with the actual expected header and an input containing a new record_id, a one-use nonce, explicit approved_at time and the complete preparation selections. Its options supply the existing native preparation and bounded JSON verification limits. Gazette inspects the whole native set, checks its destinations against the held workspace, derives publisher coverage from the site declarations, and returns a Reviewed result containing approval. This operation neither records approval nor contacts a destination.
The publisher reviews the generated output and the complete returned approval. Its canonical_body_sha256 covers every field except the digest itself: the held journal, ordered sites and targets, prepared output and evidence, publisher coverage, credential owners/helpers and review time. A changed output, destination, owner or set requires a new review and confirmation.
For register_reviewed, consume_reviewed and dispatch_reviewed, retain the original approval JSON as input.approval, supply the separately confirmed digest as input.confirmed_sha256, a current input.observed_at, and the original full input.selections. A document’s own digest does not provide confirmation. Gazette independently reconstructs native target expectations and compares the document with the workspace publisher scopes selected when the session opened. These operations require their existing separate registration, lease, consumption, read and dispatch permissions. No signing key or authority command is needed.
Optional signed authorization
The authorization is a JSON record, WebsiteReleaseBatchAuthorizationV1, that names the journal, its generation, the ordered targets and the evidence digests of the prepared set. For each target it names the domain, remote, branch, the single refspec, the commit to push, the output digest and the commit the remote is expected to hold now, or that the branch does not exist yet.
Each publisher signs the SHA-256 digest of the record's RFC 8785 canonical form, without its signatures, prefixed by the domain WEBSITE_RELEASE_BATCH_AUTHORIZATION_V1 and a zero byte, using Ed25519. Every target is covered by exactly one publisher. Decoding is strict: unknown, duplicate or missing fields, decimals, forced pushes, deletions and wildcard refspecs are all refused. gazette verify-release-authorization checks signatures and bindings alone; gazette verify-prepared-authorization also checks them against the local preparations. The exact authorization and binding fields are defined by the native release declarations. The verifier accepts their original JSON strings; its MCP schema describes that wrapper, not a generated authorization schema. See supplied verification. gazette schema covers declaration contracts only, as listed in the Theme reference.
Open the release session and acquire its writer before asking for signatures, because the authorization is signed for the generation the writer holds. Keep the same session for register, consume and dispatch.
Pushing
Consuming reviewed approval rechecks the confirmed digest, workspace scopes and complete native preparations, observes every destination through its selected credential, and compares it with the approved pre-state. The signed mode additionally checks signatures and refreshes publisher keys through its configured authority command. If any target has moved, the whole batch is refused. Otherwise one intent per target is recorded in a single transaction, and the authorization can never be consumed again.
Each dispatch records its start before Git runs, then pushes one exact, non-forced refspec, fenced on the approved pre-state. File and HTTPS remotes are supported; SSH is not. An HTTPS credential comes only from one explicitly named credential helper, with TLS verification on and no redirects. A timeout or a lost response leaves the attempt uncertain. A retry is allowed only after a completed rejection or a refusal before any effect, with the exact pre-state observed again and approval rechecked; signed mode also refreshes its authority.
Reading back and settling
Read-back asks each destination which commit its branch holds, and settlement compares that with the original approved intent. A release is succeeded when every target holds its intended commit, failed with no effect when every target still holds its pre-state and nothing was ever uncertain, partially terminal when some targets succeeded and the rest conclusively conflict, and otherwise needs reconciliation. A terminal settlement closes the release for good. A GitHub Pages build or a served page is a separate observation (gazette observe-github-pages-build, gazette observe-delivery); neither settles a release.
When the outcome stays uncertain, reconcile from what the remote holds and stop if that does not settle it. Never push again on a guess. Interrupted releases are handled through gazette recovery-session (recovery). A reviewed recovery can select the same independent workspace scopes and owner credentials through its optional reviewed field. This supplies destination-read routing only; recovery has no registration, consumption or dispatch operation. Original records and missing results remain unchanged.
Where the history lives
Every step is recorded in the SQLite journal described in store, and each has an inspect-release-* command that reads its history without contacting a destination or revalidating a signature. The policy check a release relies on is described in policy checks.

Prepare inputs for the renderer
Bind authored content, Markdown and static files so the renderer reads the files you intend it to use.
Declare content and project files
Use the workspace format, with a selected Theme and explicitly pinned sources. The brand publication selects its authored input:
# These tables extend a complete workspace declaring site:one, its publisher,
# source:content and a selected Theme source.
[[brands]]
id = "brand:one"
name = "Example Publication"
[[brands.publications]]
site = "site:one"
public_base_url = "https://example.test/mount/"
authored = [{ source = "source:content", target = "authored/one" }]

The logical corpus prefix distinguishes source ownership. It is not a public URL or a second repository path. Every configured authored source and enabled project documentation source is captured so cross-site references resolve against the actual complete declaration. Only the selected site's pages are emitted. Each object's explicit home must agree with its configured source owner; a cross-site relationship does not relocate it.
Destination-bearing page, navigation, search and graph records also carry the home site's optional presentation identity: its already-resolved Theme package and optional palette. A crossing therefore has enough information to present a different publication world without guessing from its domain or copying the foreign object. Absence stays absent when that site selected no Theme. This projection is deliberately narrower than the site's full composition: it does not expose capability bindings, provider or plugin state, logical-resource selection, selection origin, package capture readiness or publication approval.
Project-native authored documentation uses the existing placement binding:
# project:library and source:library-docs must be explicitly declared.
[[placements]]
role = 'primary'
site = "site:one"
project = "project:library"
render = true
discoverable = false
documents = { source = "source:library-docs", target = "native/library" }

These retained documents enter the same corpus, graph, route compiler and Theme as publication-authored content. The current strict frontmatter profile below applies to framed documents in either source role. A separate explicit native Markdown profile can supply structural defaults for unframed project documents, as described below. Neither path invents collections, authors or direct about/mentions from a project's placement. render = false excludes that placement from capture and output; it is not a failed optional copy. Discovery selection does not suppress this private draft-inclusive rendering or grant public admission. Generated API references and their brand-owned documentation_repository remain a separate documentation-target path.
The shared page model includes provenance.site and, for project-source input, provenance.project. These identify the configured source relationship, not semantic subject matter. Native source keys, repository paths, pins and file paths are not included in that template/JSON projection; exact acquisition and per-page source evidence retain their private association.
Choose what appears in discovery
The compiler resolves discoverable once from each exact content source binding. Publication-authored input is discoverable; rendered project documentation uses its placement's literal flag. Project lifecycle, visibility, availability and about/mentions are not substitutes for that setting. An unbound or wrong-site source fails this emitted selection instead of inheriting a default.
All selected pages, aliases, resources and static assets still materialize. Missing required input remains a failure even when its placement is undiscoverable. The flag instead controls automatic page listings, search, feeds, sitemap, site JSON-LD, graph endpoints and generated navigation. The site asset catalog uses the same source flag without dropping the actual asset files. A site may therefore render pages while having an empty automatic discovery set. Curated llms.txt references must also be discoverable; an ineligible configured reference fails rather than silently disappearing. Markdown alternates instead follow canonical materialization, including undiscoverable rendered pages.
Direct pages retain their own authored declaration, journey steps and body links. Discoverability is not privacy: explicit prose may still link to an unlisted page. Generated breadcrumbs or journey recommendations with ineligible endpoints are omitted whole, never spliced into a different ancestry or neighbor sequence. Aggregate page/graph views borrow eligible scalar metadata instead of expanding raw container-member lists. Eligible journey edges keep original positions; project assertions whose evidence includes an ineligible endpoint are omitted whole, not rewritten as a reduced assertion. Independently referenced projects remain valid project facts, even if one documentation placement is undiscoverable.
Private compiler inspection still exposes the complete canonical structure. The emitted views do not mutate that graph, reparse bodies, grant public admission or certify artifacts. Their bytes and the configured flag enter the existing output inventory and exact policy-check input identity.
Explicit content attributions bind author and rights-holder keys against the same workspace principal catalog. The ordered attributions view supplies the exact declared roles to Theme and local JSON. It does not include an unrelated global author list, infer a byline from site.publisher, or convert a declaration into identity/rights approval.
Templates can embed supplied structured values in HTML data blocks using the adapter's JSON script encoding, for example <script type="application/json">{{ content | json_script }}</script>. The same page metadata remains the source; the filter does not reconstruct it. The resulting data remains local and unadmitted. Selected JSON-LD comes from the compiler's borrowed page projection; the filter only encodes that supplied value for script-element text.
An authored Markdown file in the selected capture can contain:
+++
[content]
id = "article:introduction"
site = "site:one"
title = "Keep the observation with its context"
description = "Record what happened while the details that explain it are still available."
lifecycle = "draft"
route = { path = "/introduction/", aliases = ["/start/"] }
[content.structure]
kind = "page"
family = { kind = "article" }
+++
# Keep the observation with its context

Write what you noticed before deciding what it means. Include the place,
conditions and any detail that could change your interpretation when you return
to the note.

Keep the original measurement, sketch or quotation beside the explanation
instead of replacing it with a confident conclusion.

The fences above are literal +++ lines in a Markdown file. See the content model for collections, contained journeys, typed project relations, keywords and article-owned notes, and page resources for bundle companions and their explicit compilation limits. These structural and rendering contracts do not establish public admission or publisher approval.
Generated taxonomy navigation
The brand publication can select index and term pages using exact catalog keys, routes and retained Theme templates. These are generated navigation, not new authored objects or a second taxonomy catalog:
# Append to the selected brands.publications table. The catalog must already
# declare taxonomy:topic and term:systems.
[[brands.publications.taxonomy_pages]]
taxonomy = "taxonomy:topic"
route = "/topics/"
template = "root/taxonomy.html"

[[brands.publications.taxonomy_pages]]
taxonomy = "taxonomy:topic"
term = "term:systems"
route = "/topics/systems/"
template = "root/taxonomy.html"

An index groups only classified, discoverable pages from that site's selected corpus. A term page selects that exact term; an explicitly selected empty term page remains empty. Foreign pages and undiscoverable sources are not pulled into the listing. Labels never become identity joins or inferred slugs. A term link exists only when its route is explicitly configured.
The template receives taxonomy, optional term, title, canonical_url, output, groups and the shared typed presentation envelope. Each group carries its exact term, optional canonical_url and member pages with id, title, canonical_url and optional language. The same value enters taxonomy_pages in the site model. Selected JSON-LD adds the compiler's CollectionPage view to this value and site.jsonld; the sitemap uses the same configured listing URLs. Selected Markdown alternates also cover these generated views. They do not automatically enter curated llms.txt, whose entries name selected content identities. These pages do not manufacture content lifecycle, authorship, feed entries or publisher permission. Their paths share the ordinary output collision checks. Template and output digests remain private render evidence.
The presentation envelope has the same shape used by page, alias, taxonomy, graph and mirror rendering. Its closed surface.kind is respectively page, alias, taxonomy, graph or mirror; Themes need not infer this from payload fields or template names. The envelope also carries the effective Theme and palette, that selection's CSS-validated light/dark browser_theme_colors, typed workspace chrome, frozen capability outcomes, compiled Theme resources, the site resource/module inventory and applicable interaction/search bindings. Search's optional no_script_destination is the already-resolved page and canonical route, not renderer-authored HTML. Values remain contextual: authored pages retain their exact page resource closure, while generated site surfaces receive the stable site-level inventory. This presentation transport does not activate a plugin, select a provider or resource, change inheritance origin, or add facts to the taxonomy payload.
Publish plain project Markdown
Add this field to the owning [[placements]] table when its pinned documentation source contains ordinary Markdown without publication frontmatter:
native_markdown = { route_prefix = "/docs/library/", lifecycle = "published" }

Both fields are required. route_prefix is an explicit directory route, ending in /, beneath the site's configured public base. lifecycle selects a content state (draft, published or archived); even published here grants no public admission or release authority. The profile requires a documents binding and does not enable a disabled placement. Publication-authored inputs do not use it.
The compiler keeps native bytes and their parsed body unchanged and derives a documentation node:
Home site and project provenance come from the placement. No author, subject, collection, journey or rights claim is added.
Identity is native-document:<sha256> over a versioned coordinate containing the project key, source key and literal capture-relative entry. Body/title edits, changed commit or checkout location, site changes, mounts and logical prefixes do not change it. Renaming the native entry or changing either key does. Mirrors and identity migration are not implemented by this coordinate rule.
Title is the first nonempty H1's parsed text, otherwise the literal filename stem. derivation.title records kind = "heading" with the original heading byte span, or kind = "filename". This is derived metadata, not an authored field.
README.md and index.md map to their parent directory beneath the prefix; other Markdown files map to a directory named by their stem. Matching these two index stems and Markdown extensions is ASCII case-insensitive. With the example prefix, nested/README.md becomes /docs/library/nested/ and nested/guide.md becomes /docs/library/nested/guide/.
Native path components are encoded through the shared route codec. Spaces and Unicode are preserved; unsupported literal percent signs, query/fragment markers and unsafe paths fail rather than changing identity. README.md and index.md in the same directory conflict: the compiler never silently chooses one.
Framed TOML documents retain their explicit IDs, metadata and routes; the native profile never overwrites them or rescues malformed metadata. An unsupported YAML or ambiguous --- opening fails, preventing a draft/privacy declaration from being discarded as body text. Without the profile, unframed documents still fail structural lowering.
Source-relative documentation links
Within project-bound documents, actual Markdown .md/.markdown links resolve relative to the referring native entry, inside the same configured source, to the target object's compiled canonical URL. This works between plain and framed documents, preserves query suffixes and does not rewrite inline/fenced code examples. It uses the retained AST, not regular-expression replacement or a second source read.
Missing targets, traversal beyond the selected source and invalid encoded paths fail explicitly. Fragments such as guide.md#section resolve against the retained target's exact heading/footnote index. Same-document #section references work in both authored and native documents; native ./#section uses that same index and emits a suffix-only #section so file-shaped routes do not navigate to a different parent page. The same normalization preserves a supplied query suffix. Malformed percent escapes, invalid UTF-8 and missing anchors fail before output. Fragment lookup decodes once while emitted links retain the original encoded suffix and query spelling. Empty fragments remain valid; no implicit top heading is invented. External and root-relative URLs retain their spelling; this is not proof of destination validity. Static references use the shared source coordinate described below. Other code-file URLs and repository-platform URL generation remain separate work. Publication-authored document links do not adopt the native Markdown-to-route grammar.
Static assets from configured sources
Each authored or project-document ContentBinding can explicitly select a static destination alongside its existing source and logical target:
authored = [{ source = "source:articles", target = "articles", static_assets = { route_prefix = "/media/articles/" } }]

The same optional static_assets field is valid inside placements.documents. Its route must end in /. Every supported opaque file in that configured source is transported beneath this prefix with its source-relative filename, including unreferenced files. No page slug, output route, template or adapter invents a second destination. The site's configured public base supplies the domain and mount prefix; the output path remains site-relative.
The current transport suffixes are png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, pdf, bib, txt, csv, zip, mp4, webm and vtt, case-insensitively. This selects byte-preserving local transport, not MIME/payload validation, image transformation, rights, disclosure approval or safe public hosting. SVG, HTML, scripts, styles, notebooks and other unsupported inputs remain explicit uncompiled obligations. Video transport preserves the original clip without transcoding. WebVTT captions are transported unchanged and served as text/vtt; charset=utf-8; this does not validate caption timing or content. Preview serves MP4 as video/mp4 and WebM as video/webm, with bounded single-byte-range support. This does not decode the video or certify container metadata: strict output qualification still refuses these video files until an explicit supported video inspection profile exists.
Selecting a capability still requires its real compiler; placing its source beside a static image does not bypass that requirement.
Actual Markdown images and links to supported static suffixes resolve relative to the referring authored or native document, confined to its exact source. They must identify an entry in the selected site's retained asset plan. Missing or uncompiled targets, invalid percent encoding, encoded traversal/separators, empty components and escaping .. fail before output. Literal Unicode and spaces produce encoded URLs and literal output filenames using the existing route codec. Literal %, ? and # in source filenames remain unsupported. Queries and fragments are preserved, but anchors inside opaque assets are not validated. Code examples are never rewritten. Links/images nested inside image alt text remain label text, not emitted references or page asset dependencies; syntax inspection still records them and the original safety gate still applies. External and root-relative destinations are neither fetched nor checked by this resolver. Email autolinks retain their mailto: destination; an address ending in a supported asset suffix is not a source-relative download.
One cached AssetPlan per site supplies the Markdown mapping and output writer. The page's assets array contains its referenced records, deduplicated in URL order; the site model's assets object contains all planned records keyed by URL. Each record carries url, literal output, sha256, byte count and site/project provenance. Tera and JSON receive the same records. Logical input paths and source digests are retained separately in private asset evidence. Native source is not reopened, and wall-clock or remote observations do not enter asset identity.
Assets use the same output inventory, collision checks and file/directory/byte budgets as pages, aliases and the model artifact. A failed plan or collision returns no complete site. Per-site plan record/text ceilings reuse the configured content limits independently of the content graph; foreign assets do not consume that site's plan budget. Unbound opaque files remain unresolved obligations, not an inferred source or silently omitted file.

Inspect a local build
Read the output inventory from a local render, review the page model before templating or scan generated files for private values.
If you want to…	Use	
Render one site and inspect its inventory	Execute and inspect	
Read content and relationships without rendering	Inspect semantics	
Build a private registry for tooling	Project the complete private registry	
Review page bodies before templating or attach a response	Review pages before running the Theme and match a review response	
Check for strings that should stay private	Output disclosure	
Execute and inspect
For a single site, the direct command reads the complete workspace TOML from stdin. Use the site-set recipe when the workspace has includes or several sites must share a model:
gazette render-site --local --site site:one \
  --model-output machine/model.json < workspace.toml

Without --output-parent, Gazette reads sources and compiles in memory, with any explicitly permitted native generation. It returns private source/render evidence and the complete output inventory. --local is mandatory; draft and archived objects are not silently filtered, and site deployability is not publication permission.
Add --output-parent /absolute/existing/private/stages to create and retain a fresh private child. It never replaces an existing tree. The stage writer checks separation from every consumed native repository, writes the whole tree and verifies read-back before retention. The returned directory is the actual retained location; inspect it before retrying if receipt delivery fails. No deployment, signature, Git commit/push, database initialization or migration occurs.
Keep acquisition, syntax and resolved state
Rust callers can keep each phase: build::acquire_publication → AcquiredInputs::parse_publication → ParsedPublication::resolve → build::render_resolved_publication → optional build::stage_publication and explicit native-guard retain. ParsedPublication owns the corpus and borrows the acquisition that supplied its bytes; it cannot be paired with a different workspace. ResolvedPublication borrows that syntax and holds the validated semantic model. It can be inspected or rendered without reparsing content, re-resolving its graph or reopening native sources. Presentation validation and compilation run when rendering is requested.
The convenience build::render_publication uses this same parse/resolve/render path. CLI code contains neither semantic compilation nor staging rules. Captures can be reused after native files change without changing their retained bytes; a new acquisition must verify the newly observed source. These retained phases do not implement admission or discoverability filtering.
Inspect semantics without rendering
Check the retained publication semantics without rendering:
gazette check --stdin --publication site:one < workspace.toml

This captures the configured publication sources and selected presentation inputs, then parses the publication corpus, resolves its complete graph/routes/references and validates source-to-publication homes. Presentation bytes are captured and pin-checked, but this command does not validate presentation manifests, compile templates or resources, render bodies or create a stage. A valid semantic report can therefore precede a presentation or rendering failure. No native writes occur.
The resolved-unadmitted report includes the complete graph and private acquisition evidence, including drafts and unlisted/private values. It is operator evidence, not public output, a policy verdict or certification. Source acquisition and semantic failures still reject the operation; the command does not silently return a successful subset.
Project the complete private registry
For the complete private registry projection of those same resolved inputs:
gazette check --stdin --publication site:one --registry < workspace.toml

--registry is mutually exclusive with --review. Rust callers use ResolvedPublication::registry(RegistryLimits). This prepares typed catalogs, site/brand/publisher links, placements, the existing content graph, compiled routes/aliases and exact source associations. The consuming site does not filter this view: foreign sites, unused catalogs, disabled placements, drafts and archived content remain represented. Empty content still retains configured sites and catalogs. This is private structural evidence, not a persisted registry head, public admission or a store connection.
The gazette.registry/v1 report remains resolved-unadmitted. semantic_sha256 identifies the normalized structural model, using deterministic typed JSON field order and sorted collections. It is not a full build identity: body/asset bytes, presentation, native paths, source pins and operational state are excluded. Exact original workspace and full-document bytes have separate configuration_sha256 and documents evidence. No native input is reopened during projection. The digest is not a release signature or authorization format.
--max-registry-bytes requires --registry and bounds the complete compact JSON report, including its exact-input evidence (default 16 MiB). Pretty-print display whitespace is outside that limit. Exhaustion returns no successful subset or partial check report. Acquisition, corpus and graph limits apply independently.
Persistence is a separate effect, not another mode of check. The SDK's build::reconcile_registry consumes this retained publication; the CLI's reconcile-registry ROOT --site site:one acquires and resolves the same inputs before invoking it. Complete registry replacement and writer-generation advance require separate explicit permissions. inspect-registry PATH observes the stored rows without reconciliation or migration. See the exact flags and store guide. Neither operation turns this local unadmitted model into approved public output.
Review pages before running the Theme
Run this to inspect the page model and Markdown bodies before the Theme runs:
gazette check --stdin --publication site:one --review < workspace.toml

The result includes Markdown body fragments, the site graph, local page contexts, drafts, nested foreign references, every configured static file, effective composition and paths of uncompiled opaque inputs. A broken body reference can fail this step even when structural checks pass. Static file descriptors identify bytes without checking binary safety. This command does not run Theme or resource programs or write output. To inspect the final HTML or other files, render the site and scan its output.
Mathematical sources also need complete source-bound typesetting results. Reuse the math.results object from an explicitly authorized native render; review does not execute the typesetter. For a local workspace, extract that object and supply it on standard input:
python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.dump(json.load(sys.stdin)["math"]["results"],sys.stdout)' \
  < authorized-render.json > retained-math.json
gazette check --workspace-root "$WORKSPACE" --publication site:one --review \
  --retained-math-stdin < retained-math.json

Keep the complete result map for the captured corpus, including its original logical paths. The existing ParsedPublication::with_math admission checks the current body digests, profiles and every formula occurrence; the formatter checks emitted MathML. Extra, missing or stale results fail. Omitting required results returns publication_review_math_required. --retained-math-stdin requires --workspace-root and --review, and bounds its complete JSON input by --max-review-bytes (16 MiB by default), independently of review output. This supplied data is not an attestation of its producer or permission to publish.
The report contains sha256 and request. The latter's gazette-publication-review/1 format binds the selected site, exact configuration digest, captured source-tree identities and ordered typed surfaces. Its selection_sha256 is null for this unselected inventory; the selected Rust review instead binds full candidate intent. sha256 hashes compact request JSON, not the outer report. This is an Engine-owned inspection encoding, not a publication policy or release authorization format. Configuration comments and machine paths affect this exact request identity; do not use it as the portable identity of rendered artifacts. Neither digest equality nor a successful inventory is an owner approval. Keep the report private.
Rust callers use build::review(&resolved, ReviewLimits) with the SDK's native adapters, or ResolvedPublication::review with explicit raster/Markdown adapters; request().surfaces() exposes immutable values from the shared projections. Each surface's uses() iterator gives every scalar/container occurrence with an RFC 6901 pointer. The same subject appearing on a page and in the site graph has different use contexts, and an allowed page must not conceal a held nested value. --max-review-bytes bounds compact request JSON and, independently, aggregate pointer bytes (default 16 MiB); --max-review-uses bounds all occurrences (default 100,000). Both flags require --review. Exhaustion returns no partial request. Later admission and immutable-output review must still account for compiled resources, rendered Theme text and disclosure across the output tree.
Match a review response
Rust integrations can compare a response with that retained request using PublicationReview::match_response(bytes, &ReviewResponseBinding, ReviewResponseLimits). The binding supplies the expected ReviewPolicy (id, revision, source_sha256) and response_sha256 independently of the bytes being checked. Deriving the expectations from the same response supplies no independent proof. This operation performs no I/O, policy execution or clock reads; there is not yet a CLI response-import command.
The strict gazette-review-response/1 JSON transport contains format, request_sha256, policy and decisions. Each decision has a zero-based surface index in the exact request, its canonical pointer, an outcome (allow, hold or exclude) and a nonempty list of unique policy-native evidence keys. Every occurrence, including each root and nested container, needs exactly one row. Parent decisions, wildcard/prefix paths and normalized array indexes cannot stand in for missing children. Reported order is preserved; changing whitespace or row order changes the response-byte pin. Unknown or duplicate JSON fields, positional root/policy/decision arrays, object-form outcomes, unsupported format, mismatched pins/policy, missing/extra uses and invalid evidence references reject the complete match.
ReviewResponseLimits defaults to 16 MiB of raw input and 100,000 decoded decisions. The byte bound applies before hashing/decoding; the record bound applies before coverage matching. A successful result remains matched-unverified, including when every outcome is allow. Evidence keys are references, not verified records; the match does not authenticate the evaluator, evaluate freshness/revocation, approve rights or certify disclosure. An exclude row does not authorize silently deleting content, and a held child is not overridden by an allowed container. No renderer or release operation accepts this result as approval. The owned result retains the original response_json and request digest after the source request is dropped. Keep it private. The local preparation recipe can carry complete per-site responses through candidate checking, immutable output checking and durable read-back; the ordinary unguarded local-render recipe refuses response input.
Which failures stop a render
Missing routes, missing alias selection, output collisions, parser/template errors and resource ceilings return no successful partial tree. Output options bound entries, depth, per-file and aggregate bytes. Input acquisition currently uses 256 source keys and the native source defaults. PublicationRenderLimits separates corpus and graph limits from PublicationOutputLimits, which bounds subsequent presentation metadata, template rendering, resource compilation and capability metadata. Rendering an existing ResolvedPublication accepts only those post-resolution limits; it does not rerun semantic resolution under different limits. Native output inventory ceilings remain in SiteRenderOptions. Rust callers can choose these limits explicitly; they are not a CPU or hostile-template sandbox.
Supported scope and limits:
Capability degradation remains a closed, typed choice. Only the documented no-native-acquisition outcome can produce typed unavailable; execution failure, stale evidence and unsupported selected input still fail the site.
Opaque files become output only through an explicit supported static-asset or resource selection. Other sites' retained assets remain evidence, not this site's output obligation, and unsupported selected input fails rather than being copied or omitted.
Unframed Markdown still requires the explicit project profile. YAML metadata, unrestricted raw HTML, active notebook HTML/widgets and implicit executable or asset discovery remain unsupported by this profile. Typed resource recipes, bounded raster transformations, static notebooks and explicit route mirrors use their separately documented paths instead of weakening Markdown admission.
Candidate admission, technical qualification, disclosure checks, durable local preparation and release/recovery are connected successor phases. They do not authenticate owner rights/privacy evidence, grant publisher approval or prove a hosted-platform build; those authorities remain external to local rendering.
Scan the output for private values
          
Use Output disclosure checks to scan generated files for private values, or require supported formats before preparing a release.
