Save the manifest digest separately
backup-store uses SQLite's online backup API for a consistent copy. It reopens the copy read-only, checks its integrity and writes backup.json next to store.sqlite. Save the reported manifest digest outside the backup.
Verify the copy
verify-backup uses that digest to check the manifest, then checks the database. A backup has exactly two files. Symbolic links or extra files cause verification to fail. A failed backup remains in its original directory, marked unverified. Use a new directory for another attempt.
Restoring
gazette prepare-store-restore verifies the backup and copies it to a fresh directory with restore.json. The live journal stays in place. To switch journals, run gazette adopt-store-restore with the latest clean anchor state and the original restore record. Every release in the old journal must be settled first. Adoption creates a successor and leaves the old journal untouched.
Limits
Defaults are 256 MiB for the backup database, 16 KiB for an output directory path and 256 KiB for a command report. Run the command with --help to see its limits. When a report cannot be delivered, Gazette returns the information needed to inspect the result: the initialized header, backup manifest digest or restore record digest.
See recovery for interrupted operations and releasing for the release history.

Write Theme templates with Tera Write the HTML templates for a Theme package. Gazette uses Tera 1.20.1 and passes each template the resolved title, body, routes, navigation and presentation settings. Read those values from the template context so that links and page metadata agree with search, feeds and the rest of the site. Render a page Set the Theme manifest's render.page to your entry file, for example page.html. That path is relative to the Theme's declared template directory. A minimal page template is: {{ content.title }}
{{ body_html | safe }}
content.title and route.canonical_url receive HTML escaping. body_html is the compiler's rendered Markdown fragment; safe lets that fragment remain markup. Render it once. Do not apply safe to arbitrary authored strings. Use the Theme contract for the complete manifest and context fields. Its virtual namespace describes how to address inherited templates, includes and macros across Theme packages. The local rendering guide connects that Theme to a publication. Escape data for each output format Tera's default .html, .htm and .xml suffix-based escaping is preserved. Other suffixes are not automatically escaped. The trusted template's safe filter deliberately bypasses escaping; already-rendered Markdown must only receive that treatment through the admitted presentation contract. This is not an HTML sanitizer, a URL-policy validator or JavaScript/CSS context-aware encoding. Machine formats require their own typed serializers rather than assuming HTML escaping makes arbitrary JSON or scripts safe. JSON script data Use json_script on a supplied JSON value when embedding it as the text of an HTML JSON data block: It serializes the value once using serde_json, with JSON Unicode escapes for <, >, &, apostrophes and the Unicode line/paragraph separators. Keys and nested values receive the same treatment. JSON decoding recovers the original value, including quotes, backslashes, control characters and Unicode. It does not HTML-entity-encode the data, accept a pre-serialized string as raw JSON, or replace only one spelling of a closing script tag. Tera treats the encoded result as safe for this position; no additional safe filter is needed. This is script-element text encoding only, not an attribute, URL, CSS or arbitrary JavaScript-program encoder. It creates neither the element nor its attributes. It takes no arguments and cannot fetch data or change its meaning. Use a separately resolved JSON-LD value with application/ld+json; changing a data block's MIME type does not make ordinary publication JSON into JSON-LD. The compiler still owns vocabulary, identity and relationship projection. The expanded JSON buffer is bounded by the configured rendered-output byte ceiling before returning it to Tera. The complete rendered page is independently subject to that same ceiling, including markup and repeated blocks. Overflow is a failed render, not truncated JSON or a successful partial artifact. This does not make Tera's other filters or arbitrary template expressions allocation-bounded. The encoding addresses the HTML script-state restrictions described in JSON-LD 1.1 §7.2. CSS URLs in style-element text Use {{ resolved_url | css_url }} where a trusted template needs one complete quoted CSS url("...") token in a style element's raw text. The value must be a string; no arguments are accepted. The encoder escapes CSS quotes, backslashes, control characters and HTML raw-text delimiters with terminated CSS hexadecimal escapes. CSS decoding recovers the supplied string, including existing percent escapes, query separators and Unicode. NUL refuses because CSS replaces both its literal and escaped forms instead of preserving it. The encoded result bypasses HTML autoescaping only for this position. Do not add safe, wrap it in another url(), or use it in HTML attributes, scripts, selectors or arbitrary CSS expressions. The filter does not infer its context, validate URL schemes, select resources, build paths or fetch anything. Native resolved resource/asset URLs remain the source of addresses; geometry and preference rules remain the Theme's responsibility. Intermediate encoding uses the same configured output-byte ceiling as json_script, including the wrapper and escape expansion. Hidden assigned results cannot evade that ceiling, and the complete output independently charges repeated calls and markup. A refusal returns no successful partial artifact. The adapter remains a trusted-template renderer, not a context-aware sanitizer. Query values Use url_query for one value inside a query string. Keep the destination and parameter name explicit: Search For query = "notes & figures", the value becomes notes%20%26%20figures. url_query accepts one supplied string and no arguments, percent-encoding its UTF-8 bytes as one RFC 3986 query value. Only ASCII letters, digits and -._~ remain literal; spaces are %20, never query separators. The filter does not construct, validate or resolve a destination URL, and it does not disable HTML escaping. Expansion shares the adapter output-byte ceiling; non-string inputs and over-limit output fail without a prefix. Metadata in Markdown documents Use markdown_text for literal titles and purposes in Theme-owned Markdown text, and markdown_destination inside an inline link destination: - [{{ page.title | markdown_text }}]({{ page.url | markdown_destination }}): {{ page.description | markdown_text }} Both accept strings only and no arguments. The text encoder collapses whitespace to a single line and escapes Markdown delimiters so metadata cannot create headings, links, HTML or additional entries. Commas, sentence periods, apostrophes, parentheses and hyphens within words stay readable: science-fiction, for example. remains unchanged. Leading list markers and entity-looking text remain literal. The destination encoder escapes link delimiters and percent-encodes whitespace, angle brackets, quotes and backslashes while preserving existing percent escapes. Control-bearing destinations refuse. These are explicit Markdown encoders, not HTML/script/CSS encoders or URL resolvers. Use them in a non-HTML template such as llms.txt; they do not bypass HTML suffix autoescaping. Intermediate expansion and whole rendered output share the existing byte ceiling, including hidden assigned results. Editorial dates Use {{ content.published | editorial_date(format="%-d %B %Y") }} to show a supplied date as 19 November 2026. Keep the original value in the attribute. The optional format string uses Chrono's strftime directives and defaults to %-d %B %Y; the workspace can supply another presentation format through Theme copy. The filter accepts Gazette's calendar-date or explicit-offset timestamp strings. It keeps the authored day and offset, including timestamps near midnight, and never consults the clock or converts to a local timezone. Formatting a date-only value with time or offset fields fails rather than inventing them. Invalid dates, unsupported formats, non-string inputs and unknown arguments also fail. Output retains normal HTML escaping and shares the rendered-output byte ceiling, including a result assigned to a hidden variable. It does not choose a publication label or change lifecycle. Missing and null values The pinned Tera default filter treats an explicitly supplied JSON null and an absent value alike: both resolve to the filter's declared fallback. A Theme that needs to distinguish those states must consume a separate typed presence field; it must not rely on default to retain explicit null. Adapter and constraints This section is for maintainers extending the template adapter. Template authors also need to observe these execution restrictions. gazette-adapter-tera is a presentation adapter, not a second publication compiler. Its Compiler implements the inward TemplateCompiler port over a verified, borrowed TreeInput; the existing TemplateSet::compile convenience entry accepts a CapturedSource. Both use the same compilation implementation. The input contains only selected template files and their directory entries. Every regular file is parsed; no suffix filter, filesystem glob, Theme discovery or SQL query occurs. The set retains the input tree identity. Its render operation takes an exact EntryPath and a serialized object supplied by the application, returning complete UTF-8 bytes or an error. It does not write files. The application owns source selection, typed semantic-to-context projection and admission. Theme owns trusted presentation programs. The adapter owns Tera parsing, inheritance, includes, macros, escaping and bounded output. It never guesses an author, publisher, route, capability, collection or journey. Context data cannot register a callback or expose the filesystem. Tera is pinned to 1.20.1. Its dependency manifest declares Rust 1.85, compatible with Gazette's 1.94 toolchain. Default features, date-locale and preserve-order extensions are not enabled by this adapter, and moving to Tera 2 is a separate decision. The dependency is MIT-licensed. Gazette exposes no template loading or callback surface of its own. Ambient get_env, clock/random functions and allocating range are unavailable, including if another workspace member later unifies Tera features. Calls fail with native adapter errors rather than substitute values. The application should supply bounded collections instead. Caller-provided callbacks are not exposed. The adapter's encoding filters and editorial_date formatter operate only on supplied values; any other helper a Theme needs arrives as explicit context data, never as a callback. Limits cover the template inventory, each file, aggregate source bytes, path depth, serialized context bytes and emitted bytes. The separate execution_depth defaults to 64 and admits only values from 1 to 64. It counts template calls and nested AST containers/expressions together, rather than borrowing source path depth or allowing two independently deep call and expression chains. The output writer stops before exceeding its ceiling; a failed render discards its accumulated output. How Gazette checks template execution Before rendering, the adapter checks the native parsed AST for recursive inheritance, macro loading and reachable include/macro/block execution. The iterative loader preserves Tera's import order, cache publication before parent loading and inherited namespaces. Execution admission retains the original entry, active template and block lookup owner; an include selects only its first existing fallback. Uncalled macro definitions remain inert. Literal Boolean branches retain their native reachability; other branches and possible returned block-stack states are conservatively joined. A possible cycle or excessive combined depth is refused, so admission can reject a program whose safe execution depends on correlations it does not prove. Native inheritance and macro-file checks remain active over the same parsed templates. Bodies proved free of template calls, includes and block operations share one unchanged exact depth graph across incoming loader-cache and block-top states. The analysis restores each caller's incoming state when that body returns. This avoids copying a pure attribute helper's AST analysis for every conditional include combination; bodies with any possible template effect retain the full state-sensitive path. The proof is conservative and memoized by retained AST identity. Fixed storage/work ceilings, complete longest-path depth and cycle checks remain unchanged. The v6 admission profile reuses effect-free helper closures across loader states that differ only by empty namespace entries. The complete nonempty namespace maps and active block lookup owner remain part of the analysis, and transitive purity requires every possible same-named definition to avoid loader/block effects. Recursive closures are not purity proofs. Discarded equivalent loader-cache clones release their temporary storage charge; cumulative work, execution-depth, recursion and whole-output limits are unchanged. This keeps ordinary shared helpers composable without admitting a wider set of stateful or recursive execution paths. Native macro/function/filter argument maps can evaluate supplied expressions in a different order after an independent parse. When such a map evaluates more than one supplied expression, admission requires every argument to preserve its incoming block lookup owner and macro-loader cache. State-changing arguments are refused with an explicit order-sensitive-argument diagnostic. Pure multi-argument calls, single supplied arguments and ordered array/binary operands retain native behavior. String concatenation visits native function-call values left to right; their argument expressions participate in the same scope, recursion and complete-depth analysis as a direct function call. The adapter neither sorts native maps nor promises support for every finite Tera program. Analysis has separate bounded metadata/work accounting derived from the selected source-byte allowance, with a 64 MiB profile ceiling. Admission diagnostics name their retained template but do not invent AST source spans or a native runtime cause. Templates remain trusted programs: native parsing, expensive expressions, intermediate renderer allocations and elapsed CPU are not a hostile-code sandbox or execution-isolation guarantee. Connected application path CompositionMetadata::compile_templates uses the declared template directory from the checked Theme source. It removes that directory prefix, preserves nested and empty directories and parses all regular files there, regardless of suffix. It excludes metadata, capability inputs, assets and siblings. The application checks the complete subtree and passes its captured bytes to the rendering port without reopening or copying source files. The application verifies the adapter's template identity and returns a CompiledTheme. The private report links it to the workspace digest, site, Theme/palette, source and tree identities, manifest path/digest, compiler profile and limits. The Tera adapter's tool is tera@1.20.1/gazette-captured-templates-v8. A missing, oversized or non-printable profile fails. The profile describes adapter behavior and does not identify the built executable. The same immutable limits drive application context/output checks. The evidence passes unchanged into page/site operator reports and durable preparation history; it is not injected into public models or template context. Changing the profile or bounds changes private preparation evidence even when output bytes coincide. CompiledTheme::render delegates supplied presentation context and also refuses oversized successful adapter output; the adapter remains responsible for bounded emission. The Rust SDK selects Tera once; the CLI uses the same SDK compilation path. CompiledTheme::render_page additionally joins an exact retained authored object to this selected Theme after checking workspace digest and home site. One compiler projection feeds both Tera and the returned local JSON model; the template never reconstructs relationships or receives private source/configuration evidence. Selected Theme/palette keys are included as presentation settings, not inferred identity facts. See connected local page rendering.

Theme contract reference A Theme template receives one page context containing the writing, resolved URLs, navigation and resources it needs to render. The workspace chooses the Theme, palette, capabilities and files. Gazette resolves those choices before it invokes Tera. Use this reference to find what a template can read and what belongs in the workspace. Template question Reference What files and entrypoint does a page need? Build a page template, virtual namespace Which template is selected for a content identity? Exact page-template bindings How do I render body, listings, search and navigation? Generated reading context How do I use project, citation, image or redirect links? Project resources, citation, images, redirects How are recommendations chosen? Ranked recommendations What can template code execute, and what are its bounds? Markup and execution, resource ceilings, Tera adapter Where are the complete typed fields? Native schemas Build a page template Start with a Theme source that has a manifest and a template directory. Declare a page entry Put this in the Theme's root manifest. package = "theme:root" namespace = "root" templates = "templates" browser_theme_colors = { light = "#ffffff", dark = "#20221f" } render = { page = "page.html" } Write the page template Save this as templates/page.html: {{ content.title }}
{{ body_html | safe }}
Render a page Choose the Theme through workspace composition and render a publication. Gazette resolves root/page.html inside the Theme's namespace. The output should use the content title and canonical URL, then show the body. content.title and route.canonical_url use ordinary HTML escaping. Use safe here only for the compiler's body_html, which already includes an authored opening heading. The template reads the supplied context without opening the source. This manifest has no alias or graph entry. Your first publication includes a fuller Theme with collection and journey navigation. Look at theme/theme.toml, theme/templates/page.html and the workspace that chooses them. When a filesystem source is used only by Themes and its root is a Git working repository, Gazette leaves out Git-ignored tooling such as an ignored node_modules directory before opening its contents. Git supplies the ignore rules, including nested rules and exceptions; tracked inputs remain included. A configured subdirectory uses that repository root's rules. Literal exclusions still apply, and an included-filesystem selection reads exactly the files or trees you named, even when Git ignores them. Sources shared with content, manuals, generated reference, plugins or policy inputs keep their ordinary selection, as do pinned repository sources and directories without a Git repository. A nonignored link or special file still fails capture. Virtual Tera namespace Give every Theme package one stable lowercase namespace. Gazette mounts its template directory under that namespace and compiles the dependency graph together. A package named theme:root with namespace root and render.page = "page.html" has entry root/page.html. A dependency with namespace foundation can supply foundation/layout.html. The root package supplies the page, alias and graph entries. An omitted render.llms, render.not_found or render.social_card can come from an explicit dependency. A local declaration overrides it. Two independent providers fail instead of using whichever package comes first. The namespace of the defining package makes it possible for several roots to use one Base template. Dependencies, includes, imports and inheritance resolve only in this virtual namespace. Gazette rejects cycles, undeclared packages, namespace collisions, missing entries and duplicate identities. It does not search other directories or derive a fallback from the site name. Supply interface copy A Theme may declare default labels in its manifest’s [chrome] tables. Use the site chrome fields for skip links, navigation, footer, search and settings, and [chrome.regions] for namespaced component copy. Dependencies provide omitted labels; a dependent Theme, workspace or site can override individual phrases. Gazette retains each label’s declaring package or configuration origin and rejects unresolved conflicts between dependency branches. Themes cannot supply reading handoffs, no-script content destinations or search-control enablement through these defaults. Those remain explicit workspace or site choices. The compiled presentation.chrome contains the effective copy, and hosted components receive the same resolved region labels. Choose the template for one page Set sites.composition.page_templates to map a content ID to a path in the Theme namespace, such as field-notes/product.html. The site map replaces the workspace map as a whole. Omit it to inherit the workspace map or give an empty map to clear it. Gazette checks in this order: The composing site's binding for this content ID. The source's optional template field. The root Theme's ordinary render.page entry. Use the composition origin API to see which setting won. The source declaration remains available. Gazette does not use a title, URL, filename or collection to guess a template. It rejects unknown content IDs, IDs on another site and template paths that are missing, directories or outside the Theme namespace. A generated listing continuation uses its owning content's template and ID. Generated reading context Body and opening heading An ordinary page may carry opening = {heading_html, remainder_html} when its Markdown starts with a top-level H1. These are exact formatter-produced slices; body_html remains the complete body for existing consumers. Declared notebooks are not part of the body: they arrive in notes.notebooks as structured cells, described in notebooks in Notes. To compose a reading header, render opening.heading_html once with the native metadata and render opening.remainder_html once as the body. Never also render the full body in that composition. When opening is absent, preserve the complete body_html; do not promote a later heading or invent one from the document title. Heading IDs, inline links, Notes, search text and JSON-LD meaning remain independently unchanged. Publication metadata and navigation Shared publication metadata includes an optional resolved rights_holder principal selected by the site, never a publisher fallback, and optional render_year supplied by rendering context. Page and generated-listing Themes read site.metadata; a graph Theme reads the same metadata through presentation.publication. Named navigation and footer entries retain their optional namespaced key and native destination facts. The Theme may use these public semantic addresses; it never resolves a URL from a label. Product-documentation outline On a product-documentation collection and its descendants, optional documentation_navigation supplies the resolved manual outline. It contains a root navigation link, current for that entrance and balanced events. Render those events in their supplied order; no recursive template or route lookup is needed. A minimal page-template consumer is: {% if documentation_navigation is defined %}
{% if documentation_navigation.root.route %} {{ documentation_navigation.root.node.title }} {% endif %}
    {% for item in documentation_navigation.events %} {% if item.kind == "group-open" %}
  • {{ item.title }}
      {% elif item.kind == "group-close" %}
    • {% elif item.kind == "page-open" %}
  • {% if item.destination.route %} {{ item.destination.node.title }} {% else %}{{ item.destination.node.title }}{% endif %} {% if item.has_children %}
      {% endif %} {% elif item.kind == "page-close" %} {% if item.has_children %}
    {% endif %}
    • {% endif %} {% endfor %}
{% endif %} ancestor on a page opening can mark the current branch. A page without a route remains a label, rather than receiving a guessed address. Group labels and page titles receive ordinary HTML escaping. Link classification, responsive controls and styling remain Theme decisions. The content model owns outline selection, complete coverage, inheritance and filtering. With no authored order, the compiler supplies structural order; standalone documentation outside a collection has no outline. Discovery projections omit ineligible destinations and empty groups and recompute has_children, so render each view's own balanced events rather than sharing a cached tree between private and discovery output. Search destination A publication-selected Search page is addressed through presentation.search.page (also presentation.chrome.shell.search.page). Match its native content identity to the current page when selecting the search view, rather than testing a route spelling or publication name. An all-pages listing provides the complete admitted, paginated browse fallback using the same ListingLink fields below. The shared chrome labels inherit individually through the Theme, workspace and site declarations; each publication owns its independent search_page destination. A Theme may progressively enhance this native browse view with the configured search index and SDK, preserving usable ordinary links without JavaScript. Listing identity and pagination A configured declaration-only index receives optional listing. Gazette selects and sorts its items before rendering. Render the supplied endpoints and order; the Theme does not derive routes, select candidates or maintain pagination state. Fields Meaning content, title, route, url, output The existing index identity and the compiled destination for this view. page_number, page_size, page_count, total_items One-based current slice, configured slice size, total slices and complete item count. items Ordered existing-item references for this slice. Optional previous, next Resolved serving URLs for adjacent slices. variant primary or alternate. Optional direction Authored ascending or descending chronology; absent for priorities. pages At most seven {number, url, current, gap_before} entries: first, last and current plus/minus two. Optional sorts {direction, url, current} for each configured chronology, always linking to that ordering's page one. Listing items, attribution and artwork Each item refers to existing content with id, authored title, canonical url and optional declared language, published, modified and destination presentation. Optional attributions preserve the item's direct role order and use the same resolved principal shape as a page: Attribution field Meaning principal, role The resolved principal and its directly declared role. Optional website.url Selected serving URL. Optional website.canonical_url Stable public canonical URL. website.destination Native link kind, optional site and destination presentation relative to the listing's owning site, present with the selected website. An empty attribution remains absent; neither the index nor the publisher supplies an author. A Theme can render published as and an author's website.url with rel="author" without catalogue joins or per-page URL settings. Optional artwork contains a required default URL and only explicitly authored light/dark URLs. These decorative URLs come from the eligible item owner's selected static asset plan; private source keys and entries are not exposed. A missing mode variant uses the default; a missing artwork field stays absent. The Theme owns preference dispatch, geometry and decorative markup, using these resolved URLs. Rendition occurrences and URL text share the complete listing bounds. Latest item Optional listing.latest is one existing-item reference with the same shape as items. It is selected from the complete eligible, discoverable population before pagination and independently of display order. Selection uses the index's editorial-day convention: an authored calendar day for date-only values and the UTC day for timestamps. Within the newest day, timestamps compare by instant; equal instants or date-only values use title then identity as stable ties. Undated items are excluded. The field is absent when no dated item exists or the newest day mixes date-only values and timestamps. Different precision on older days does not suppress a clear newest-day choice. This is an editorial-day selection, not an inferred time or timezone for a calendar date. Every continuation and alternate ordering receives the same reference within the shared projection bounds, so a Theme can link to the latest publication without fetching another rendered page. Themes should use this reference rather than guessing from the first item of a paginated or differently ordered list. Project article views A project-articles view additionally supplies listing.subject: Field Meaning project, optional name The exact subject project and configured display name. residence The explicit all, standalone or collected choice. landing {id, title, url, destination} for the selected project landing. Optional explore The configured own-publication unfiltered index in that same link shape, including in an empty view. Every item carries its exact site and native destination facts, preserving cross-publication link treatment for ecosystem articles. Use these fields for contextual copy and onward links. Subject context survives both chronologies and all continuation pages; generated JSON-LD identifies the same project and its landing. These are relevance views, so they add no article browsing_locations. Generated listing views Primary page one is the original index. An alternate ordering's page one and all continuations are generated output views of that same content identity. They use the same template and presentation with a compiler-resolved serving route and listing slice. Each view's JSON-LD describes its collection-page view and ordered item references; it creates no additional authored page or search identity. The shared site model exposes continuation contexts under output-keyed listing_pages. Private rendering evidence binds each exact template and emitted model/HTML digest separately. Generated indexes retain the authored document title and current navigation without needing a redundant visible or concealed page heading. Ordinary article bodies and article-owned Notes keep their separate heading contracts. Declare selection, chronology, priority and pagination in workspace listings, rather than template loops or source-folder conventions. Browsing locations Article and container contexts may receive browsing_locations. Each shallow entry supplies a resolved browsing path: Field Meaning index, title, url Existing index identity, literal index title and exact serving URL. via The listed identity: this page or one of its declared editorial ancestors. kind listing for a generated listing location, or declared for an authored browsing association. page_number, page_count Present for generated locations, identifying the slice containing the listed item. Absent for declared locations. Generated locations join against the same bounded, discovery-selected listing pages used for index rendering. They do not select or sort a second catalogue. Declared locations use the declaring page as via. Both kinds use resolved serving URLs, including the selected preview base. Multiple explicit paths stay multiple paths; no primary is inferred, and empty locations are omitted. The complete generated-plus-declared array shares one occurrence and encoded-text ceiling, with an independent final render-model bound. A Theme may match index to configured navigation by identity, retain its label, mark the current location and expose the supplied URL. Preserve via when interpreting an ancestor's location. These entries establish browsing paths, not editorial parentage or the reader's arrival history. Project landing links Project context can include optional projects[].landing = {id, title, url, destination} from the project’s explicitly selected introduction. Use that exact URL and destination metadata to link an existing project name; keep the name plain when the field is absent. The page’s About/Mentions relationship and its evidence remain separate and unchanged. This projection borrows the retained title and route; it does not copy a body or choose a manual/index as a substitute. Hosted product resources A project-family page with exactly one direct about declaration receives optional project_resources. Hosted components receive the same value at component.context.host.project_resources; projects[].resources uses the same resolver for its exact project. Field Meaning project, optional name Exact project identity and configured display name. actions Ordered {kind, url, destination} records for available destinations. Action kinds are code-documentation, learn, github, mentions, followed by any independently configured blogs, thoughts and available-through. Absent destinations are not fabricated. Each destination carries the native link kind, known content/site identity, relationship facts and selected destination presentation. The Theme uses the supplied links without joining catalogues or constructing routes. Project facts may come from the selected authored landing or a complete inline workspace record; both produce the same joined view. Docs can derive from the exact configured documentation module. Learn omits links to the current page or the project's own landing. available-through points to the exact content destination declared for gated access, including another publication; it does not imply a generic purchase or trial action. See project facts and resources for ownership and validation. Hosted components also receive copy at presentation.chrome.regions: Theme defaults completed with the workspace's and site's individual label overrides, within the same region limits. Missing chrome is an empty map. Shared component templates can render resource anatomy with these supplied labels. The native Markdown transport uses the same component formatter, preserving the resource links without appending a second body. Authored citation tools When supplied, top-level citation contains optional plain text, ordered formats (label, plain text), and optional resolved bibtex / pdf URLs. Use these URLs rather than the authored source references in content.citation. Each present URL has corresponding optional bibtex_destination / pdf_destination facts in the native LinkDestination shape, so shared link markup can classify it without parsing an href. Render text with normal escaping, never safe; omit unavailable tools. Presence is independent of headings, Notes, Markdown alternates and article subtype. No citation formatting algorithm or download generation is implied. See the content-model contract. Emitted reading images images[] describes actual body image occurrences; notes.images[] describes the separately rendered Notes occurrences, including file-referenced notebook Markdown images. Each entry has one-based occurrence, exact resolved destination, native plain-text alt and optional title. Hosted entries have address, also emitted on the matching img as data-gazette-image. Addresses are page/namespace occurrence identities, not source paths. Empty alt stays empty. Optional caption is the admitted reading text from an explicitly declared figure caption; no caption or visual claim is inferred. An image may also carry variants.light and/or variants.dark, resolved through the same source and public/preview addressing as destination; destination remains the default fallback. Optional positive integer width is the authored display width in CSS pixels. Optional intrinsic carries independently verified raster display width/height. Optional svg carries separate verified viewport geometry. Native HTML reserves width and proportional height before enhancement when that evidence permits it; authored width is marked with data-gazette-image-sized. Optional loading and fetch_priority preserve explicit authored browser delivery hints. A compiled page resource’s rendition_of maps the original serving URL to its derived url, without private input coordinates. A viewer matches the occurrence address and one of those declared URLs, and enlarges the rendition currently displayed. An opted-in inline SVG has a separate span[data-gazette-image-ref] with that same address beside its hidden source img; move and restore the complete wrapper to preserve its scoped IDs and live presentation. Do not infer a relationship from sibling position. Notebook cell addresses remain distinct from the primary body and Notes. See image renditions for declarations and Theme responsibilities. This projection includes compiled SVG image uses while leaving those resources out of assets; static asset inventory is not an image-use or MIME registry. Dark image sources and the starting colour mode An image occurrence with a declared dark alternative is wrapped in picture[data-gazette-image-modes]. One source[data-gazette-image-mode="dark"] precedes the unchanged img. Its srcset holds the dark responsive candidates with the image's sizes, or the dark URL alone when the image has no candidates. The img keeps the default src, srcset and sizes, so the browser fetches only the rendition for the mode it shows. Images without a dark alternative keep their unwrapped markup. The source's media follows the Theme's initial_color_mode manifest value, which names the colour mode shown before the reader chooses one: initial_color_mode Dark source media Use it when system (default) (prefers-color-scheme: dark) the stylesheet follows the operating system, as with color-scheme: light dark light not all the Theme starts light whatever the system preference dark all the Theme starts dark whatever the system preference A package without the value inherits it from its nearest declaring dependency; when independent dependencies each declare it, the dependent package must declare its own. Only those three values are admitted. The value describes the Theme's own stylesheet, so declare it beside the rule that pins the starting mode. A Theme that lets the reader choose a mode keeps each dark source in step with that choice: media="all" for dark, media="not all" for light, and (prefers-color-scheme: dark) for a choice to follow the system. Without a choice, restore the emitted media. A Theme that prints in light mode sets not all while printing. The picture adds no layout box only if the Theme makes it display: contents; selectors that expect the image as a direct child also need to match picture > img. Resolved body-link attributes When the compiler resolves an authored Markdown link into the publication graph, the Markdown adapter emits the ordinary href plus Gazette-owned data attributes. They expose the already-resolved destination to Theme CSS and browser behavior; they are not a second resolver and must not be used to infer publication authority: Attribute Meaning data-gazette-link Stable address of this exact link occurrence. data-gazette-destination-kind One of internal-native (the page's own site), cross-site (another configured site), external (outside the configured sites) or resource (a compiled asset or download). data-gazette-destination-content Destination content identity, when the target is content. data-gazette-destination-site Destination site identity, when one is resolved. data-gazette-destination-relationships Space-separated typed relationship names attached to this edge. data-gazette-destination-theme Effective Theme identity of the destination site, when applicable. data-gazette-destination-palette Effective destination palette identity, when applicable. Optional attributes are absent when the compiler has no corresponding fact. Theme code may classify or style the link from these values, but must not reconstruct a route, content identity, relationship, Theme or palette from URL spelling. Redirect destination facts Alias and mirror contexts add optional presentation.redirect_destination in the same native LinkDestination shape (kind, optional content, site, presentation, and relationships). It identifies the already compiled canonical content target relative to the actual serving site. A local alias is internal-native; a canonical copy or mirror targeting another publication is cross-site. route.canonical_url remains the destination URL for the canonical link, refresh and ordinary anchor. These facts do not create another content identity or imply an HTTP redirect. Ordinary page, site and graph contexts omit this field. Theme code must not reconstruct the target from hostnames, paths, page names or mirror labels. Optional reading assistance presentation.chrome.reading_assistance, when selected by the composing workspace, contains label, prompt_template, selection_limit, context_limit and ordered providers: [{id, label, endpoint, query_parameter}]. It is the same validated native chrome object for page and graph rendering; absent configuration supplies no actions. The compiler contains no provider names, activation behavior or prompt execution. See the workspace contract for exact slot syntax, endpoint validation and Unicode character bounds. A Theme owns the selection controls and opens an external handoff only after a reader chooses it. It uses the native page title/route and publication name/home coordinates, bounds selected text and nearby context by the configured character limits, substitutes only documented slots, and sets the configured prompt query parameter through a URL encoder. Provider identities, destinations and visible copy come from the selected chrome object. They are not authored components, region-map JSON, schema.org claims, or inferred relationships. The contract neither promises remote prompt-prefill support nor authorizes automatic transmission. Emitted discovery destinations In complete site assemblies, presentation.discovery contains the successfully emitted site entrypoints. Each record has kind (sitemap, llms, web-manifest or tdm-policy), resolved url and media_type. The sitemap record points to sitemap.xml, whether it is a single map or the index of partitioned maps. It does not list individual partitions. A tdm-policy record appears when the publication reserves text and data mining; its url is the terms page, so a Theme can emit and with that address. These records use the selected serving base, including local preview ports and mount prefixes. The tdm-policy address is the exception: it always names the production terms page. They are shared by authored pages, aliases, listing continuations, taxonomy, graph and mirror views. Disabled outputs and standalone page renders omit the corresponding records; an empty list is absent. Failed output generation or a later collision fails the entire assembly. The workspace supplies human labels and footer placement. Themes render the resolved URLs; they do not infer them from publication domains or configuration flags. Emitted feeds retain their separate presentation.feeds records and their existing empty-feed policy. Machine reading guide An optional render.llms = "llms.txt" declares a captured Theme entry for the publication's generated machine reading guide. The application owns llms.txt placement and supplies one bounded llms object: title, description, coverage, include_human_link, pages and sections. pages is the complete serving-URL-ordered built catalogue for all-pages; sections is the explicit curated path, with title and pages per section. Each page has authored title, optional authored description, actual Markdown url, serving html_url, an existing id when one exists, and optional generated-view page_number/page_count, listing_variant and listing_direction. Themes format this data using the native markdown_text and markdown_destination encoders; they do not discover pages or summarize bodies. The .txt entry does not use HTML suffix escaping. Without an entry the existing bounded native Markdown writer supplies the guide. See workspace machine outputs and the native generation contract. Ranked recommendations Recommendations are how a publication's authored structure becomes what it suggests to a reader next: collections, journeys, editorial links and keywords admit and rank each candidate, so suggestions follow the connections the authors declared. Every native page context includes recommendations = { algorithm, items }, independently of authored related. algorithm is gazette-related/5. items contains zero to five shallow destinations with id, site, authored title, optional authored description, compiled route, optional destination presentation, native destination facts relative to the recommending page, integer score and ordered reasons. They also carry the same bounded shallow listing metadata: optional decorative artwork, authored language, published and modified, direct ordered attributions, and exact classifications. Missing values stay absent; no page body, structural inventory, publisher-as-author or inferred image is copied. The shared listing builder resolves principal websites and artwork from the existing catalog/assets; native destination kinds remain relative to each source consumer. Templates render the supplied order and use route.url; they do not rank, fill missing items, infer addresses or turn suggestions into authored relationships. The same value enters direct-page, discovery, search and shared machine contexts through one page projection. An absent relevant candidate produces an empty list. Candidate eligibility Version 5 considers only positively source-bound, discoverable, canonically routed articles, documentation, project pages, collections and journeys in the compiled corpus. Utility, index and extension pages, self, unrouted records and republished route copies are excluded. A cross-site candidate must meet the same native conditions; there is no same-site bonus. Local previews use their compiled serving addresses. Discoverability is not publication approval, and this algorithm adds no lifecycle, rights or availability claim. A source-unbound inspection has no automatic suggestions for its unbound pages. Admission requires an eligible editorial/structural graph relationship, an existing authored page link (including notes), or an exact normalized authored keyword phrase. Word overlap in titles, descriptions or keyword fragments cannot admit a candidate, even when several discriminating words agree: those words can have different meanings. Topical metadata only strengthens the ranking of candidates admitted by the other evidence categories. The compiler does not invent editorial links to compensate for missing evidence. How recommendations score Scores add independent evidence categories, once per category unless stated otherwise: Evidence Points Reason Current page explicitly relates to destination 120 outgoing-related Destination explicitly relates to current page 100 incoming-related Current page links to the destination 90 outgoing-reference Destination links to the current page 70 incoming-reference Shared exact declared journey 80 shared-journey Shared immediate collection context 50 shared-collection Shared resolved project assertion 60 About/About; 35 About/Mentions; 15 Mentions/Mentions shared-project Exact normalized authored keyword phrase 24 each, at most three shared-keywords Discriminating topical metadata At most 48 topical-metadata Multiple shared projects use the strongest pair, rather than inflating a score with catalogue breadth. A journey contributes only when its declaration and every member are discoverable. Collection context means a direct collection membership or an exact participating journey's containing collection, never a broad recursive ancestor. Hidden containers contribute nothing. Project assertions use the graph's already resolved About/Mentions meaning only when every declaration origin is discoverable; source provenance, author, publisher, project placement and site identity add no points. How topical words affect the score Topical metadata uses Unicode NFKC normalization and lowercase, splitting at nonalphanumeric characters and retaining tokens of at least three characters. For a record whose explicit prose language has primary subtag en, the retained English search provider's stop-word vocabulary is removed from these tokens before corpus frequencies, anchors and scores are computed. The compiler uses parity-checked native lexical data; it does not execute the browser provider, apply stemming or inherit machine.search profile selection. Missing or other prose languages retain lexical tokens without an English fallback. Exact normalized keyword phrases and editorial/structural evidence remain independent and unchanged. A token's strongest field weight is 3 for title or keywords and 1 for description. For N eligible candidates and df records containing a shared token, its points are ceil((source_weight + destination_weight) * (N - df) / N); tokens appearing in every candidate contribute nothing. This category requires at least two distinct shared anchors occurring in the title or authored keywords of both records, as well as at least eight points before its 48-point cap. Anchors use the same normalized token vocabulary and df < N eligibility as scored tokens; raw phrase intersections or generic description overlap cannot supply an anchor. Descriptions can strengthen the ranking of an admitted, anchored match but cannot manufacture eligibility. This conservative rule may omit related prose without a graph relationship or exact shared keyword phrase. Keyword phrases normalize Unicode, case and whitespace. No body, private notes or external service is consulted. Order and limit recommendations Results with positive evidence sort by descending total score, then exact content ID. No irrelevant item is added to reach five. Reasons follow the table order and express ranking evidence, not confidence, truth, an additional editorial edge or a reading sequence. Metadata features are cached once per resolved corpus; route values remain borrowed from its current native route table. Retained endpoints and encoded destination bytes share the existing complete navigation projection ceilings; exhaustion fails the projection rather than silently truncating a resource failure into a successful list. Publication-home social card recipe The optional resource_requirements list preserves declared order and rejects duplicate logical resources. Every requirement must resolve to an independently enabled selection; use = "dependency" keeps these resources out of ordinary page roots. Only the card context adds these resource projections and their compiled module closure to its existing presentation. No resource identity is inferred from a filename. A Theme may declare one render.social_card recipe for the publication's configured home. An explicit identity_assets.link_preview takes precedence and skips generation; it does not exempt an invalid recipe or missing template from package validation. Other pages do not acquire generated cards from this recipe. [render.social_card] resource_requirements = ["stylesheet:social-card", "module:social-card-media"] template = "social-card.html" width = 1200 height = 630 media_selector = "[data-social-media]" media_kind = "image" template is package-local and enters the retained template closure. The recipe inherits as a whole from the nearest declaring dependency, with its template qualified in that package's namespace. A dependent declaration replaces all capture settings. Independent providers conflict until a dependent package chooses a recipe; matching filenames do not settle the conflict. Both dimensions are required integers from 1 through 4096 pixels. media_selector is required, contains 1 through 1024 UTF-8 bytes, and has no control characters or surrounding whitespace. The fixed browser helper checks selector syntax, requires one matching element and checks its declared media kind. media_kind is exactly image or video; a video recipe may also declare video_time_ms from 0 through 600000. An omitted seek selects the helper's initial-frame behavior. Image recipes reject a seek field. The application supplies the full resolved home-page context, its presentation and card.width and card.height. A recipe owns presentation and capture settings, not executable paths, shell arguments, environment variables or helper source files. Native programs are selected separately through the workspace's social-card renderer binding. For an image selected by the recipe, capture binds its data-gazette-image occurrence to the native page image declaration. After the isolated card’s styles load, its resolved CSS color-scheme selects the declared light or dark rendition; a mixed or unspecified scheme follows the browser preference. A missing rendition keeps the original destination. The selected declaration’s destinations must all be retained media assets. Capture neither guesses variant filenames nor executes the source page’s scripts. Component and module names Components are declared at the Theme-manifest root, for example [components.callout], and their template paths are package-local. An optional [components.callout.interaction] selects a logical browser module, an exact export and the supported mount convention. The export is never guessed: it is 1–128 ASCII bytes; the first byte is an ASCII letter, _ or $; remaining bytes are ASCII letters, digits, _ or $; default is valid only when written explicitly. A browser-module recipe may declare at most 512 import aliases. Each alias is a nonempty 1–256-byte ASCII literal, must not start with . or /, may use only ASCII letters, digits, @, /, _, - and ., and may not contain an empty, . or .. slash component. Aliases are exact non-relative specifiers mapped by the workspace to logical resource identities; Gazette does not search package managers, the filesystem or the network. When an enhancement needs an SVG filter chain, construct its SVG nodes inside the element mount slot supplied to the selected browser export. Keep the complete CSS or still-image fallback in the component’s static template. The emitted-HTML profile accepts only its limited inert SVG vocabulary; filter definitions and filter primitives are not admitted inline. Place container contents within the authored body Declare a component with semantic = { kind = "container-contents" } and a package-local template. Its local name is up to the Theme. A collection or journey may use one empty, top-level occurrence without arguments; the compiler rejects other placements. The template receives component.container_contents with kind (collection or journey), documentation, ordered entries and an optional balanced outline. Each entry carries id, site, title and optional description, url, presentation and artwork. Presentation contains the selected theme and optional palette; artwork contains default and optional light and dark renditions. These are the existing resolved child or step facts, including the selected public or preview address. An absent URL remains unlinked. An outline preserves authored documentation groups over the direct entries. Its events are {kind: "group-open", title}, {kind: "entry", content} and {kind: "group-close"}; an entry refers to the matching identity in entries. The payload contains no recursively copied content. Use component.context.host.site as the serving site when passing entries to the Theme's existing link or card renderer. When the slot is present, the direct page model sets container_contents_placed = true. Guard the Theme's existing appended container deck with this flag so the deck appears once. The field is absent otherwise, preserving the existing default. Generated navigation is omitted from excerpts, public component-use metadata and search text. Native Markdown places the compiler's existing discovery-filtered reading list at the slot and suppresses its old append; that reading fragment is private and never exposed to the template. HTML keeps direct journey membership, so it can legitimately show explicit steps that the discovery reading list omits. Render FAQ text and structured data from one list Declare an FAQ group and its question items explicitly. The component names are local to the Theme; the semantic declaration supplies their meaning: [components.faq] template = "components/faq.html" semantic = { kind = "faq" } [components.faq-item] template = "components/faq-item.html" semantic = { kind = "faq-item", question_argument = "question" } arguments = { type = "object", required = ["question"], additionalProperties = false, properties = { question = { type = "string", minLength = 1 } } } Each item takes its question from that argument and its answer from its Markdown body. A landing page can author the list once: - component: faq heading: { level: 2, text: Before starting } sections: - component: faq-item arguments: { question: Can we begin with one workflow? } body: Yes. Choose one workflow and agree what a useful result would look like. The item template renders the question with ordinary escaping and the admitted component.body.html as its answer. The group template retains its complete body. Gazette compares each template's decoded words with those inputs and refuses changed, missing or additional wording. Formatting and whitespace may differ. This check does not establish browser visibility; test the actual disclosure, keyboard and no-script views too. When JSON-LD is selected, each group contributes a FAQPage under the page's existing hasPart entries. Its ordered Question entries use the same question arguments; each acceptedAnswer.text carries the exact admitted answer HTML, including resolved links and formatting. The surrounding CollectionPage or other page type, description, navigation and listing mainEntity stay intact. Generated listing summaries do not copy a page's FAQ claims. There is no second authored answer list or promise of search placement. FAQ items require an enclosing declared group, a nonempty question and an answer body. Nested FAQ groups or items, empty groups and FAQs inside presentation-only payloads fail rather than producing incomplete structured data. Ordinary components without a semantic declaration keep their existing behavior. Bind an image to its authored caption Declare the figure and caption roles in the Theme. Their local names can differ; the semantic roles establish the relationship: [components.figure] template = "components/figure.html" semantic = { kind = "figure" } [components.figure-caption] template = "components/figure-caption.html" semantic = { kind = "figure-caption" } The figure template renders ; the caption template renders . Inert wrapper attributes and surrounding whitespace are allowed. Gazette checks the wrapper separately and requires its complete admitted body to remain unchanged, including the image destination, alt, title, caption formatting and links. The existing Markdown, MathML and inline SVG admission rules continue to govern that body; the figure guard does not reinterpret it through the smaller SVG profile used for general Theme HTML. ::::figure ![A diagram of the shared interface](./shared-interface.svg) :::figure-caption Different models use the same interface while retaining their own state. ::: :::: Each declared figure requires exactly one emitted Markdown image and one nested caption with nonempty reading text. Linked images retain their surrounding link. The caption's admitted plain text becomes that occurrence's optional images[].caption and its JSON-LD ImageObject.caption; the original Markdown supplies HTML, search text and the Markdown alternate once. Alt text and image titles keep their separate meanings. Ordinary images and following paragraphs do not acquire a caption automatically. Nested figures, orphan or repeated captions, images inside captions, semantic components inside captions and presentation-only figure content are rejected. A figure can appear inside an FAQ answer without changing the FAQ's question-and-answer relationship. Notebook attachment figures keep their visible caption and reading text, while embedded data URIs remain outside the public image-occurrence metadata. Keep playback payloads out of reading outputs Set presentation_only = true on a component definition when its entire body supplies playback data or decoration rather than something to read. For example, a film may carry hundreds of frame resource links in a separate component: [components.animation-frames] template = "components/animation-frames.html" presentation_only = true Gazette still validates every child, resolves its resources and renders the complete HTML. It omits that component subtree from search text and Markdown alternatives, including notes referenced only from the omitted subtree. The setting defaults to false; it does not depend on component names, link labels, CSS visibility or whether JavaScript runs. Important Keep the film’s meaningful description, still-image alternatives, captions and actions outside the presentation-only component. Mark only the playback payload; marking the enclosing film would remove its readable account too. Resource ceilings The default resource-compilation profile admits at most 512 declared input entries, 32 path components per entry, 256 KiB per retained file and 4 MiB for the complete declared input tree. A successful emitted artifact is at most 8 MiB. Raster and font recipes have their own additional typed limits. These ceilings bound accepted work; they are not a process sandbox or publication certification. What each markup profile permits Markup What to expect Authored Markdown Its parser and compiler reject raw HTML. Notebook HTML and MathML Separate profiles accept documented forms under their own limits. Tera templates The workspace trusts the captured template code. Autoescaping follows the template suffix. Use safe only for compiler-produced fragments such as body_html. Tera is not a sandbox. Final HTML/XML, CSS, JavaScript and resource links Separate structural and disclosure checks apply. Resource links must match the allowed inventory. Output prepared for release Inline event handler attributes fail. Policy checks, technical checks and approval still apply. The font profile permits one emitted WOFF2 resource with the documented @font-face descriptors. Unsupported font shapes and at-rules fail. Style the Markdown table wrapper Native Markdown HTML places each unchanged table inside
. The marker identifies one table's presentation boundary without assigning a theme, width, scrolling rule, ARIA role or focus stop. Themes may make that boundary locally scrollable while leaving the table, header groups, row groups, cell alignment and inline content native. Markdown alternates retain ordinary Markdown tables. The wrapper exists without JavaScript; conditional overflow hints and keyboard enhancement remain Theme responsibilities. Print the Theme and template schemas The schemas are generated from the same Rust types that parse or serialize the native contracts; they are not separately maintained copies: gazette schema theme-manifest gazette schema template-context gazette schema workspace gazette schema authored-content gazette schema legal-source MCP exposes the same owner as contract_schema, whose contract value is theme-manifest, template-context, workspace, authored-content or legal-source. Schema discovery performs no native read or mutation. The schemas describe the current Gazette 0.1 contract; they do not create an independent compatibility promise. The Theme-manifest schema covers the package identity, namespace, template root, optional root render recipes, browser colors and palettes, the initial colour mode, components, exact package dependencies, declared resources, ordered resource requirements and capability needs. The workspace schema covers unresolved declarations before native path acquisition. The template-context schema describes the exact page value sent to Tera, including the shared presentation envelope and optional compiler-owned JSON-LD value. CLI outcome contract When a Theme development tool invokes Gazette's CLI for schema inspection or local rendering, interpret the exit status separately from the operation result. The process uses these stable status classes: 0: the selected application operation completed successfully. A deliberately handled broken output pipe may also terminate successfully because the consumer closed a read-only stream. 1: application, encoding or I/O failure. For effectful work, retained evidence may say that an external outcome is unknown; this status never implies safe retry. 2: invocation or argument error reported by the command parser, including an explicitly invalid operation relationship. Exact effect state and recovery guidance belong to the operation result and retained evidence, not to exit-code guesswork. MCP and VS Code project the same canonical operation metadata rather than maintaining a second lifecycle model. See local rendering, page resources, Markdown, browser capabilities and MCP for the behavior behind each contract.

VS Code integration
Gazette meets each actor where it works, with the same publication model behind every mode: a person writing in an editor arrives through the language server, an agent helping in Claude Code or Codex through the MCP server and its skill, and a build or integration through the command line and SDKs.
Build the Gazette extension from source and load it in a separate VS Code development window. Then connect it to the same publication you can already preview. If the extension is installed and you want to edit a publication, start with Write with feedback.
The extension starts one language server for each configured workspace folder. Microsoft's language client handles LSP updates. Gazette's Rust SDK handles configuration and content analysis. When you ask for an application operation, the extension starts a separate MCP process and displays its result.
The extension is named Gazette, with publisher rtepl and extension ID rtepl.gazette-vscode. These are its manifest identifiers; the checkout instructions below load it locally. Marketplace publication remains a separate release step.
Gazette: Check Saved Site checks the active file's workspace using the same native check as gazette check. With no active workspace file, it uses the only open folder or asks you to choose among several. The result opens as plain text with file names, line numbers and missing IDs. It checks saved files; save your edits first to include them. The language server continues to report problems in unsaved text.
Open the local extension from a source checkout
For an installed VSIX, follow the installation guide. To work on this editable checkout, use VS Code's extension development host to load this checkout. You need a built Gazette executable, VS Code 1.96 or newer, Node and npm for the locked extension dependencies, and a local authoring folder. Build the executable using Installing and running Gazette.
Build the extension
From the Gazette repository root, install the extension's locked dependencies without lifecycle scripts and compile its TypeScript:
npm --prefix integrations/vscode ci --ignore-scripts
npm --prefix integrations/vscode run build

Select your publication
Open the folder you created in Your first publication. Keep its files and preview; this setup adds editor feedback to the same writing.
The starter already supplies .vscode/settings.json:
{
  "gazette.workspace.configuration": "gazette.toml",
  "gazette.workspace.discovery": true
}

Gazette selects pages, included configuration, manual navigation and package manifests from that workspace. A new page beneath a configured content source is admitted when first opened. Sources outside the open folder use the workspace's configured roots and machine binding. For an older starter, remove its explicit gazette.workspace.documents list to use automatic discovery.
Open a trusted development window
Launch the extension in a separate window. Substitute your own absolute paths; the profile and extensions directories should be new, short local paths. VS Code uses a socket below the profile on macOS, so a long path can prevent startup. The code command is VS Code's command-line launcher.
code --new-window \
  --extensionDevelopmentPath="/absolute/path/to/gazette/integrations/vscode" \
  --user-data-dir="/absolute/short/gazette-editor-profile" \
  --extensions-dir="/absolute/short/gazette-editor-extensions" \
  "/absolute/path/to/gazette-notes"

In this separate window, review and grant trust to the authoring folder when VS Code asks. Set Gazette: Server Path in User settings to your exact absolute Gazette executable. Keep that executable setting out of the workspace JSON above. Then run Gazette: Restart Server from the Command Palette.
Check feedback and navigation
Open gazette.toml and use Go to Definition on 'owner:field-notes' to select the principal declaration. Change a publisher reference to 'owner:missing' without saving; Problems should show the unresolved reference. Restore the original value to clear it.
Open content/keep-the-context/index.md. Its heading should appear in Outline. Gazette: Page Details opens the page's source context. Return to Correct a declaration in the publication to edit the article and see its saved result in your preview.
If the extension does not load, confirm the development path names the folder containing package.json and that the build produced bundle/extension.js. If the language server does not start, check workspace trust, the User executable setting and the selected root configuration; inspect Output → Gazette for the cause. A readable configuration with a typo remains open for correction, including unsaved repair. Unrelated folders without that configuration stay inactive. For client development, use the extension build and checks.
Configure the files the extension reads
An installed platform package uses its included Gazette program when gazette.server.path is empty. To choose another program, set that User or machine setting to an absolute path; a source-checkout development host requires this explicit setting. Workspace, folder and workspace-language overrides fail, even in trusted repositories. The extension starts the selected executable with the fixed argument lsp and the folder as its working directory. It uses no shell, PATH fallback or extra arguments.
Folder setting	What it controls	
gazette.authoring.enabled	Own an authoring session. Defaults to true. In a multi-root workspace, you can disable it for the whole workspace and enable it on the composition folder only. Source-only folders still supply their named files. Disabling stops the session and releases its files. Application commands remain available.	
gazette.workspace.configuration	Folder-relative workspace configuration. Defaults to gazette.toml.	
gazette.workspace.discovery	Discover sources from the configuration when no explicit source lists are supplied. Defaults to true.	
gazette.workspace.manualSupport	Additional manual files outside configured navigation, as { source, path }. Each path is relative to its configured Gazette source.	
gazette.workspace.configurationDocuments	Folder-relative TOML include files. The compiler checks that they match the root's includes.	
gazette.workspace.roots	Additional opened folders as { id, uri }. The anchor folder uses workspace as its root ID.	
gazette.workspace.documents	Authored Markdown, article-owned notes.md or project-documentation files. Give a relative path within the anchor folder or use { root, file, path } to set the physical file and its logical compiler path separately. Notes are editable documents under their article ID.	
gazette.workspace.manuals	Manuals with their configured source ID, root, file and logical path.	
gazette.workspace.pagePackageInputs	Opaque files belonging to a page bundle.	
gazette.workspace.packageBaselines	Named theme or plugin manifests with their package IDs.	
Automatic discovery reads text selected by native workspace roles and retains asset metadata without reading asset payloads. The discovery contract explains exact includes, manual support, package manifests and refresh. Nonempty explicit source lists keep the older named-file mode; set gazette.workspace.discovery to false to choose that mode even with empty lists. The remaining paragraphs in this section describe its locators and opened-root requirements.
If the server cannot start, a notification names the cause and offers Choose Gazette Program, Open Settings and Show Output. Choosing a program saves its path in User settings. Repeated attempts with the same failure do not stack notifications. If one folder has invalid settings, fix it and run Gazette: Restart Server. Other folders can start independently. Gazette's editor language highlighting does not make a file part of the workspace. Source parsing and membership belong to the native compiler and SDK.
Paths keep their literal percent signs and Unicode. Empty or dot components, traversal, backslashes, controls and duplicate physical files across roles fail. Every file must belong to the configured opened root. For nested folders, use the nearest owning folder as VS Code does. A logical compiler prefix supplies no editorial membership or public route.
The extension sends file locators through LSP native_selection. It does not read the bodies itself. The request allows 4096 files and 512 KiB for serialized locators, below the default 1 MiB incoming frame. The server reads the named regular files. TOML limits apply to configuration and package manifests, and content limits apply to authored files. One entry/byte budget covers all roots. SDK limits also count IDs, baseline text and open edits. See the file-backed LSP contract for initialization.
The files are read during one request, but changes across roots are not atomic. When a watched source changes, the client requests a fresh read. Invalid TOML and unresolved references remain available to diagnose. An editor read does not authorize a build or code execution.
Visible authoring context
Open the workspace containing gazette.toml. Discovery follows its configured source roots. Explicit distributed selections still require their named folders to be opened. Configured TOML modules, package manifests and the +++ frontmatter in Markdown get TOML highlighting. Highlighting leaves source membership unchanged.
Command	What you can inspect	
Gazette: Page Details	Current field meanings, diagnostics, cursor assistance, inherited identity and page companions in the Gazette Authoring view. Refresh clears outdated results.	
Gazette: Inspect Current Editor with MCP	A read-only MCP query over the current editor snapshot, including unsaved text and versions. Results name Gazette as the provider and link to ranges when the analysis reports them. Export the full private result from the view if needed.	
For automatic discovery, the MCP handoff transfers only unsaved text, up to 12 MiB under a separate 16 MiB frame limit. It retains the complete selection and clean open versions. The receiving SDK reads saved files and checks their baseline hashes before replaying edits; a changed saved file or changed membership refuses the handoff. Saved inputs still have native source and retention limits. Explicit supplied-buffer selections transfer their complete bounded inputs. A change during transfer or querying invalidates the result. The temporary MCP handle closes after the query. Build commands still use the inputs you give them.
Sessions and overlays
A composition client selects either native discovery from one owning folder or an explicit root and file set. It requires the server advertisement gazette.authoring = 0.1.0 inside experimental capabilities and standard document-symbol support. Discovery also requires the advertised gazette/selectSource method. A server that does not advertise these contracts is stopped; there is no independent-buffer compatibility mode.
In discovery mode, the client asks the server whether a newly opened native path is selected before forwarding its text. The returned selection supplies exact identities and shared-file custody. Unrelated text is not forwarded. Explicit mode uses exact file selectors and opened-root ownership. Configured TOML files receive Gazette language highlighting; source roles remain native workspace facts.
The client sends already-open and newly opened selected buffers, including unsaved text, as overlays. Full-text changes retain editor versions. A save acknowledges the exact open text as the new retained baseline; closing removes the overlay and restores that baseline in the server. Every selected configuration module and content source participates in the same composition's analysis. An open module's current buffer replaces its captured baseline throughout the resolved graph. Diagnostic interpretation, cross-document consequences and symbol construction remain in Rust.
The extension watches exact selected files and, in discovery mode, the declared configuration files and separate machine binding. Closed-file changes refresh the existing native session while preserving open overlays. Explicit mode instead retires the affected composition and captures its fixed selection again. An observed external change to an open text file is deferred until it closes. New content files can be discovered on first open. Snapshots, authoring context and source navigation from pending or replaced clients are refused.
The diagnostic transport guard rejects foreign URIs, stale versions and unversioned baseline results while the source is open, including empty results. It rechecks editor identity/version after asynchronous conversion and before applying results. One active conversion plus one coalesced latest packet per selected source bounds queued work; retired clients cannot apply late results. Version 9.0.1 discards the protocol version before ordinary diagnostic middleware. The narrow bridge therefore registers a raw diagnostic notification handler through the client's public onNotification API before startup. The pinned client installs pending public handlers after its builtin diagnostic handler; the registered handler retains the original version through public conversion and collection APIs. There is no private-method override or second diagnostic model. A dependency upgrade must requalify this registration order and packet delivery behavior.
Definition, reference, workspace identity hover and reference-completion requests share a selected-buffer guard around the standard language-client middleware. Before forwarding and after asynchronous transport/conversion, it checks current folder ownership, the exact open-document object, version, source text, cancellation and session retirement. Changed or retired requests return no result; current transport failures remain failures. Rust supplies locations, Markdown hover, schema-derived field/enum assistance and source-bound reference replacement proposals; the extension neither parses labels nor constructs targets, identity descriptions or a completion catalog.
