For a new resource or relationship, add a focused case when the existing journeys do not cover its behavior. Inspect the affected host output and the refusal cases relevant to the change.
Configuration and file review belong to the workspace contract. Running the project’s own check is a separate step. The verifier recipe needs a real exit status, and a pass shows only what that check tests. Inspect the generated instructions as well as running the compiler checks. Actual host invocation, task quality, outside effects and owner acceptance each need their own observation when they are part of the task.
Package source bundles covers copying and checking selected source files for distribution. Extraction makes the source available. Choosing a resource for a project and checking that it works there are separate steps.

Package source bundles
Use a source bundle when another checkout or host needs Pale's Package methods. The archive contains the requested Packages, their pinned dependencies, and the licences and notices that identify where the files came from.
Inventory a detached Package source set
From the checkout, run python3 tools/package_corpus_inventory.py /absolute/source-root to list each Package's declared licence, source file digests and pinned dependencies. This uses Pale's Rust reader through the CLI, so declaration and link checks agree with compilation. Creating the inventory needs the checkout's Rust toolchain and Python 3.11 or newer. The inventory includes the corpus notices and the upstream licences. It fails on an undeclared Package file, missing notices or a dependency pin it cannot resolve. The bundle does not include Pale’s runtime.
For a bundle of design methods, pass --package pale.design to include that Package and the dependencies in its manifests. Repeat --package to request more Packages, or omit it to inventory all Package sources. These flags choose files for the archive. The project, operation, host, grants and runtime profile are outside that choice.
--paths prints relative paths within the source root. It includes the notices, upstream licences and verification tools, and writes no files. From the source repository, create a fresh directory for the outputs and pass the path list to tar.
mkdir /absolute/fresh
python3 tools/package_corpus_inventory.py . --package pale.design > /absolute/fresh/inventory.json
python3 tools/package_corpus_inventory.py . --package pale.design --paths > /absolute/fresh/paths.txt
COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar -cf /absolute/fresh/methods.tar -T /absolute/fresh/paths.txt

Compare tar -tf /absolute/fresh/methods.tar with /absolute/fresh/paths.txt. Use the verbose listing to confirm every member is a regular file. Reject symlinks, AppleDouble metadata and generated bytecode. On macOS, COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 suppresses that metadata, and the archive listing confirms which files are present.
Extract into a new empty directory. Run python3 /absolute/extracted/tools/package_corpus_inventory.py /absolute/extracted --verify /absolute/fresh/inventory.json. This detached check needs only Python: it checks the exact files and digests against the saved inventory without reinterpreting Package declarations. A changed or extra Package file fails verification. Deliver the inventory alongside the archive and compare it with the sender's original. Keep any host-written instructions and inspection records with the delivery, clearly identified apart from the upstream source files. Record the archive digest separately from the source revision so you can identify both what you delivered and where it came from. Change the maintained sources upstream, then regenerate the bundle.
Before distributing the archive, review its included licences. In the receiving host, check that the requested methods load and their required links lead to the bundled guidance. You can read the methods without a running Pale service or a private checkout. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -p test_package_corpus_inventory.py to test whether the inventory detects missing or altered sources.
Verify current Package composition
After checking the extracted files, point a disposable workspace's machine binding at their root and run distribution-info to calculate the compiler's release digests. Use the distribution lock for that source to validate the profiles, then review a plan and inspect the files it writes to a disposable target. The archive inventory identifies the copied files. The lock tells the compiler which release inputs to use. Record build and licence checks against the files that actually ship.
Run cargo test --locked --offline -p pale-application --test packages to check how Pale reads and accepts Package sources. Run cargo test --locked --offline -p pale-application --test compile current_corpus to check the current authored workflows.
The second test builds disposable fixtures from the maintained sources and checks what Pale writes for Codex and Claude. Required guidance appears once, optional guidance stays discoverable, and links from skills, agents, startup and internal-operation files reach their intended resources. Pale refuses a Publication operation when its provider is missing. For rejected link destinations, diagnostics report a hash of the destination without copying the raw source text. These tests need no previously built executable. They check compiler and renderer behavior. To establish host invocation, agent judgment or publication quality, inspect those outcomes separately.
When changing resource bodies, follow the body-link authoring contract.
To find the implementation, return to Source layout.

Repository-guidance workspace
Use this complete example to inspect or integrate Pale's source-guidance route. It chooses Engineering's change role and four Engineering/Governance policy families for one repository. It contains no operation, provider, lifecycle hook or runtime execution path.
For copying the starter, setting machine paths, inspecting guidance and applying a reviewed plan, follow Add coding instructions to a repository. That product task owns the installation procedure.
What the inputs describe
Input	Meaning	
pale-workspace.toml	Project repository, execution workspace local-guidance and repository source	
capabilities.toml	Source-only method selection without callable runtime operations	
machines/local.toml	Local Pale distribution and canonical target-repository paths	
distribution.lock.toml	Package content identities produced by distribution-info --lockfile for the actual distribution	
resolution.lock.toml and universe.lock.toml	Workspace resolution and universe identities	
The distribution lock is created after copying the example; it is not supplied as a universal pin. Review it when the distribution changes. Project facts, commands, credentials and acceptance criteria stay with the repository and its tools.
Both hosts use the target's AGENTS.md, preserving local text and each other's marked contributions. Skills and references use each host's native paths. Pale does not create CLAUDE.md; see Load the shared entry in Claude Code for how Claude Code reads the shared file.
Embed the same workflow
The Rust SDK compiles the effective profile and renders a repository/host projection. Its native source-guidance methods additionally plan against real file baselines, remember a displayed proposal, apply that exact review and reconcile interrupted writes. The CLI exposes those operations with a readable text diff and a digest-free apply.
Inspection does not write guidance. A plan does not authorize a write. Applying the reviewed plan confirms its files, while the coding host's use of that guidance needs an actual task in that host. A source-guidance result cannot be passed to runtime apply.
Load the shared entry in Claude Code
Use Claude Code 2.1.285 or later with its built-in instruction-file plugin enabled. An existing project or ancestor CLAUDE.md can mask AGENTS.md under the default loading mode. To load both without replacing those instructions, select claude-md-and-agents-md under Project instructions in /config, or in user settings, managed settings or the invocation's --settings JSON:
{
  "pluginConfigs": {
    "cc-plugin-agents-md@builtin": {
      "options": {
        "instructionFiles": "claude-md-and-agents-md"
      }
    }
  }
}

Project and local settings do not control this option. Check /memory in the actual host to confirm the shared file was loaded; the file's presence on disk does not show that. Claude's instruction-file documentation describes the plugin. Pale does not change global settings or create a second repository entry file, and existing client and upstream instruction files keep their owners.
An earlier Pale ownership record may name CLAUDE.md. An update then refuses to install into the new entry. Review guidance plan --host claude-code --intent remove with the same workspace and repository selections, apply that removal, then plan and apply the new installation. Removal preserves text outside Pale's exact recorded contribution. Reconcile any pending journal through the CLI recovery route before proceeding.

    NativeEffect,

Consequence class of a public capability invocation.

The invocation cannot plan or cause an external effect.

The invocation constructs an immutable plan candidate but causes no effect.

The invocation admits authority for a later effect but causes no effect itself.

The invocation may cause a confined native external effect.

pub enum ConfigurationImprovementReviewResult {
    Preview {
        summary: ConfigurationImprovementPreviewSummary,
        impacts: PortableWorkspaceImpactPage,
    },
    Details {
        summary: ConfigurationImprovementPreviewSummary,
        explanation: PortableWorkspaceExplanation,
        source: Box<PortableWorkspaceSubjectInspection>,
        source_page_state: ConfigurationImprovementSourcePageState,
    },
    Finished {
        terminal: ConfigurationImprovementTerminal,
    },
}
Exact transport result of a stateless source-based configuration review.

A preview carries the first bounded impact page beside its complete summary.
Details carry one subject’s causal and source evidence after checking that
summary. A finished result carries the caller’s explicit disposition. No
result writes configuration or establishes authority for a later effect.



Variants§
§Preview

Fresh review facts and the first bounded impact page.


Fields
§summary: ConfigurationImprovementPreviewSummaryComplete coordinates and counts for the review.



§impacts: PortableWorkspaceImpactPageFirst impact page in the SDK’s canonical order.




§Details

Causal and source evidence for one subject in a checked preview.


Fields
§summary: ConfigurationImprovementPreviewSummaryComplete coordinates and counts for the checked review.



§explanation: PortableWorkspaceExplanationExisting comparison-owner explanation for the selected subject.



§source: Box<PortableWorkspaceSubjectInspection>Bounded candidate-source evidence from the exact compilation.



§source_page_state: ConfigurationImprovementSourcePageStateWhether this stateless page is complete or needs retained review.




§Finished

One explicit effect-free review decision.


Fields
§terminal: ConfigurationImprovementTerminalDisposition and exact preview governed by that decision.

    Complete,
    RetainedReviewRequired,

Whether the returned candidate-source page exhausts its evidence.

Stateless transports do not carry the inspection cursor because that
cursor belongs to its retained review. An incomplete page therefore tells
the caller to continue through a retained SDK or editor review.



Variants§
§Complete

The proof-input and source-occurrence sections are both exhausted.


§RetainedReviewRequired

More evidence exists and this stateless result cannot resume the scan.

pub enum DiagnosticStage {
    InputAdmission,
    ContractValidation,
    SemanticAdmission,
    PackageLoading,
    WorkspaceLoading,
    Compilation,
    Rendering,
    OperationAdmission,
    ResidentAdmission,
    ResidentRecovery,
    Planning,
    Materialization,
    NativeAction,
    HostObservation,
    Internal,

}
Closed processing stage at which an admitted DiagnosticV1 was established.



Variants§
§InputAdmission

External bytes or command values failed initial admission.


§ContractValidation

A value failed an embedded structural contract.


§SemanticAdmission

A structurally valid value failed owner-specific meaning.


§PackageLoading

Package sources failed loading or verification.


§WorkspaceLoading

Principal-workspace sources failed loading or verification.


§Compilation

Compiler resolution, projection, or sealing failed.


§Rendering

A Pale-rendered surface could not be produced.


§OperationAdmission

An operation was not admitted under current compiled state.


§ResidentAdmission

A resident generation or durable runtime transition failed admission.


§ResidentRecovery

Recovery could not establish a safe continuation or retry posture.


§Planning

An effect-free plan could not be constructed or admitted.


§Materialization

An admitted plan could not be materialized or reconciled.


§NativeAction

A pure built-in action failed admission or computation.


§HostObservation

An external prerequisite could not be observed reliably.


§Internal

A Pale application invariant failed outside a narrower stage.

Variants§
§UnsafeEntryKind

The canonical leaf is not a private, non-symlink regular file.


§CorruptOrPartial

SQLite could not decode the required initial-v1 structures.


§WrongStoreKind

Persisted physical kind names the other control-store class.


§WrongLogicalStoreId

Persisted logical store identity differs from the expected identity.


§WrongControlIncarnation

Persisted control-store incarnation differs from the expected incarnation.


§WrongPrincipalScope

Persisted principal scope differs from the expected principal.


§WrongDeploymentScope

Persisted deployment scope differs from the expected immutable binding.

pub enum ObservationStepCompletion {
    Complete,
    Stopped(ObservationStepLimit),
    Incomplete(ObservationStepLimit),
}
Whether a bounded step exhausted its selected input.



Variants§
§Complete

The selected input for this snapshot and filter was exhausted.


§Stopped(ObservationStepLimit)

More input can remain after an ordinary resource stop. Continue with the
returned cursor; this state does not prove absence.


§Incomplete(ObservationStepLimit)

The next indivisible result does not fit the raw request limits. No
continuation is available because the same limits cannot make progress;
later input can still exist.

through PortableWorkspaceCompilation::direct_dependencies. An empty page
is conclusive only after its scan reports completion.

    TerminalAlreadyEstablished,

}
Exact result of one resident Cancel request.



Variants§
§TerminalAlreadyEstablished

The operation had already reached a final state before this request.


§AlreadyRequested

The same Cancel request was already recorded.


§RequestRetained

The Cancel request was durably recorded.


§LocallyCancelled

Final cancellation of the local operation was durably recorded.


§DispatchedRequestRetained

A dispatched operation retained the request and received local notification.


§A2aResponseReadStopped

The local A2A response read stopped without proving remote cancellation.


§ConsultationCollected

Consultation collection had already completed.


§ReconciliationOnly

Recovery or uncertainty requires reconciliation.


§DispatchOwnerRequired

The selected dispatch needs another exact process owner.


§ConsultationStopped

The consultation request and its stopped roster were durably recorded.


§NotCollecting

The target is not an open consultation.

pub const fn capability_inventory() -> &'static [ApiCapability]
Return the immutable current API capability inventory.

The slice is conformance and exposure metadata only. Looking up a row does

Crate pale_sdk 
Source 
Compile, inspect, and review Pale configuration through one shared API.

This crate builds on pale-application, pale-contracts, pale-core and
pale-ports, and composes the filesystem, process, Unix-socket and
control-store adapters for local work. The CLI, LSP, ACP and A2A interfaces,
the agent host and the Go, JavaScript, Python and WebAssembly bindings build
on it; MCP reaches it through the CLI.

Rust callers and language bindings use these application operations without
implementing another compiler or diagnostic policy. Requests contain owned
input data. Compilation returns opaque handles that retain validated state;
callers use their methods instead of inspecting compiler internals.

§First call

Read a schema embedded in this binary and handle an unavailable schema:


use pale_sdk::PaleApi;

let api = PaleApi::new()?;
let schema = api.contract_schema("diagnostic.v1")?;
assert_eq!(schema.registry_id(), "diagnostic.v1");
println!("{}: {} bytes", schema.schema_uri(), schema.bytes().len());

if let Err(error) = api.contract_schema("not-a-selected-schema") {
    eprintln!("{}", error.diagnostic().summary());
}


This lookup reads embedded data. It does not start a runtime, contact a
provider, or change files. ApiError carries a structured DiagnosticV1;
use its fields rather than parsing a failure message. Initialization can
fail separately with ApiInitializationError.

§Configuration workflows


PaleApi::compile_portable_workspace compiles the workspace documents
supplied by the caller. Its handles support comparisons, pages of changes
and affected items, and explanations tied to those compilations.

EffectiveProfileCompilation lets callers inspect a profile while authoring.
Snapshots, pages, changes, explanations and visual views use the facts kept
in that compilation. They make no new observations of the machine.

PaleApi::inspect_configuration_improvement starts a review of a
proposed change. Checking or accepting a proposal does not apply it.

OneShotCompilation summarizes a complete captured compilation and
prepares repository plans for a separate review and application step.


Other operations inspect Package inputs to create or repair a lock without
relying on the old lock, validate selected public contracts, run built-in
computations without external effects, and check or construct structured
diagnostics. capability_inventory lists the operations each interface
may expose.

§Resident operations

A resident is Pale’s long-running local service. Connect to one through a
caller-supplied ResidentAttachment. Its carrier chooses the endpoint and
authenticates the peer. Its response checker verifies signatures, authority
changes and protection against restoring older state. The SDK does not find,
start or administer the resident.

Starting an operation returns a durable handle before dispatch. Each advance
performs one step within its limits. Observe reads the current signed records;
Cancel requests cancellation, but does not confirm that the operation ended.

§Local operations and their limits

The opt-in native-local feature adds filesystem and process methods. Use
them to inspect local state, save plans, check saved plans before writing,
apply, adopt or remove files under a checked plan, and inspect evidence
when a write’s outcome is uncertain. Enabling the feature makes these methods
available; it runs nothing and grants no permission to act. Local adapters
remain internal, and callers still supply any authenticated resident connection.
Inspecting the control store reports its storage state, not resident health.

The hook API checks that a host event matches its configured route. It stops
at that check: it cannot deliver the event to the resident, evaluate policy or
perform an action. Portable comparisons likewise describe configuration;
changing the active generation, observing a provider, checking a plan for writes
and establishing readiness to act each require their own checks.

Installation and activation sit outside this API. Compiler internals, native
path types, adapters, provider payloads, resident-generation bodies and decoded
machine bindings remain internal. Interfaces own terminal rendering and exit
status; the Pale application owns the rules for verifying receipts.

Struct A2aDelegateHandle

pub struct A2aDelegateHandle { /* private fields */ }
Structurally verified identity of one Delegate operation.

This SDK-owned projection proves exact canonical bytes, the selected public
contract, the handle’s self-carried digest, and the Delegate operation
class. Its record reference has passed only public syntax validation; proving
that the reference retains these bytes requires resident custody. This type
does not verify the signature, grant caller or disclosure authority, recover
the operation, select an A2A route, or permit a send.

A failed API call with a structured explanation and its underlying cause.

Read Self::diagnostic for machine-readable failure and retry information.
Display shows only the summary, within its length limit.
std::error::Error::source exposes the typed Rust cause only when its error
chain is safe to show publicly. Otherwise the cause stays internal and callers

pub struct AuthoringIdentity { /* private fields */ }
One binding-safe semantic identity returned by the public façade.

Equality preserves the compiler’s complete semantic key, including its
reference scope. The three serialized fields are a readable description,
not a reconstructible complete key or authority: equal descriptions need
not identify equal semantic subjects. Bindings retain the opaque identity
separately. The identity itself has no compilation-generation affinity;
query continuations must retain their exact owning compilation separately.

pub struct AuthoringOccurrencePage { /* private fields */ }
Owned matching occurrences and bounded scan progress.

An empty page can be incomplete. A byte-deferred matching row is re-inspected
on the next page and returned once; no location is truncated. Inspected counts
describe this retained index, not permission to reveal it to another caller.

Resume a source lookup against the same compilation and query.

Cloning shares the compiler owner; it does not copy the graph. The owner
remains alive until all its handles and cursor copies are dropped. Neither
Debug nor serialization exposes a reconstructible cursor: this type has no
serializer, parser or public constructor. It grants no disclosure authority.

pub struct CodexCommandObservation { /* private fields */ }
SDK-owned view of correlated native evidence, with raw data replaced by identities.

Serialization intentionally exposes the complete observation. Its native
correlation fields do not authenticate a provider, establish command equivalence,
register an operation or consume a tool occurrence. The application owns the
codec and exact observation meaning; the private wrapper leaks no engine type.

Struct CompiledInterfaceIdentity

pub struct CompiledInterfaceIdentity { /* private fields */ }
Version, protocol, target, and publication claims compiled into this interface.

Self::canonical_bytes remains the admitted initial-v1
[SurfaceExecutableIdentityV1] record used for an executable handshake. The
record is only a compiled claim until
PaleApi::verify_current_executable_binding binds it to the executable
selected by an admitted local workspace. In Python and Node hosts, “current
executable” means the interpreter or Node executable, not extension-module
or native-addon bytes. Neither this record nor successful binding
verification proves a complete deployment, resident state, service readiness, or
process health.

pub struct DiagnosticProjection { /* private fields */ }
Unadmitted owner projection for one initial-v1 diagnostic.

This type is intentionally not a wire record. A consumer supplies the
classification it owns and optional presentation candidates, then passes the
value to DiagnosticProjector::project or PaleApi::project_diagnostic.
Both routes use the same application-owned admission path. That path redacts
and bounds text, resolves schema identity, accounts for omissions, validates
the generated contract, and admits cross-field semantics before returning
DiagnosticV1.

The projection carries no retry authority beyond its explicit
DiagnosticRetry and DiagnosticEffectCertainty values. In particular,
a fact, subject, or source label is presentation context, not evidence that an
effect occurred or is safe to repeat.

The rendered implication uses outcome_unknown for
DiagnosticEffectCertainty::OutcomeUnknown and reconcile_first for
DiagnosticRetry::ReconcileFirst.
outcome_unknown⁡⟹reconcile_first⁡,reconcile_first⁡⇏outcome_unknown⁡.\operatorname{outcome\_unknown}\Longrightarrow\operatorname{reconcile\_first},\qquad\operatorname{reconcile\_first}\nRightarrow\operatorname{outcome\_unknown}.

pub struct EffectiveProfileCompilation { /* private fields */ }
Opaque admitted profile phase retained for bounded inspection.

The handle contains no source bytes and exposes no compiler IR. It proves
portable profile, declared private projection, Package semantics, and
composition admission only. Machine/native realization remains unobserved.



Implementations§
Source§impl EffectiveProfileCompilation


Sourcepub fn authoring_occurrences(
    &self,
    request: AuthoringOccurrencePageRequest,
) -> Result<AuthoringOccurrencePage, ApiError>


Page exact occurrences in this retained profile’s combined source index.

Aliases of this compilation can resume; a fresh compilation cannot, even
with equal semantic coordinates. The identity itself remains reusable.
Results own their locations and roles; cursors share the compiler owner
until dropped. The caller owns permission to disclose the source scope.

§Errors
Returns ApiError before scanning if a continuation’s owner, complete
identity or either raw requested limit differs.





Source§impl EffectiveProfileCompilation


Sourcepub fn inspect_authoring(
    &self,
    request: AuthoringInspectionRequest,
) -> Result<AuthoringInspection, ApiError>


Inspect structural authoring facts across workspace, private, and Package sources.

The effective-profile phase retains only logical labels and exact grammar
selections. Source bytes, syntax trees, provider payloads, and secrets do
not cross this projection.

§Errors
Returns ApiError when the path exceeds its fixed bound or embedded
generated metadata is incoherent. Absent documents and paths remain typed
result states.



Sourcepub fn navigate_authoring(
    &self,
    request: AuthoringNavigationRequest,
) -> AuthoringNavigation


Resolve one source occurrence retained by the effective compiler phase.





Source§impl EffectiveProfileCompilation


Sourcepub fn repository_context(
    &self,
    repository_id: &str,
) -> Result<String, ApiError>


Render the selected repository’s private scope and ordered reading references.

Configured machine paths appear only in this explicit output, never in
the portable files returned by Self::source_guidance. Keep it within
the project’s disclosure scope. No source is read and no host is admitted.

§Errors
Rejects invalid or unselected repositories and incomplete read-only
source bindings. The diagnostic omits private paths and source bodies.



Sourcepub fn source_guidance(
    &self,
    repository_id: &str,
    host: SourceGuidanceHost,
) -> Result<SourceGuidanceProjection, ApiError>


Render Package judgment for a host before a runtime deployment exists.

Uses the retained admitted source owner without rereading source or
observing a machine. The application owns selection, composition, host
layout and refusal semantics. This method performs no write and cannot
be substituted for runtime compilation or operation admission.

§Errors
Returns a structured diagnostic for an invalid or unselected repository,
runtime-dependent selections, or an inconsistent content projection.

Sourcepub fn inspect(
    &self,
    request: EffectiveProfilePageRequest,
) -> EffectiveProfilePage


Project one bounded page from the owned inspection retained at compile time.

This method reveals compiler-owned members and typed differences already
established by the application-owned effective-profile set model. It
does not reparse source, recompute closure, score a configuration, or
construct machine realization. A zero limit selects 64
entries; larger values are capped at 256.



Sourcepub fn explain(
    &self,
    handle: &EffectiveProfileExplanationHandle,
) -> Option<EffectiveProfileExplanation>


Return one bounded explanation retained with this exact compilation.

The opaque handle is meaningful only within the profile coordinates that
produced it. This lookup reparses no source and recomputes no semantic
closure, provider disposition, composition proof, or native state.



Sourcepub fn inspect_effective_authoring(
    &self,
    identity: &AuthoringIdentity,
) -> EffectiveAuthoringInspection


Join one compiler-resolved authoring identity to retained profile facts.

Identities can come from Self::navigate_authoring or
PortableWorkspaceCompilation::navigate_authoring. The identity’s
kind and value select rows from this profile; the result carries this
profile’s coordinates, not the source compilation’s coordinates. An
unmatched identity returns no rows.

The join reads the retained projection. It does not parse editor text,
repeat semantic resolution, or infer machine realization. Results are
capped at 64 rows and report truncation.



Sourcepub fn inspect_effective_authoring_page(
    &self,
    identity: &AuthoringIdentity,
    continuation: Option<&EffectiveAuthoringContinuation>,
    limit: u16,
) -> Result<EffectiveAuthoringPage, ApiError>


Enumerate profile rows associated with one compiler-resolved identity.

This uses the same kind-and-value association as
Self::inspect_effective_authoring. It reads the retained index and
copies only the requested window; it does not scan preceding pages or
recompile source. Zero selects 64 rows; larger limits are capped at 256.

A continuation binds this projection allocation, the full identity
and the raw requested limit. A clone of this compilation can resume
it. A fresh compilation cannot, even when its public coordinates match.
Keep the limit unchanged when resuming: 0 and 64 have the same page
size but are distinct requests. An unmatched identity yields a complete
empty page. Dropping a page or token has no configuration effect.

§Errors
Returns ApiError when the continuation belongs to another retained
projection, authoring identity or requested limit. The diagnostic does
not disclose the mismatched identities.

pub struct LocalAgentCarrierSource { /* private fields */ }
A configured native connection source for either agent host’s SDK attachment.

Each application request uses one fresh authenticated socket. The retained
endpoint directory is rechecked before connecting. Credentials, peer pinning
and response-record checks remain explicit choices of the composing host.
This source discovers no endpoint, creates no keys and retries no payload.



Implementations§
Source§impl LocalAgentCarrierSource


Sourcepub fn load(
    endpoint_configuration: &str,
    caller_credential: &str,
    caller_public_key: [u8; 32],
    resident_public_key: [u8; 32],
) -> Result<Self, LocalAgentCarrierSourceError>


Load explicit protected endpoint and transport-credential files.

Paths are UTF-8 and must pass the native owner-private, no-follow checks.
The credential is a raw 32-byte Ed25519 seed matching the caller pin.
The connection uses operating-system randomness and a 1 MiB frame bound.
This selects no response authority and opens no socket. Custom carriers
use crate::AuthenticatedResidentCarrierSource directly.

§Errors
Refuses unsafe files, invalid endpoint configuration or mismatched credentials.

§continuation: Option<ObservationLensCursor>Continuation when selected subjects may remain.


§completion: ObservationStepCompletionWhether this step exhausted its selected input.


§inspected_subjects: u16Retained subjects examined, including nonmatches.


§copied_string_bytes: u32Variable-length UTF-8 bytes copied into this result.


§causal_path_lookups: u16Causal-path lookups performed by this step.

A lookup is charged before its path passes the causal-step and copied-byte
limits, so the count can include an unreturned subject.


§causal_steps: u16Causal steps copied into this result.


§snapshot_omitted_count: u32Owner facts omitted when the bounded snapshot was constructed.

Sourcepub fn associate_recipient_qualified_profile(
    &self,
    profile: &EffectiveProfileCompilation,
    inspection: &RecipientQualifiedWorkspaceInspection,
) -> Result<Result<ObservationProfileAssociation, ObservationProfileError>, RecipientQualifiedWorkspaceAccessError>


Associate this snapshot with a profile through an admitted inspection owner.

Recipient authority is checked before source or coordinate comparison. A
denial therefore reveals neither source membership nor profile freshness.

§Errors
Returns an authority or aggregate-budget failure. Profile association
refusals remain the inner typed result.



Sourcepub fn associate_profile(
    &self,
    profile: &EffectiveProfileCompilation,
    workspace: &PortableWorkspaceCompilation,
) -> Result<ObservationProfileAssociation, ObservationProfileError>


Associate this exact snapshot with an effective profile.

The profile and workspace must share the snapshot’s admitted source and
the snapshot must carry the same profile, private instance, and
composition coordinates. The returned handle copies no rows or facts.

§Errors
Returns ObservationProfileError when the source is unavailable or
differs, or when the profile generation differs.



Sourcepub fn inspect_profile(
    &self,
    profile: &EffectiveProfileCompilation,
    workspace: &PortableWorkspaceCompilation,
    subject: &ObservationSubject,
    after: Option<&ObservationProfileContinuation>,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_returned: u16,
) -> Result<ObservationProfilePage, ObservationProfileError>


Associate one configured subject with its retained profile rows.

Supply the profile and portable workspace explicitly. Both must share
the snapshot’s original admitted source; a separately admitted equal-byte
workspace does not qualify. Another profile allocation from that source
may qualify when profile, instance and composition coordinates match.
This snapshot and its continuation do not keep the profile alive.

Both limits are in 1..=256. Each call examines at most
maximum_inspected raw rows and copies at most maximum_returned rows.
Nested payloads, provenance keys and caller-retained pages have additional
costs; these limits do not establish aggregate memory or byte bounds.
No source is parsed, state is activated or native evidence inferred.

§Errors
Returns ObservationProfileError for expired/different source, different
coordinates, invalid limits, or a foreign/differently parameterized token.

Sourcepub fn page(

Query one bounded page from this exact handle.

Returns ObservationResynchronization when the continuation belongs

Sourcepub fn delta_from(
    &self,
    prior: &Self,
    request: ObservationDeltaRequest,
) -> ObservationDeltaOutcome


Compare prior with this snapshot and return changes or a recovery instruction.

Use the resume position for the snapshot already applied by the client,
not a ObservationPageCursor from a partially read page sequence.
ObservationDeltaOutcome::Delta contains the complete ordered update:
apply all changes and the successor omitted-fact count before replacing
the client’s cursor with ObservationDelta::to.

CaughtUp requires no changes. Resynchronize and Backpressured
require a fresh snapshot, not a partial delta. Cancelled preserves the
caller’s resume position; it reports cancellation checked before the
comparison, not interruption of work already running. This call compares
retained data and does not subscribe to resident or provider events.



Sourcepub fn causal_path(

Return one retained exact causal path for a subject from this snapshot.

Returns ObservationResynchronization when the selector belongs to a
different admitted generation.

Opaque admitted result of one complete portable compiler invocation.

The handle retains the application-owned one-shot result behind shared
immutable ownership so inspection and planning consume the same admitted
identity. It is explicitly not a resident compiled generation: it has no
generation sequence, journal custody, publication, activation, operation,
provider observation, or native-effect authority.

Whether two handles select one record under the same complete source owner.

This supports exact joins between independently paged entries. It is not
semantic equality or cross-generation correspondence. Equal values or

Sourcepub fn sources(
    &self,
    after: Option<&OrganizationSourceCursor>,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_returned: u16,
    maximum_copied_bytes: u32,
) -> Result<OrganizationSourcePage, ApiError>


Query the existing exact record/source owner without recompilation.

Raw limits are 1..=256. The additional copy budget limits UTF-8 payload
of returned labels and path fields before using the existing occurrence
projection. It excludes vector capacity, numeric path steps, opaque
cursor metadata and the retained compilation. No source text is copied.
An empty named page may continue; unmapped means no exact mapping, not
absence of source. Changing record or raw limits rejects continuation.

§Errors
Invalid limits/custody precede copying. Copy-budget exhaustion publishes
no result or advanced cursor; the caller still owns its original cursor.

pub struct PaleApi { /* private fields */ }
Immutable API handle for Pale’s checked contracts and built-in computations.

Construction verifies the complete embedded contract registry and computation
catalog. The handle holds no filesystem, process, network or provider access,
and no permission to install, activate or perform effects. With native-local,
explicit method calls can create internal adapters for local checks and writes
within their declared limits. Those adapters and machine paths never become part
of the handle’s public state.

This effect-free boundary gives an interface a typed structural identity

authenticated resident attachment, current authority, production signing
and anti-rollback custody, and a separately qualified HTTPS carrier.

§Errors
Returns ApiError when the record reference is invalid, the bytes are
absent, non-canonical, outside the selected contract, carry the wrong
schema identity or digest, or describe an operation other than

use pale_sdk::{PaleApi, NativeActionRequest};

let api = PaleApi::new()?;

Sourcepub fn project_diagnostic(
    &self,
    projection: DiagnosticProjection,

Sourcepub fn admit_diagnostic(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<DiagnosticV1, ApiError>


Admit untrusted initial-v1 diagnostic bytes through the complete boundary.

Admission applies strict duplicate-free JSON parsing, the generated
diagnostic.v1 schema, typed decoding, and the semantic invariants that
JSON Schema cannot express. The returned fields remain private.

§Examples
Diagnostics emitted by another façade call re-enter through the same
byte boundary used by non-Rust consumers:


use pale_sdk::PaleApi;

let api = PaleApi::new()?;
let failure = match api.contract_schema("not-registered.v1") {
    Ok(_) => return Err("unexpected registered schema".into()),
    Err(failure) => failure,
};
let admitted = api.admit_diagnostic(failure.diagnostic().canonical_bytes())?;
assert_eq!(admitted.code(), failure.diagnostic().code());

§Errors
Returns ApiError when the input exceeds the bounded ingress size or
fails any stage of diagnostic admission. The error preserves the typed
source while presenting a separately admitted diagnostic.

Sourcepub fn settle_local_materialization_run(
    &self,
    run: &mut LocalMaterializationAdmittedRun,
) -> Result<LocalMaterializationRunResult, ApiError>


Apply, adopt, or remove local repository files according to an admitted run.

This method writes files; it is not a preview. It executes the admitted
repository plans, updates their ownership records and any planned local
Git-exclude protection, and records receipts. Declared deferred effects
remain outside this transaction.

The run must still be prepared. Before changing repository files, this
method verifies the current executable against the admitted binding,
creates the evidence directory if absent, and checks every receipt slot
and the run-result capacity under one retained lock. Evidence preparation
can itself change directories, lock files, or the prior run summary.

Repositories are processed in order. For each, file changes are visible
before its exact immutable receipt is published. Publication precedes
commit, which keeps those changes and releases in-process recovery state.
An absent or colliding receipt publication triggers restoration of the
repository and planned machine-local files; coordination lock files and
their parent directories may remain. Uncertain publication instead keeps
the changed files for reconciliation. Recovery does not span a process
crash, and the run is not workspace-wide atomic.

A target failure stops later repositories without undoing earlier
successes. Check LocalMaterializationRunResult::outcome even on Ok.

§Errors
Returns ApiError for an invalid run phase or failed executable-binding
or evidence checks before repository effects; diagnostics distinguish any evidence
preparation effects. Failed restoration or uncertain target publication
requires reconciliation, not replay. A retained unknown target can be
inspected through Self::inspect_local_materialization_reconciliation.

Run-summary construction or publication can also fail after target outcomes
are confirmed. That error does not undo those outcomes or justify repeating
repository effects merely to obtain the summary.

§Errors

fails, or trusted ownership cannot be established.

pub struct PortableWorkspaceComparison { /* private fields */ }
Opaque, verified comparison of two admitted portable workspaces.

This handle retains both immutable semantic owners and the exact derivation
receipt rebuilt from them. It is not a resident generation diff and carries
no runtime state, provider observation, native consequence, or effect
authority. Root and impact queries are paged; causal explanation returns one
deterministic witness from the receipt’s existing proof DAG.

Let I be every impact subject, A the affected subjects, and U the
unaffected subjects. They obey the
disjoint-partition and cardinality laws:
I=A∪˙U,∣I∣=∣A∣+∣U∣,Removed<Modified<Added.\mathcal{I}=\mathcal{A}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal{U},\quad |\mathcal{I}|=|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{U}|,\qquad \mathrm{Removed}<\mathrm{Modified}<\mathrm{Added}.

Root selection minimizes (change-kind rank, root digest). The rendered
order assigns ranks Removed, then Modified, then Added, so predecessor
discontinuities cannot be hidden by current-frontier causes. For that root,
witness selection minimizes (path length, complete digest sequence).



Implementations§
Source§impl PortableWorkspaceComparison


Sourcepub fn subjects(
    &self,
    after: Option<&PortableWorkspaceComparisonSubjectCursor>,
    limit: u16,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceComparisonSubjectPage, ApiError>


Enumerate selected subjects in either input, including predecessor-only facts.

This merges bounded ranges of the existing fact maps. Zero selects 64;
requests above 256 cap at 256. The application also caps the UTF-8 bytes
copied from subject identity fields and resumes before the first subject
that does not fit. No complete union, total count, graph walk, receipt
rebuild or eager value comparison is performed. Every returned subject
exists in at least one input. Self::compare_subject supplies membership
and typed values on demand; Self::impacts remains current-only.

Each page performs two range seeks, at most one merge-key comparison per
returned subject and up to two entry reads per row plus one look-ahead per
side. Look-ahead is charged again on resume. Subject identity string bytes
have a separate fixed page ceiling. Range-seek work, canonical encoding
bytes and the retained compilation owners are not measured by that ceiling.
Results copy selected identities, summary and output bytes. They retain
compilations through shared ownership, without copying graphs or source bodies.

Continuations bind the ordered input pair, receipt and unchanged raw limit.
A missing cursor starts a new enumeration. Supplied-input custody is not
recipient authority and does not expose every unselected source occurrence.

§Errors
A mismatched pair, receipt or raw limit produces an input diagnostic before
opening either range. It never silently restarts or skips to a nearby key.

Sourcepub fn compare_subject(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,

The application reads its existing fact indexes and compares the typed
outputs. Dependency impact remains available separately through
Self::impacts and Self::explain. An affected subject can be equal.
No graph traversal, source parsing or native observation occurs here.
Work includes two indexed lookups, key and value comparison, and copying
and encoding the selected subject and up to two outputs.



Sourcepub fn compare_subject_selector(

A valid subject absent from both compilations is a successful result.



Sourcepub fn explain(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceExplanation, ApiError>


Explain one subject previously projected by this or another comparison.

For an affected subject, the result contains one shortest root-to-target
path. Root class order is rendered on Self, then root digest, so a
predecessor-only discontinuity is not hidden. Equal-length paths use
their complete node-digest sequence. The result never pretends that a
predecessor-only node exists in the current DAG, and other causal roots
may also reach the target.

§Errors
Returns ApiError only if the already-admitted proof contradicts its
exact comparison owners or causal invariants.



Sourcepub fn explain_selector(
    &self,
    selector: PortableWorkspaceSubjectSelector,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceExplanation, ApiError>


Admit one transport-neutral selector and explain its causal subject.

Leaves pass the closed selector unchanged so this API boundary remains
the sole owner of compound-identity admission and its diagnostic.

§Errors
Returns ApiError when a selector member violates the workspace
identity grammar or when the admitted proof contradicts its owners.

Sourcepub fn contributing_roots(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,
    after: Option<&PortableWorkspaceContributingRootsCursor>,
    limit: u16,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceContributingRootsPage, ApiError>


Page the verified change roots that contribute to one current subject.

Zero selects 64 roots; requests above 256 are capped. Continuations bind
the exact prior/current compilation pair, receipt, full subject and raw
requested limit. Even normalization-equivalent limits must match.

The application reads the retained contribution list, not a new graph
traversal. Each page performs one subject lookup, up to the returned
limit of root lookups, and the existing current-fact lookup for each
added/modified root. It copies selected root/fact payloads and parent
summary, then canonicalizes once. This is not a byte, time or aggregate
memory bound. Retained compilations are shared, not copied.

No recipient authority, renderer state, or native observation is admitted.
Existing explanation selection and value comparison remain separate.

§Errors
Rejects a foreign or stale input pair, receipt, full subject or raw limit.
An impossible retained offset is an internal failure, never completion.

grants no recipient disclosure authority.

Sourcepub fn correspond_organization_record(
    &self,
    selected_side: OrganizationComparisonSide,
    selected: &OrganizationRecordHandle,
    after: Option<&OrganizationCorrespondenceCursor>,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_copied_bytes: u32,
) -> Result<OrganizationCorrespondence, ApiError>


Locate an exact selected organization record in the other compilation.

The retained comparison already established the pair’s existing proof
and compatibility requirements. This result is relative to that pair;
matching keys never permit substitution of source-owner handles.
Uses application-owned canonical keys, not labels, source positions or
shallow SDK row equality. Changed binding intervals are different keys;
a stable explicit relation ID can have changed values. Source queries use
the independently retained selected and other handles. No unmapped source
is replaced with a guessed occurrence or proof.

The visit limit is 1..=256; copied UTF-8 payload is independently bounded
by MAX_ORGANIZATION_COPY_BYTES. At most one complete matching record
is compared by its existing typed equality. Its nested work is bounded by
admitted record limits, not the visit/output-copy budgets. This does not
bound retained compilation memory, metadata allocation or elapsed time.
This query grants no disclosure, rendering or native-operation authority.

§Errors
Rejects a different exact owner, pair, direction, selected record or raw

pub struct PortableWorkspaceCompilation { /* private fields */ }
Opaque admitted handle for one portable workspace universe.

This handle is neither the complete one-shot Package compilation nor a
resident compiled generation. It retains only the admitted path-free
workspace universe; source bytes were consumed and dropped before return.



Implementations§
Source§impl PortableWorkspaceCompilation


Sourcepub fn source_subject(
    &self,
    request: AuthoringNavigationRequest,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceSourceInspection, ApiError>


Read the compiler subject directly named at one source location.

Uses the retained index without parsing text or inferring identity from
labels. A captured but unadopted definition can return Unselected.
Policy, import and extension provenance must use their own proof subjects;
this method does not turn nearby declarations into those records.

The result retains the exact compilation, including captured occurrences
outside selected proof. An editor must also retain its own generation.
Neither the source occurrence nor selected membership grants disclosure
permission or establishes native readiness.

§Errors
Returns the existing authoring diagnostic when the path exceeds
super::AUTHORING_PATH_SEGMENT_LIMIT.



Sourcepub fn subject_occurrences(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,
    after: Option<&AuthoringOccurrencePageCursor>,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_returned: u16,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceSubjectOccurrences, ApiError>


Page source occurrences that directly name a full compiler-proof subject.

The application determines both membership and matches. Every inspected
occurrence counts toward work, including nonmatches; a candidate lookup
is performed for each. Zero selects 64 and values above 256 are capped.
Row limits combine with a fixed copied-string ceiling. Neither bounds
elapsed time or retained compilation memory.

Resume on this exact compilation with the same subject and both raw
limits. Identity-navigation cursors are not subject-mapping cursors, even
if the two queries happen to return identical locations. Empty incomplete
pages must be resumed to establish exhaustion. This supplied-input query
does not admit a recipient or filter disclosure.

§Errors
Returns the existing authoring continuation diagnostic before scanning
when the owner, query kind, full subject or either raw limit differs.



Sourcepub fn authoring_occurrences(
    &self,
    request: AuthoringOccurrencePageRequest,
) -> Result<AuthoringOccurrencePage, ApiError>


Page exact occurrences of a compiler identity in this retained workspace.

An identity may originate in another compilation; a continuation may not.
A fresh compilation with identical digests is still a different cursor
owner. Results copy only locations and roles; cursors share owner custody.
The caller remains responsible for the permitted source-disclosure scope.

§Errors
Returns ApiError before scanning if a continuation’s owner, complete
identity or either raw requested limit differs.

Resolve one admitted source occurrence through the canonical linker.

Sourcepub fn inspect_subject(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,
    after: Option<&PortableWorkspaceSubjectInspectionCursor>,
    input_limit: u16,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_returned: u16,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceSubjectInspection, ApiError>


Inspect one subject’s fact, direct inputs and source evidence without recompiling.

The application owns selection and section consistency. Zero limits use
its 64-row defaults and each is capped at 256. Completed sections are not
restarted; an empty source page may still require continuation. The root,
owner coordinates and optional record anchor repeat so every page is usable.

Resume with this exact compilation, full subject and all three raw limits.
Equal digests or a fresh identical compilation cannot substitute for it.
Each result, including terminal/unselected results, retains the exact owner.
Graph data are shared; root/input facts, source locations and encoded bytes
are copied. Dependency and source counters report their actual copied
string bytes. Source bytes include the occurrence page and any repeated
record anchor; they do not bound time or aggregate retained memory.
This supplied-input query neither admits recipients nor authorizes disclosure.

A mismatched continuation is rejected before either query. Application
position or membership failures map to canonical internal diagnostics.
Unselected subjects and missing source evidence are successful results.

§Panics
Panics if the application violates its 256-candidate source-scan cap and
returns an inspected count that does not fit the public 16-bit count.

string fields. The first whole step that would exceed either ceiling is left
for the existing continuation; no causal fact is truncated. The repeated root,
fixed storage, canonical encoding, retained graph and caller-accumulated pages
are not included. This does not filter disclosure, observe a resident, infer
impact, or calculate a renderer layout.

§Errors
Rejects a continuation from another owner, subject or raw limit. Internal
position inconsistency is a separate diagnostic, never an empty result.





Source§impl PortableWorkspaceCompilation


Sourcepub fn direct_dependents(
    &self,
    subject: &PortableWorkspaceSubject,
    after: Option<&PortableWorkspaceDependentCursor>,
    maximum_inspected: u16,
    maximum_returned: u16,
) -> Result<PortableWorkspaceDependentPage, ApiError>


Find direct consumers of one selected compiler fact without a reverse index.

The application scans retained nodes in proof-digest order. Each inspected
candidate costs one unit even when it has no inputs or does not match.
Zero selects 64 for each independent limit; values above 256 cap at 256.
An empty page can remain incomplete. Resume with this exact compilation,
full subject and both unchanged raw limits; absence of a cursor starts a
new scan, not an implicit continuation of a completed result.

The root fact repeats. Results copy selected typed facts and encoded bytes
while retaining the compiler owner. Candidate and row limits combine with
the fixed application-owned aggregate input-comparison ceiling. Reaching
any ceiling leaves a continuation and never skips its next candidate.
These bounds do not limit elapsed time, encoded bytes or accumulated
retained memory. This is a supplied-input query, not recipient admission
or transitive impact.

§Errors
A foreign owner, subject or raw limit produces a canonical input diagnostic
before scanning. An impossible retained position is an internal diagnostic.

Selected compiler fact and a page of its direct proof inputs.

A missing root means the subject is absent. A present root with no inputs
is different: it is a known fact with no direct proof dependencies. Neither
condition describes provider readiness or native execution. Edges point
from each input fact to this root; they do not imply transitive reachability.

pub struct PortableWorkspaceDependentPage { /* private fields */ }
Selected compiler fact and direct consumers found within one scan budget.

Root absence means unselected. A selected root can have no consumers, and
an empty page can be incomplete. Every result retains its exact compiler
owner, including terminal and unselected results. Clones copy projected
values and bytes but share that owner; no graph or source body is copied.

Source§impl PortableWorkspaceDependentPage


Sourcepub fn workspace_id(&self) -> &str


Workspace identity from the compilation actually queried.



Sourcepub fn principal_universe_digest(&self) -> &str


Principal-relative universe identity of that compilation.



Sourcepub fn semantic_ir_digest(&self) -> &str


Semantic-IR identity, not a transferable exact-input handle.



Sourcepub fn admission_evidence_digest(&self) -> &str


Owner-admission evidence used by the producing compilation.



Sourcepub const fn subject(&self) -> &PortableWorkspaceSubject


Full subject whose direct consumers were requested.



Sourcepub const fn root(&self) -> Option<&PortableWorkspaceCausalStep>


Repeated selected fact, or none when the subject is unselected.



Sourcepub fn dependents(&self) -> &[PortableWorkspaceCausalStep]


Consumers in the compiler’s node-digest order.

Each consumer uses the root as a direct input under its own derivation
rule. This does not claim transitive impact or runtime causation.



Sourcepub const fn inspected(&self) -> usize


Candidate nodes examined, including leaves and nonmatches.



Sourcepub const fn input_digest_comparisons(&self) -> usize


Actual comparisons within candidate input searches; root lookup is excluded.

This mechanical count can vary with the standard library implementation.
It is not semantic identity, generation membership or causal evidence.



Sourcepub const fn is_complete(&self) -> bool


Whether the selected root’s candidate scan is exhausted, or it is unselected.



Sourcepub const fn continuation(&self) -> Option<&PortableWorkspaceDependentCursor>


Next candidate position with its exact owner and query custody.



Sourcepub fn belongs_to(&self, compilation: &PortableWorkspaceCompilation) -> bool


Check exact retained compilation custody, not matching digests or authority.



Sourcepub fn canonical_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] ⓘ


Canonical projection computed once, without encoding the opaque cursor.

The bytes include mechanical scan counts but cannot reconstruct compiler
custody or authorize disclosure. Existing canonicalization still creates
temporary JSON values; once-only encoding does not mean zero allocation.

A well-formed full identity for a compiler-proof subject.

Obtain a subject from compiler results or validate a typed selector with
Self::try_from. Valid syntax does not prove that any compilation selects
the subject. Membership and value comparison remain separate queries.
Private storage preserves compound identities without joining them into text.

pub struct PortableWorkspaceSubjectInspection { /* private fields */ }
Owned fact and source evidence from one exact retained compilation.

Selected membership, source matches and an optional owning record anchor are
separate observations. Terminal and unselected results retain the owner too;
equal semantic digests do not imply equal captured-input custody. Clones copy
projected values/bytes and share the immutable compilation until last drop.
This result grants no permission to disclose source or execute an operation.

pub struct RecipientQualifiedWorkspaceInspection { /* private fields */ }
Recipient-qualified access to one exact retained workspace compilation.

The application issues the admission object. The SDK only verifies that it
belongs to the same retained compilation and projects admitted results. This
type accepts no recipient fields, authority tokens, or callbacks. Every query,
including every continuation, returns to the application authority owner.
Live acquisition remains unavailable until the authenticated resident route
can return this opaque handle; callers cannot create or self-grant one.

pub struct ResidentAttachment { /* private fields */ }
Connection handle for a resident whose authentication the caller supplies.

The trusted calling application supplies the connection configuration or
factory. Operation and observation attachments also require independent
checks for signed records; a hook-only attachment exposes neither. This
handle discovers no endpoint, opens no resident store
and retries no request. A failed request can close its connection; a later,
separately issued request may ask the factory for one fresh connection.

Configure a read-only handle using the caller’s connection and response checks.

The connection factory chooses the endpoint and authenticates the peer.
The response checker verifies signatures, authority changes and protection
against rollback. This function opens no connection and sends no request.
Observe calls run one at a time; this handle cannot start or change operations.

§Errors
Returns ResidentAttachmentBuildError::ZeroTimeout when call_timeout
is zero and ResidentAttachmentBuildError::DeadlineOverflow when the
timeout cannot be represented as a monotonic deadline.



Sourcepub fn provision_operations(
    carrier_source: Box<dyn AuthenticatedResidentCarrierSource>,
    call_timeout: Duration,
    response_admission: Arc<dyn ResidentResponseAdmission>,
) -> Result<Self, ResidentAttachmentBuildError>


Configure a handle for resident operations using the caller’s connection and checks.

The caller asserts that each supplied resident serves Observe, Invoke,
Consult, Delegate, Cancel, and repository-hook frames. The SDK does not
negotiate or infer those capabilities. Connection and response checks have the same requirements
as Self::provision_observation.

§Errors
Returns ResidentAttachmentBuildError::ZeroTimeout when call_timeout
is zero and ResidentAttachmentBuildError::DeadlineOverflow when the
timeout cannot be represented as a monotonic deadline.





Source§impl ResidentAttachment


Sourcepub fn load_hook_configuration(
    path: &str,
) -> Result<Self, ResidentHookConfigurationError>


Load an explicitly selected, owner-private JSON hook configuration.

The closed document has schema_version: 1, absolute
endpoint_configuration and caller_credential paths, two 32-byte arrays
named caller_public_key and resident_public_key, and timeout_ms in
1..=30000. The endpoint file uses the native adapter’s endpoint format;
the credential is a separately provisioned raw Ed25519 seed matching the
caller pin. Files must pass native owner-private, no-follow checks.

No connection opens here. Nothing is searched, generated, installed or
repaired. File custody does not protect against other same-UID processes
or backups. This attachment permits only blocking hook replies; it has
no operation or observation authority and provides no host enforcement.

§Errors
Refuses unsafe files, invalid documents, mismatched credentials or timeouts.

pub struct ResidentOperationObservationPreflight { /* private fields */ }
An observation request that passed the SDK’s checks before connection.

Those checks cover canonical formatting, the public contract, embedded digests,
the operation.observe capability and agreement with the operation locator.
Signature verification, resident selection, peer authentication, session and
operation recovery, and permission to disclose data remain separate checks.
This value grants no retry or permission to perform work.

Interfaces can reject malformed input before finding a resident connection.
The private state keeps a checked request from being constructed as if it were
proof of resident authority.
