Reuse shared utilities without assuming a portable host
The provider router, preflight payloads, language guard, claim labels, scale guard, idempotency utilities and artifact hashing can serve another lane. Flask's app factory, the OASIS runner bridge, engine services and the Graphiti/Neo4j integration depend on this host and need adaptation elsewhere.
A catalog entry proves discovery, not successful execution. Keep unsupported capabilities explicit and preserve the guardrail distinctions in any new interface.

RawFish UI contract
Build cockpit screens from shared tokens and primitives. Screen files arrange those components; the components own color, type, spacing and state. Use this contract when changing the prototype UI. Its rules do not choose the fresh rebuild's design.
The six rules
Each rule exists because a screen built without a shared system breaks it in a predictable way. The numbers are stable: code and gates cite them.
1. Spacing belongs to a primitive, so text never collides
Two pieces of text never sit as adjacent inline nodes. Every title and caption, or label and value, lives inside a primitive (LabelRow, a Panel header) whose flex or grid gap owns the spacing. If two texts touch, the primitive is missing. Typical failures: a card title and its caption running together as one line, helper prose injected into the step list, a label column overlapping a message column, a strip clipped at the top of a panel.
2. State is a variant of a primitive, never a rewrite of its label
A locked or disabled control is dimmed to --t4 and gives its reason in an adjacent chip or a title tooltip. Nothing writes the state into content: no tab labelled "UPLOAD DISABLED", no gate reason printed inside the primary button, no unreachable step drawn struck through. text-decoration: line-through is banned everywhere. A disabled control without a visible reason is a defect.
3. One concept has one control, rendered once
A concept is rendered once, by one primitive. If it is echoed elsewhere, the echo is the same primitive in the same variant. Showing a source choice as both a console tab and a chip, or readiness as both full-width rows and chips, breaks this rule.
4. Colour carries meaning, and there are two chromatic tokens
--accent means the active item or the primary action, and nothing else. --danger means an error or a halt, and nothing else. Identity and data are shown with weight, opacity and position, never hue, so lanes and cohorts get no colours of their own and the accent is never used for emphasis. The one exception is --target, a yellow flash used only to highlight a linked target and fading in 900 milliseconds.
5. Type has fixed roles
Noto Sans is for human text: titles, body and buttons. JetBrains Mono is for machine text only: numbers, counters, identifiers, hashes, phase and status strings, the console and step numbers. Fonts are set only through the --f-* role tokens, and both families are self-hosted. A raw font-size: or font: with a literal pixel value in a screen file fails the build.
6. The shell owns density
The top bar carries the brand, the step spine and one mono context line (lane, phase, environment), nothing else. Helper prose lives in the step's panel body. Run metrics live in the console's status line. A pane exists only when it has content: the graph pane mounts only once a graph exists, and the console is a 34 pixel line unless a run is streaming.
The order of work
The steps below are done in this order. A screen counts as done only when the steps before it hold.
Step 1. The token sheet is the only source of paint
The token block in frontend/src/styles/rawfish.css is the single source of truth. It defines exactly these tokens, and no other colour, shadow, radius, type or spacing tokens exist. The --rf-* namespace is not used anywhere.
:root {
  /* colour: the only chromatic tokens in the product */
  --accent: #FF5722;
  --danger: #B23A2E;

  /* surfaces and ink */
  --ink: #141410;
  --paper: #ffffff;
  --bg: #f1f1ee;
  --line: rgba(20,20,15,0.14);
  --line-strong: rgba(20,20,15,0.30);

  /* text tiers: hierarchy comes from opacity, not new greys */
  --t1: #141410;
  --t2: rgba(20,20,16,0.60);
  --t3: rgba(20,20,16,0.42);
  --t4: rgba(20,20,16,0.26);

  /* families */
  --sans: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, sans-serif;  /* human text */
  --mono: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;         /* machine text only */

  /* type roles: the only legal font declarations */
  --f-display: 600 23px/1 var(--sans);       /* step title */
  --f-title:   600 15px/1.2 var(--sans);     /* card or panel title */
  --f-body:    400 13.5px/1.55 var(--sans);
  --f-btn:     600 12px/1 var(--sans);
  --f-label:   600 10px/1 var(--mono);       /* uppercase, letter-spacing 1px */
  --f-value:   600 12px/1 var(--mono);
  --f-num:     600 30px/1 var(--mono);       /* stat numerals */

  /* spacing scale */
  --s1: 4px; --s2: 8px; --s3: 12px; --s4: 16px; --s5: 20px; --s6: 26px;
}

The sheet also carries the --target flash from rule 4 and a few layout measures used by the shell (--console-h, --control-h, --dock-w, --dock-w-wide).
Step 2. Every visual element is one of the primitives
Each primitive lives in one file under frontend/src/cockpit/primitives/, is imported everywhere it is used, and selects its variants through props. Nothing else may define these styles. A new visual need extends a primitive; it never adds inline style to a screen.
Primitive	Anatomy and props	Rules	
Panel	optional header (title in --f-label, plus meta) and a body	hairline --line, radius 0, no shadow; the header owns its padding and gap	
Card	a Panel without a header, padding --s4	none beyond Panel	
Chip	variant: default, accent or caution	one padding (3px 8px), --f-label; caution uses a --danger glyph, not a new background	
Button	role: primary, default or quiet; optional reason	a disabled button requires reason, shown beside it (chip or tooltip), never inside the label	
LabelRow	label (--f-label, --t3) and value (--f-value)	the only way to render a caption and value pair; owns the gap	
Meter	label, value, percentage	a 5 to 9 pixel track in --line; fill --t1 for data, --accent only for a budget or the primary item	
SentimentTrack	a value from -1 to +1	a position on the track with a centre tick; monochrome	
StepHeading	number (mono, accent), title (--f-display), hint (mono, no wrap)	identical on every step	
StepSpine	steps, each with state: done, active, reachable, locked or halted	locked is --t4 with a title reason; active is accent with a 2 pixel underline; halted uses --danger; never struck through	
Console	a 34 pixel mono status line that expands into a log	expands only while a run streams; the log is a fixed-width grid of time, tag and message	
Step 3. The shell fixes where everything goes
The top bar holds the brand, the StepSpine and one mono context line. The active step owns the work surface: its dock is 484 pixels wide, or 720 pixels when the step is dense, and on Scenario it stands alone. The graph pane (300 pixels, with a hairline on its left) mounts only when a graph exists, and never on Scenario. The Console stays collapsed unless a run is streaming.
The six steps (scenario, build, cohorts, preflight, simulate, findings) are each data plus a composition of primitives. A step file may declare layout only (grid, flex, gap and width using the --s* scale); it may not declare paint (colour, background, border, font, shadow or radius).
When a run halts, the spine marks the step as halted, the console shows the error with a hint on how to fix it, and the step offers "duplicate as draft" so the operator can edit a copy. A frozen field says the same thing in its reason.
Step 4. Run the static interface checks
Every gate passes before screen work counts as done. process/check_ui_contract.sh runs them from the repository root as gates U1 to U10: type only from role tokens (U1), no raw hex colours (U2), no shadows (U3), radius 0 everywhere (U4), no strikethrough (U5), no state words in labels (U6), no --rf-* tokens (U7), no raw colour functions outside the token file (U8), no inline paint bindings (U9), and screens that declare layout only (U10, a ratchet toward zero against process/ui_paint_baseline.txt). The core of the first six, as plain shell:
# paint may only come from tokens and primitives
grep -rn "font-size\|font:" frontend/src --include='*.vue' | grep -v "var(--f" | grep -v tokens && exit 1
grep -rnE "#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}" frontend/src --include='*.vue' | grep -v tokens && exit 1
grep -rn "box-shadow" frontend/src | grep -v "none" && exit 1
grep -rn "border-radius" frontend/src | grep -vE "border-radius: ?0" && exit 1
# state is never written into content
grep -rn "line-through" frontend/src && exit 1
grep -rniE "disabled\"?>|DISABLED<" frontend/src --include='*.vue'   # review: no state words in labels

These static checks enforce the listed source constraints. They do not establish readable spacing or that each concept appears as one control. Review the rendered layout too: visual acceptance takes a screenshot of each step at 1280 by 800 and checks six things:
The StepHeading block is pixel-identical in size and position on every step.
Every button is one of the three roles, and every chip one of the three variants.
No two text nodes sit side by side without a parent that owns the gap.
At most two chromatic colours are visible on any screen: the accent and, when there is an error, danger.
No disabled control lacks a visible reason beside it.
The console is at most 40 pixels tall unless a run is streaming, and there is no graph pane on Scenario.
This is the proof-of-concept UI manual. The fresh rebuild's target and this tree's current departures are separated in the product contract, and the current codebase is described in the architecture.

Guardrails
RawFish rejects some operations and attaches warnings to others. A rejected request stops the operation; a warning changes how its result should be read. Keep that difference visible when integrating a lane or changing report handling.
What blocks an operation
The prototype rejects invalid request, catalog, report and manifest schemas; a catalog missing its lane_manifest; an unavailable selected provider; scale above the active cap; and an idempotency key reused with a different body. Unsafe artifact ids and path traversal are refused too.
During generation, the report must pass its schema and language check before persistence proceeds. These checks run at particular boundaries, not continuously over every saved file.
What changes the interpretation
Numeric and comparative checks can expose gaps or demote claims. Driver attribution is a co-occurrence hint rather than a cause. Missing evidence, field-validation questions and surrogate sensitivity caveats need to stay with the result they qualify. An unknown external model price is reported as unavailable.
Do not turn one of these warnings into a guarantee or hide it behind a successful response.
Stored reports need different care
Stored JSON reads validate the lane's schema but do not repeat the language check or verify the recorded digest and embedded run identity. JSON, Markdown and metadata are separate writes, so a readable JSON file can survive a later publication failure. Integrations must preserve generation errors rather than treating HTTP 200 as completed report publication. Report storage explains that boundary.
Creator has another limit: its deterministic runner provides no executed conversation, and its generator does not consume the evidence catalog. A schema-valid report and its claim labels cannot create that missing support. The findings guide explains how readers should use the output.
Check source rules and runtime behavior separately
Static process gates reject stale routes and ids, external font fetches, empty statistical manifests and wording that makes an external provider mandatory. Check a change lists the commands. Runtime tests must exercise each lane's rejection and warning paths separately.
The rebuild contract requires stronger report read-back and settings guards than this prototype implements.

RawFish
RawFish rehearses what could follow from a decision before anyone commits to it, while it can still be changed: the problem is seeing where a decision could lead, and how it could go wrong, before it is made. In RawThoughts' one system it asks the counterfactuals, what could follow if a direction were taken, and it is a local-first simulation product. This repository contains its reference prototype: a Flask backend, Vue cockpit, three decision lanes and model-generated reports. The rebuild's design has three callable layers, a swarm simulation, an intervention and counterfactual comparison, and the lanes that supply each domain's questions (layers); this prototype is not layered that way. It declares baseline, counterfactual and sensitivity variants and compares saved statistical settings; the comparison layer is not built and gets its own contract. The product is planned for a fresh rebuild; this code provides examples and lessons rather than the rebuild's starting codebase.
Important

Creator does not run an agent swarm. Its runner writes a deterministic completion marker. A separate model call generates report text without using the evidence catalog or cohort statistical settings. Generated reactions are hypotheses, not observed audience behavior.

Target rebuild product contract
Use this contract to design the fresh RawFish rebuild: one cockpit, three lanes, explicit model choice and evidence-linked reports. It describes intended behavior, not a working replacement. For the current prototype, start with using RawFish or its architecture.
Features outside the target remain absent until their behavior is defined and implemented; disabled placeholders do not make them available.
Target product surface
RawFish has two browser routes:
/, Launch;
/run/:runId?, the cockpit, for a draft or a saved run.
Everything else about a run is state within the cockpit: step= selects Scenario, Build, Cohorts, Preflight, Simulate or Findings, and mode=read|ask|data selects the Findings modes, with data shown as Analysis. Report, chat, compare and sensitivity are cockpit states, not routes. Unknown query values and keys are rejected rather than guessed at, and a link never carries scenario text, source material, credentials or configuration. Share copies a link to a saved run and its current step, and grants nothing by itself.
Lane ids are creator, internal_policy and public_policy. Backend lane traffic flows through /api/sim/use-cases/<lane_id>/....
Target lane catalog
Every registered lane returns a catalog with a required, nested lane_manifest. The manifest publishes the lane's cockpit slots, scenario fields, cohort pack, connector capabilities, evaluation ids, report sections, caveats and the reference to its statistical manifest. The statistical manifest is the only list of the lane's statistical controls; a control that does not apply to a lane is omitted. Pasted text is the only admitted source.
Target provider router
RawFish supports three provider modes:
local_ollama
local_openai_compatible
external
Local modes do not require external provider credentials. The first working route is local Ollama. External mode requires an explicit provider, model and key selected when launching that run; it is never an automatic fallback. The preflight meter returns the scale cap, token estimate, provider readiness, model id, latency and, in external mode, the cost estimate, or cost_unavailable when the price is unknown. The provider chosen for a run is kept with it and used for its report.
Target report posture
Reports describe simulated responses and hypotheses. Forecasting real-world outcomes requires empirical validation of the claim; generated personas are not a sample of a real population. Every claim carries one of five labels (simulated observation, inference, grounded in source, assumption, needs validation) and must point to evidence of a kind its label allows, or it is demoted to "needs validation". Every report passes the language guard before it is kept and again whenever it is read; the guard proves only that its lexical rules ran. Every report states that its content was generated by AI personas in a simulation and is not attributable to any real person. What blocks and what only advises is in guardrails.
Target workbench
Statistical changes go through guarded JSON Patch requests that carry the settings hash the client last read and an idempotency key. Save stores a new revision before the run starts; Save and re-seed forks a new variant run and never changes the base run. Variants, their lineage and the comparison between a base run and a variant are kept as records of their own, and the run's metadata keeps the provider, preflight and statistical state its report was generated from.
Current proof-of-concept departures
When reusing examples from this prototype, account for these differences:
Launch exposes paste, cached, live and graph source markers, and the backend admits all four names in source_context, while the target below admits pasted text only. The markers do not establish working admitted connectors for the other modes.
The backend retains both the generic comparison endpoint and /<use_case_id>/simulation/<sim_id>/statistical-config/compare; the target has one generic comparison surface.
The cockpit is not fully manifest-only: Launch branches on lane id for presets and parser identity, and the run store branches for parser identity, creator-versus-policy scenario payloads and the two policy stakeholder fallbacks. A genuinely distinct new lane therefore needs cockpit work and tests in this tree; the target removes those lane-id branches.
The creator runner writes a deterministic completion marker instead of executing an agent swarm. Its report generator consumes the scenario and segment identities/types, not the evidence catalog or the workbench's cohort statistical settings. Its report can use a real model without becoming evidence of agent interactions or the effect of those settings.
The current Reseed variant control updates the same pre-start run and appends a settings lineage snapshot. It does not fork a separately executable run. The comparison endpoint compares those settings, then reports findings-subject presence without reading and validating both reports. The displayed findings buckets are not a report comparison.
The cockpit supplies an expected hash for Save patch, but the backend accepts patches without it. The seed-only reseed path does not require an expected hash either. Both routes reject starting, running, completed and reported phases, but omit failed from that phase check. The cockpit freezes failed runs too; the API's failed-run mutation gap remains.
Report JSON reads validate the adapter schema without rechecking the language guard, recorded digest or embedded run identity. Report JSON, Markdown and metadata are separate writes; a readable JSON file can survive a later publication failure.
Use the target sections above for the rebuild's requirements. The prototype architecture follows its current calls and stored results. Keep the two versions separate when testing or explaining them.

Run ownership and transitions
These requirements describe the rebuild, not the Flask prototype. The Rust SDK is the common implementation for the standalone application, an embedded host and an optional service. Pale links it as a normal crate dependency, without a RawFish source submodule. Thin Python and TypeScript SDKs expose the same operations.
The run operations check and record each transition. An accepted request creates one run identity. Execution and cancellation check that run's current generation and revision, and retries recover its recorded result. A generation distinguishes a new preparation of the run from an earlier attempt; the revision identifies the state a particular change expects.
The lifecycle below describes the intended behaviour; the protocol's exact state names remain to be defined.
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Received
  Received --> Rejected: permission checks failed
  Received --> Allowed
  Allowed --> Sealed: inputs frozen
  Sealed --> Prepared
  Prepared --> Running
  Running --> Paused: declared pause when operator leaves
  Paused --> Running: permitted resume
  Running --> Completed
  Running --> Failed
  Running --> CancelRequested
  CancelRequested --> Cancelled
  CancelRequested --> Completed: completion won the race
  CancelRequested --> Failed: failure won the race
  CancelRequested --> Reconciling: uncertain commit
  Reconciling --> [*]: recover the owner's recorded state

Accepting the request. A rejected request produces a denial record, without an executable run or use of a source. An accepted request records one run identity with the request's retry key, principal, data controller, optional relationship scope, purpose, instance, generation and expected revision. Repeating the same request returns its existing result. Reusing its key with a changed body, or asking to change a stale revision, must fail.
Fixing the inputs. RawFish freezes the lane manifest, source bundle, packs, scenario, cohorts, statistical settings, provider and runner profiles, permissions, budgets and source revisions together. Changing the lane or any of those inputs requires a new generation or run, which passes the same checks.
Preparing and starting. Preparation checks that the chosen provider, runner and resources can use those fixed inputs. Running begins only when the checked run operations record the execution attempt with the owner: the embedded host or RawFish's standalone/service application. A ready-looking interface, live process or allocated worker alone cannot establish either state. The host supplies the transaction and storage in embedded mode. Before recovery, match provider output and report references to the run, generation, execution attempt and fixed inputs. Read their recorded digests and the owner’s committed state; reject output from a different or superseded attempt.
Finishing or cancelling. The operations check the exact run, generation and revision before its owner commits a terminal state with the artifact, finding and result references. The owner then supplies that record for read-back. Cancellation can lose a race to completion or failure; its reply must report the state that actually committed. Exercise completion and failure winning the cancellation race, duplicate cancellation and late provider output. Only the terminal result committed for this run generation may enter accepted history.
An uncertain commit can require recovery at any step; the diagram draws it once. Recovery reads the owner's record to determine whether the change committed. It never creates a second run to resolve that uncertainty.
The simulation's terminal result, a caller's acceptance, an outside effect, delivery of an event, settlement and the eventual real-world outcome each need their own record and responsible owner. For example, finishing a simulation can produce a deliverable for Weave without establishing that Weave accepted it or that anyone acted on it.
Mode	Who keeps the work and storage	How the result is recorded	
Standalone	RawFish's application owns the run and store.	Its checked operations record execution, findings, cancellation and the terminal result. It works without Pale, a host or another service.	
Embedded crate	The host owns the work, transaction and run storage.	The host calls RawFish's Rust SDK and records results through the agreed operation and storage interfaces. RawFish supplies the simulation behaviour without a parallel store. The host records its own acceptance separately.	
Remote service	The caller owns its operation; RawFish owns a separately identified simulation run.	Each keeps its own commit and recovery record. Delivery, completion of the simulation and the caller's acceptance are recorded separately.	
Every request names the caller, principal, data controller, relationship scope where applicable, purpose and request identity. Run references include the instance, generation and expected revision. The invocation contract establishes who may write each record. Displaying a cockpit in a plugin or iframe, or delivering a message, supplies no additional permission. A host's surrounding work also remains distinct from the simulation's inputs and results.
People use the same cockpit journey, run states, claim labels and unavailable states in every mode. A host follows the shared world and module design without changing what a control or result means. Linking the Rust crate provides embedded operation. Running a child process over an authenticated local socket provides a local service, which needs its own installation, supervision and recovery checks; access to its socket alone grants no permission to operate it. Removing either connection preserves the owners' existing records and independent operation.
A deployment may also choose an event outbox. The run change and its outgoing event are written in the same database transaction, allowing delivery to be retried without inventing another run change. Events sent to Pale's history contain only permitted identifiers, transitions and result references, with no source text or credentials. Standalone RawFish works without this outbox. Receiving an event establishes delivery; the named owner still supplies the underlying result, acceptance or outside-effect record.
Planned Pale operations
These operation names are proposed interfaces; none is implemented yet.
Capability	RawFish's responsibility	
product.rawfish.run.start.v1	Validate one request, create its run and return a run reference and receipt.	
product.rawfish.run.observe.v1	Return permitted lifecycle, artifact, evaluation and terminal references within the request's limits, without exporting the run store.

A provider adapter performs only the declared acquisition, with the acquisition actor, legal entity, data controller, rights holders, source authorities, artifact issuer and custodian evidenced separately. Cockpit state and navigation
The visible phase words are draft, prepared, running, paused, halted, complete and reported. Failed and Cancelled map to halted with their recorded reason. Rejected stays in draft with its reason. Reconciling is a separate label and blocks edits until the owner's state is recovered. A cancellation request is pending until its committed result is known. A halted run offers only its record until a recovery contract exists: no Stop, resume or restart control. A run paused because the operator left under its declared pause policy shows no running light, explains that cause and offers Resume through the pause operation.
An evidence link and its sheet header use the same narrowest applicable scope, for example “3 of 41 acts in round 5 cite this”. The web host records every overlay level in browser history so Back undoes one level. Embedded hosts use the same typed identifiers in their own navigation. Identifiers such as claim:c-03/acts and node:n-18 do not require one fragment mechanism across hosts. Links carry identifiers, not draft contents or permission.
Findings shows Read, Ask and Analysis in its heading's mode switch with the current mode visible. Download report is Read's primary action. Analysis includes one-at-a-time sensitivity only when a real rerun/evaluation supports it; a surrogate explanation cannot establish sensitivity or causation.
Preflight shows a token range with its basis, for example “350,000–470,000 tokens · 212 agents × 16 rounds at this model's last measured rate”. These are illustrative values, not measured RawFish results. Until a rate has been measured it shows “No estimate yet”; an unknown provider price remains unavailable. Enforced budgets are independent of that estimate.
