Migrations run through their own journaled runner
schema/
  V001_core_entities.sql
  V002_workspace_projection_memberships.sql
  V003_context_evidence.sql
  V004_people.sql
  V005_resources.sql

The runner takes the writer fence, stops normal writes, hashes every migration file and reads the exact authoritative branch head and the migrations table; free-form dolt_log messages are diagnostic only. Each migration's identity is its version and file hash, and its manifest also binds the filename, the exact expected prior migration, head and schema digest, the target schema digest, the minimum and maximum Dolt versions and the rollback class; the same version with changed bytes or a mismatched prior state conflicts. The runner creates or resumes the deterministic branch __scope_migration/V###-<file_hash_prefix> from the expected prior head, and its append-only journal records prepared, sql_committed, dolt_committed and verified, each binding its predecessor. prepared commits first; the file runs in one SQL transaction on the branch and appends sql_committed with the measured schema digest; DOLT_COMMIT creates the candidate, the runner resolves the exact ref, commit and tree and appends dolt_committed, verifies schema and data invariants, appends verified and commits; then the authoritative branch advances from the expected prior head to the verified candidate by compare-and-swap or fast-forward. A moved head, an unrelated dirty working set, an unknown ref or a changed file fails closed.
State on restart	What happens	
No journal or branch, and the prior head matches	Create prepared	
prepared, no SQL change	Execute once	
sql_committed with the matching dirty working set	Verify and commit those bytes; never rerun the DDL	
Candidate commit exists, authoritative head still prior	Verify the commit, then compare-and-swap or fast-forward	
Authoritative head equals the verified candidate	Exact replay returns the original migration receipt	
Any hash, schema or ref divergence, or a partial journal	Quarantine and require operator recovery	
On failure only the migration transaction rolls back or the candidate branch is quarantined; unrelated accepted state is never hard-reset, and if the pinned Dolt version cannot prove the branch, working-set, transaction and swap semantics, migration stays disabled. The migration receipt binds the version and file hash, manifest hash, expected prior head and schema, every journal transition, the candidate commit and tree, the measured schema, the prior and new authoritative heads, the runner's fence and the activation time; it is emitted only after the authoritative ref advances, exact replay returns the same bytes, and it stays an internal record. Tests crash the runner before and after every transition, SQL commit, Dolt commit, verification and ref advance, and cover changed-file reuse, skipped versions, a wrong prior schema, an unrelated dirty working set, concurrent runners and exact replay. Source imports never reuse this runner; they have their own journal on Source imports.
Performance limits come from measurement
Each deployment sets its limits only after measuring the exact Scope and Dolt versions, schema, corpus, controller isolation, hardware and concurrency. At minimum it benchmarks warm and cold resolves, durable use and episode admission, import activation, compiler and whole-snapshot build and validation, each route and fusion, atomic activation, old-reader drain, strict and full degradation, full projection rebuild, liveness, readiness and explicit reload, recording p50, p95 and p99 latency, throughput, resident and peak memory, queue depth, and timeout and cancellation behaviour under normal load, contention, degraded dependencies, restart and recovery. Promotion needs headroom above what was observed; meeting a median with no margin in the tail or in memory is a failure, and no figure, such as a sub-millisecond graph walk or a fifty-millisecond resolve, is a threshold until measured and approved. Liveness proves only that the process answers without a dependency read; readiness separately checks the admitted authority and checkpoint, the writer fence, storage and required source frontiers. Structured spans record the operation, profile and exact revisions without secrets, and alerts compare against the admitted profile. Scope makes no model call on its base path, but no model cost is not no cost: latency, CPU, memory, storage and failure amplification are measured where they are owned, and the whole machine's margin is measured idle and loaded with every store and daemon running.
Recovery must be proved before this is called built
For an issued bundle or use receipt that depends on exact historical bytes, retain its immutable revision and digest under the owner's retention rules. Resolve it after a mutable view changes and after its storage location moves. Recovery either reads preserved bytes or rebuilds from the exact saved inputs, configuration and tool revision; compare the result with the original digest and distinguish those routes from different bytes or no result. If exact rebuilding is impossible, retain the original while policy permits and the claim depends on it. Otherwise leave the claim unproved. A digest match establishes content identity; custody, rights and permission to use the restored state need separate checks. Scope determines which revisions remain reconstructible under its accepted frontier and deletion rules.
For an exact serialized bundle, preserve the expected digest and byte count, original carrier, selected members and their order, the selector rule and original key mappings. Distinguish an order recorded at issuance from one recovered later. Reject missing, duplicate or ambiguous selections while retaining legitimate repeated members at their separate positions. Fix the serializer and every byte-affecting option: encoding, escaping, indentation, separators, newline conversion and final newline. Rebuild in isolation using the original sequence rather than filesystem traversal; compare digest and byte count. Test changed order, changed options and missing members. Equal parsed values with different bytes do not prove exact recovery. Where only a checksum is needed and reading is permitted, stream into the digest calculation; keep any inspection copy within the owner's retention and disclosure rules.
Equal bytes shared by several receipts remain separate records. Preserve each occurrence's identity, original locator, revision, digest, length, custody, retention or hold, access scope and captured metadata, including file kind, mode and timestamp precision when needed. Distinguish restored metadata from an observation retained about it, and do not count equal captures as independent evidence. Check permission through the requested occurrence before opening or revealing a shared body or alias. Reconstruct each authorised occurrence separately and compare its bytes and required metadata. Test equal bytes at two locators with different metadata, changed bytes under a familiar locator, forbidden lookup and loss of the shared body. Removing one route must deny that route while preserving independently required retention. Keep storage separate if holds, erasure or recovery promises cannot be honoured independently; retiring a redundant copy needs its owner's decision after all affected recovery routes pass.
Tests must show that killing the process before or after every import, inbox apply, use receipt and episode close leaves either the old revision or the complete new one; that stale writer generations and duplicate owner events change nothing; that losing the graph, the replay ring or the score projections is recovered from accepted records without inventing evidence; that a replaced source keeps the previous generation until the new one validates atomically; that deletion removes only policy-authorised payload, keeps required identity, lineage and tombstones, invalidates dependent bundles and never resurrects on replay; that an unauthorised principal cannot infer hidden nodes through counts, scores, timing, errors, replay gaps, health data or aggregate changes; that optional degradation is visible and critical failure fails closed; that a crash around snapshot publication and activation leaves exactly one active head with pinned readers finishing and rollback reactivating the prior bytes; that deletion, revocation and freshness invalidation reach every dependent snapshot, embedding, affinity feature and cache while deleting only affinity changes no truth; that strict mode loads no model-made artifact and an unavailable route is never an empty success; that vector output, traversal influence and observable isolation meet the declared level; and that governed deletion leaves decisions marked unreconstructible where their inputs are gone. The complete list is on Acceptance tests.
Part of Scope engineering.

Episodes and use
Scope must distinguish sending a context bundle, reading its exact bytes again, a caller reporting that it used them, a model actually receiving them, the work's outcome and the owner's acceptance. Each event needs its own evidence. A receipt for one event cannot establish the others.
The independent contract covers resolving context, reading the same bundle again and recording use reports under either standalone or integrated permission checks. An execution episode connects one run to its selected context variant and to the owner's outcome records. That path requires a concrete run-identity proposal, approval by the responsible owners and their published successor contract; the issuing-owner question remains open below.
The task's owner says how much context the work needs
A context requirement is signed by the owner of the task, never by Scope; Scope owns only its vocabulary and validation, and cannot let work continue by issuing its own requirement. It names the task, one of three classes, the scope, role, purpose and classification ceiling, the required and optional sources with their consistency class and freshness requirement, a token or size budget, and the context variants the task accepts.
Task class	Variants it may accept	Rules	
Context-critical	An exact bundle only	At least one required source; no degradation policy	
Context-enhanced	An exact bundle, or an authorised degraded answer	Degradation only with an immutable degradation policy	
Context-independent	Independence only	No required source; keeps its authority reference	
Source arrays are sorted by source, duplicate-free, and never unbounded when empty. A resolve request tied to execution must be the same as or narrower than the requirement it references; its own query and budget fields cannot widen the signed policy.

Freshness is the owner's word; required context fails closed
At handoff and again when dependent work uses the context, check each required source's owner, role, exact revision and delivered bytes, permitted recipient and purpose. Recheck observed and valid-through times, expected refresh cadence, dependencies, contradictions, deletion and revocation. Selecting, capturing and observing that a recipient received a source are separate facts. A missing, stale, denied or oversized required input holds the dependent decision unless the owner permits a narrower task. Scope first tries a lineage- and genealogy-aware refresh from the source owner. Changed bytes need a newly accepted task association, never silent replacement in the original handoff. Any source repair follows the owner's separate effect and read-back. The task owner's signed requirement binds the permitted degradation policy; that variant still needs its own required acceptance records. The receipt records the actual limitation. Changes to authority, canon or lifecycle count as effects.
Test optional-source omission, one missing required source, selection by the wrong owner, an insufficient budget, a handoff delayed past expiry or revocation and a still-valid handoff. Exercise a refresh with new bytes and the separately admitted successor. For a permitted reduced variant, withhold each required acceptance record and substitute one from another handoff or expired generation. Refuse dispatch when its evidence is missing; failure of the assisted path cannot authorise context-independent work.
Kind of work	If refresh or repair cannot restore the context	
Public, reversible drafting	Continue only as context-enhanced work with a signed degradation policy and an explicit receipt	
Internal analysis with optional context	Continue only under the signed degradation policy, with limitations visible	
Confidential analysis or drafting	Apply the signed degradation policy and disclose its limits. Effects, irreversible disclosure, changes to authority, canon or lifecycle, and native mutation remain outside this degraded path	
Context-critical work	Stop until freshness is restored, including when the work is analysis or drafting	
Confidential, legal, financial, policy, publication or effectful work that requires the missing context	Stop until freshness is restored	
Engineering recovery	Use the pinned repository or workspace evidence the handoff names. A signed context requirement still applies	
Context-independent	Proceed without Scope	
Degradation here covers missing source context. An assisted launch still needs both Scope episode receipts described below.
A bundle is read back as the exact bytes that were bound
Reading a bundle retrieves one already signed bundle; it performs no traversal and cannot substitute a newer one. Work tied to an execution must present the complete execution binding (the episode identity, attempt, authorisation, reservation, fence, handoff, requirement and context-binding hash) as one object, and Scope checks the exact successful reservation, handoff, exact-bundle binding, caller and session scope and bundle signature before returning the bytes. Reads outside execution omit the binding. Scope checks its own grant and request admission in standalone mode and Pale's common request in integrated mode. A partial binding is invalid in either mode. A refresh that changes the bundle needs a new admitted request, and when execution-bound a new execution generation and handoff, never a mutation of the old binding. Later enrichment needs an exact Scope-published relation to its base bundle; it cannot replace or retroactively satisfy the original required bytes.
Check current disclosure authority and source invalidation at delivery, including after restore and on a retry. A valid signature proves what was issued. A prior read or use receipt records its own event. If the bundle has since lost eligibility, refuse the exact read and retain only the historical evidence its policy allows. Snapshot freshness and revocation
Use is reported by the caller and receipted by Scope
The caller submits a use report naming the bundle and its digest, the caller, the use scope, the task, which items it reports consuming or ignoring and why, the artifacts it reports generating, and any staleness it observed. Only the deferred execution-bound branch carries an execution binding, and it requires the complete object. In standalone mode the report is the body bound by the request admission. In the Pale mode it is the body of the caller-signed common request. Scope validates and deduplicates durably before signing the receipt. The report carries no admission or receipt hash. The receipt binds the admission and the SHA-256 of the report's canonical form as submitted.
An accepted receipt records Scope's validation of the admitted caller's report. It echoes the bundle, caller, use scope, task and the reported items and artifacts. The use scope must match the request and admission. An execution-bound receipt, in the deferred branch, also echoes the complete execution binding and verifies scope against the handoff, session grant and requirement. A duplicate names the original receipt and echoes its accepted evidence. A rejected receipt carries a bounded reason and no accepted evidence. Pale's federation members in the binding are both present or both absent, and reusing a report identifier or admission with a changed body conflicts. Golden vectors cover empty optional evidence, changed scope, reordered items and null. The deferred branch also needs exact and partial execution-binding cases. Model visibility takes separate harness evidence. Outcomes and causal claims require their own evidence.
An executing agent reads the context already bound to its handoff
The executing agent reads the exact bundle bound to its handoff through an authenticated request. It later reports which items it used and receives Scope's receipt. The command forms below are the design of the command line; none of it exists yet, because the kernel is an empty library. Native development manual
scope read --request-ref <authenticated bundle-read request> --format json
scope report-use  --report-ref  <context use report>

Provider commands and credentials go through separately admitted Pale or owner capabilities; Scope offers neither. An agent cannot issue a fresh first-turn resolve and claim that the handoff bound its result. Context survives session rotation and compaction by re-reading the same immutable bytes, never by history or a silent refresh. How many tokens a model's context window holds, how a harness compacts and what rate limits apply are facts about the selected harness and model; Scope obeys the declared bundle budget with headroom and holds no universal allocation. A pre-run injection of the same bound bytes, where an execution owner offers one, may never resolve, refresh or substitute different bytes. Any Skill that teaches this procedure is owned and released outside Scope, and Scope may only propose changes to it.
An episode is opened before resolve and bound once to its handoff
For work tied to an execution, the order is strict:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Owner as Execution owner
  participant Scope
  participant Bridge as Admitted bridge through Pale
  participant Exec as Executing agent
  Owner->>Owner: commit the reservation
  Owner->>Scope: open request (reservation, requirement, fence, expiry policy)
  Scope-->>Owner: open receipt, provisional revision 1
  alt Exact bundle
    Bridge->>Scope: resolve against the reservation and requirement
    Scope-->>Bridge: signed bundle
  else Authorised degraded
    Owner->>Owner: verify signed degradation evidence
  end
  Owner->>Owner: sign the handoff with the selected evidence
  Owner->>Scope: handoff-bind request
  Scope-->>Owner: bind receipt, revision 2
  Owner->>Owner: durably admit the handoff, start the child
  opt Exact bundle
    Exec->>Scope: read the bound bundle, later report use
    Scope-->>Exec: use receipt
  end

Scope opens revision one with the exact reservation, requirement, fence, expiry policy and clock basis and no context evidence. The open receipt must match the reservation and fence before either assisted branch proceeds. An exact-bundle handoff binds the signed resolve result. An authorised-degraded handoff binds the named policy's signed degradation evidence and has no resolve, bundle read or use receipt of its own. A limited retrieval result still needs exact-bundle admission if the handoff binds its bytes.
Scope admits the bind request only against revision one with empty context evidence. It advances the open episode to revision two with exactly one context variant matching the handoff and signs the bind receipt. Both assisted variants need that receipt before dispatch. A context-independent handoff carries the owner's signed classification and creates no Scope episode, bind, bundle or use receipt.
Both requests are typed bodies inside a caller-signed common request issued by the admitted execution owner, whose identity must equal the reservation's issuer. A bridge may carry or verify the owner's signed request. One episode identity can have only one initial revision. Scope returns the original receipt when an admitted replay matches the original open request identifier and digest. A new open request for the same episode, or changed bytes under the original identifier, conflicts. For binding, Scope matches the request identifier and digest on replay and checks the exact expected revision and digest for a new request. A new bind request after a successful bind conflicts. committed requires every committed-episode field, and conflict or rejected forbids them. The revision, request and receipt commit together. Each episode binds one handoff. Later revisions preserve the context evidence, reservation, handoff and binding hashes byte for byte and may only append outcome and use evidence.
In the deferred branch the store keeps the complete canonical signed bytes of each episode revision and a head keyed by the selected identity. Normalised indexes must match the parsed signed record before commit. An append and head advance commit together, comparing both the prior revision number and digest. A failed swap rolls both back. Diagnostics and scoring stay outside the signed record.
An episode ends once, either closed or expired
Before closing an episode or recording late terminal evidence, Scope verifies the execution owner's native commit and matches the event to the exact episode, attempt, fence and handoff. A provisional open has no handoff to match. The carrier's observation and an organiser's acceptance are separate records. Scope commits the episode update and inbox disposition together and returns the original disposition on exact replay.
Expiry and closure compete to advance the same revision. Only one can commit a terminal transition. A closed record has a closing time, an expired record has an expiry time, and either terminal state stays fixed. Expiry needs an accepted Pale request bound to the exact open revision, expiry policy and clock evidence. It succeeds only when the evaluated time reaches the policy deadline and the expected revision still matches. Exact replay returns the recorded disposition. Reusing the request identity with changed bytes is refused. A schedule declared in Weave may invoke the check through Pale, following Weave → Pale → execution. The owner's policy supplies the deadline, reason and clock basis, and Scope signs the resulting revision. A process clock, mutable timeout table or adapter's wall clock cannot substitute for that evidence.
A terminal event that arrives after expiry is kept in a successor revision as late evidence. It cannot rewrite the status, mint a closing time or become scoring or authority evidence automatically; its review fields stay absent until an applicable authority admits it for a bounded purpose, and even then the lifecycle does not change.
Outcomes are several facts, never one score
Process termination, a verifier's result, acceptance of the task, acceptance by whoever organised it, the owner's approval and satisfaction of the goal are separate owner facts. They answer different questions: a later approval does not erase a failed verifier, and a successful attempt does not imply acceptance or satisfaction of the goal. The owner's observed outcome takes priority over a labelled proxy answering the same question; reported use, a model's judgment or frequent retrieval cannot replace it. Each outcome may be appended to a closed or expired episode in a successor revision without overwriting another, imposing an order across different questions, rewriting the source event or reopening the work. Missing evidence stays missing.
Any scalar used for evaluation is a versioned projection for one declared question, never accepted truth. The initial feature map for terminal process categories is a successful finish as +1.0, a failure as −0.5, a timeout as −0.3 and a cancellation as 0 with no credit; it lives in the scoring configuration, changes only through a Scope proposal and release, and never changes the source event or the episode's own lifecycle. Where coordination work is later evaluated, three dimensions stay separate: how useful the coordination was, what it cost, and whether the owner's stated goal was met. Scope preserves references to each and never mints a goal-level approval or a second graph of goals; the owner-published acceptance and satisfaction evidence it would join is still to be defined.
Which owner gives an episode its identity is still open
The issuing owner and successor run-identity contract remain open decisions. The contract must distinguish an organiser's acceptance, such as Weave accepting parent work, from the executor's terminal event. Scope follows the approved identity and signs only its own revisions.
Until that contract is approved and published:
Independently admitted requests can still resolve context, read the exact signed bundle and receipt reported use without an execution binding.
Scope cannot open, bind or close an execution episode. The episode family and execution-bound request and receipt branches stay out of the independent contract checkpoint. Outcome-weighted scoring has no episode input.
Evidence from a direct Claude Code or Codex path, or from Gas Town without an organising owner, may still enter a research export by exact owner references, and no episode is ever fabricated for it.
Three rules carry into whatever owner is chosen: outcome evidence stays several separate facts, resolving context never creates an episode, and an agent that loses its working memory re-reads the immutable bundle rather than trusting a summary. Scope's own continuity, separate stores for each system's memory, and its refusal to write another owner's store also carry over unchanged.
Part of Scope engineering.

Evidence export and Reckon
Scope's research-export design lets a researcher examine evidence from real work while keeping private material under its owners' permissions. Scope signs an export containing only the derived evidence and exact source references allowed for that purpose, with exact references to every required permission. This is the admission check for the export. Real operation can reveal conditions a synthetic test misses; using that evidence for training needs its own permission.
An export can inform a separately frozen case, which Scope may propose to Reckon's official corpus. Reckon alone accepts the proposal and creates the canonical corpus record. The export, case, proposal and corpus record keep separate identities. Each further use, including evaluation, training, a ruling, release or activation, needs its own authority. The source owner's privacy, consent and permitted-use records govern each use; admission checks authority before access.
An export is a membrane, not a query
The export family is a signed request from an admitted research requester and a signed export from Scope. It is a derived-evidence boundary: not a database query, a connector, a training pipeline or an execution episode. The request binds independently issued authority evidence, and the export contains only minimised derived evidence or exact opaque references that the request admits, as the same or a narrower projection of the request and its authority set. Check owner, caller, purpose, fixed source revision and member eligibility separately. Select permitted members before counts, limits, pagination, summaries or archive assembly; metadata and errors obey the same visibility. Refuse unknown revisions and unsupported required members, and disclose optional omissions only within the permitted scope. Bind order, tie-breaks, limits and any cursor to that scope and revision. Recheck permission and source invalidation before staged delivery. The field sketches are on Record reference.
Test overlapping identifiers from different sources, a member outside the grant, wrong caller or purpose, stale revision or cursor, empty selection and an unsupported option. Changes outside the selected scope must not leak through content, counts, errors or attachments. Repeat against the same fixed source to check deterministic order and limits, then revoke permission between staging and inspection. Keep the source and output identities, effective scope, allowed omissions, retention and invalidation rules with the export.
Permitted use is an allowlist, not a ladder. Recorded source or runtime use, context retention, evaluation, calibration, training, fine-tuning, a derivative checkpoint or model, reusable generalisation and publication are separate permissions. Runtime use does not imply retention or evaluation; evaluation does not imply training; training does not imply a derivative, generalisation, publication, release or activation. Every authority role the export policy requires (source owner, data controller, relationship, confidentiality, consent, rights, and research, training, derivative, generalisation and publication use) must resolve to an independently valid record. Scope cannot manufacture any of them by re-signing, and empty selectors mean empty, never all.
One provenance class per export. Real operational evidence and synthetic simulation evidence, such as a RawFish run, are compared only as separately identified corpora and are never pooled under an unlabelled split. Raw prompts, private source payloads, hidden reasoning, credentials, secrets and unrestricted owner records are never export fields. A bounded derivation names its exact inputs, transform, output hash, loss and redaction, and cannot present an inferred outcome as owner truth. Omissions and unknowns are listed explicitly; an unknown is never coerced into absent, false or zero. Each export carries its transform profile, dataset split, leakage report and selection-bias report, and its retention, deletion and expiry.
Execution evidence travels as opaque references. An export may reference a direct Claude Code or Codex path, or a Gas Town path with no organising owner, when each item is an exact admitted Pale or owner record; it does not need, and must never fabricate, an organisation identifier or an episode. An episode that does exist is referenced only by its full identity and exact revision. Execution-path, delegation and terminal-leaf evidence travel as opaque reference and hash pairs to Pale-owned records; Scope binds and compares them but never enumerates their values or parses product names into path structure, and an empty delegation list means the selected path had no delegation. Outcome evidence enters only by exact owner reference; a missing outcome stays an explicit unknown.
Invalidation follows the source. Deletion, revocation, supersession, authority expiry or a change in a source frontier invalidates dependent exports according to the bound policy. Scope records the invalidation or tombstone and requires the destination owner's custody and deletion evidence where a copy was materialised; it cannot claim to recall bytes it does not control. An export grants no online read, model update, candidate publication, Pale admission or activation. Private evidence cannot become reusable package or Skill content or a derivative model without its own generalisation or derivative grant, and a reward- or candidate-generating evaluator can never be the only evaluator for a promotion.
A Causality research consumer requires the affected owners' approval, a defined experiment and candidate class, and separate data permission. Under that proposed connection, Causality owns only a preregistered matched comparison, MUON and HENA keep their own research artifacts, and Reckon provides evaluation and, for a learned promotion, the required curated case and recorded decision. A result returns to Pale only as evidence for a new admission decision, never as a Scope memory proposal. Describing this connection grants none of its required permissions.

A case is proposed to Reckon's corpus; Reckon alone mints
owner projection or reference
  -> Scope admits a case and freezes a secret-free revision
  -> Scope verifies source, controller, purpose, consent, privacy, rights and model-use records
  -> bounded case proposal to Reckon
  -> Reckon's curator disposition
  -> for an eligible accepted case only: Reckon mints the canonical record and version
  -> exact version plus an authorised-use grant
  -> Reckon's corpus-use receipt, and Scope's own consumption record

Scope may assemble and freeze one bounded, secret-free case revision from its admitted projections and exact owner references. Before proposing it, Scope verifies the independent source-owner, controller, purpose, confidentiality, consent, privacy, rights and model-use records and keeps their exact references, hashes, scope, destination, validity and supersession state; it neither issues nor widens them. Missing, stale, expired, conflicting or purpose-mismatched authority yields a fail-closed non-proposal. The proposal carries only the frozen case's identity and digest, provenance, omissions and unknowns, permission references, the requested corpus purpose and the requested retention and use scope; credentials, raw private payloads, hidden reasoning, mutable source pointers and unbounded provider access are prohibited.
Reckon owns curator disposition, minting and the corpus-use receipt. Scope records the exact disposition by reference. Before consumption, verify the case and input revision, digest, accepted reference answer, current status and permission for the consumer, purpose, scope, destination, model use and time. Keep original annotations, corrections, adjudications and accepted answers distinct; a correction needs a successor revision. Fix dataset membership and partitions by exact case identities, revisions and digests, grouping related sources or derivatives to prevent leakage. Unreviewed, deferred, conflicting, denied or withdrawn items remain outside the accepted set. An unavailable item leaves a coverage gap rather than silently acquiring a replacement.
Scope records its own consumption and matches the fixed input and run identity to Reckon's use receipt. Inspecting an old receipt, reconstructing its inputs and using those bytes in a new run require separate permission. An unchanged digest, earlier receipt, restored snapshot or cached grant cannot override current withdrawal or expiry. Hold dependent use when current authority cannot be established. Before exposing a result, recheck the exact recipient, result and current grant, resolving any withdrawal race under the owner's ordering rules. Preserve earlier receipts only as retention permits, record withheld delivery separately from processing already observed, and invalidate dependent evidence from exact lifecycle references.
Test matching use, permission for a different purpose or destination, an expired or withdrawn revision, a receipt for another run, a restored but now-ineligible copy, a lost delivery acknowledgement followed by withdrawal, and permission changing between acceptance and delivery. Refusal exposes no protected result. A permitted replacement needs separately accepted inputs and its own receipt. An ordinary research comparison may use a separately permitted Scope export where its experiment allows it. A learned promotion still requires its curated case in Reckon's shared set.
Use published results without a live Reckon dependency
Pale and Scope use published, versioned Reckon results when making decisions. Scope may select a published calibration table or case set for a permitted use, records its exact version, and continues from that version when Reckon is unavailable. Scope owns how the result informs its decision; source permissions, eligibility and the learned-promotion rule still apply. The consumer must pin the published result format, check it at use and exercise an outage with that retained version in the go-live rehearsal.
Reckon evaluates learned changes and preserves the decision
Every learned change requires Reckon's evaluation, a curated case and the responsible owner's preserved decision. Ordinary work and changes the owner authors directly remain independent. Reckon is not Scope's runtime, store, authority or online learner. No Reckon process writes Scope's source, ledger, episode, score, proposal, deletion, supersession or release state; Scope never imports Reckon's Python runtime into its hot path or treats Reckon's in-memory store as durable memory; and Reckon never gets live Scope reads, provider access, a caller identity, credentials or a mutation path.

Case assembly, admission and freezing	Scope	Creates no corpus membership	
Source, controller, purpose, rights and model-use admission	Each named authority	Scope and Reckon verify and never issue, widen or infer	
Curator disposition and minting	Reckon	Mint certifies corpus identity and curation, not truth

Every evaluator candidate binds a unique identifier that is never reused, its source revision and content digest, formula and configuration version, input schema, numeric domain and missing-value rules, deterministic reference vectors and parity tolerance, the outcome evidence it may use, dataset split and leakage controls, resource limits and failure disposition, and its output schema and digest. An evaluator name or the phrase "causal score" is not evidence of causal identification; a candidate may carry a causal label only under Reckon's accepted causal-evidence profile, and otherwise it is called ablation, attribution, proxy or ranking evidence. Signed, zero, near-zero, non-finite and empty inputs need explicit behaviour, and an undefined domain, unsafe normalisation or missing adversarial vectors makes a candidate ineligible rather than coercing a score. Improvement and go-live separates Scope's scorer, retrieval-policy and memory candidates from Pale's instruction candidates; Reckon owns the published evaluator contract each comparison pins.
Scope preregisters the experiment and freezes its permitted evidence. For a learned candidate it binds the curated case version, and Reckon evaluates the candidate and signs the result. Bind the source and configuration, data lineage, method and prompt, workflow and adapter, model settings, validator, output schema, execution mode and reference-vector parity. Keep the case, assessment and provider attempt distinct, with raw output, normalised result, evaluator observation and accepted decision separately inspectable. Stage replay fixes upstream outputs; end-to-end replay regenerates them under the candidate. Exclude later labels from decision-time inputs, prevent live effects during replay, and count failed attempts, retries, fallback, shadow calls and review in cost and coverage. A required evaluation that fails, is partial or stale, or cannot be verified holds the dependent proposal. The responsible owner then decides; Reckon preserves the exact decision and returns its reference. Scope verifies it before its separate release. The adaptive go-live rehearsal exercises this whole path. A Reckon outage holds new learned promotion while ordinary Scope work continues.
Scope may also offer Reckon a bounded projection of its edit lineage, when both owners select that relationship: Scope then produces and signs each projection instance against Reckon's published schema, and keeps every original record and all mutation, decision and release authority. Ordinary owner-authored releases remain outside the learned-promotion path. Reckon publishes the record-store protocol: versioned write and retrieval, observation, probes and bounded run export. Scope pins that published contract rather than deriving it from these operation names.
For a comparison across evaluator versions, retain each historical observation with its evaluator, rubric, metric, schema, cases and available evidence. Admit a separate comparison for a shared question, matching case identities and revisions and fixing candidate outputs, independent references and scoring policies. Check common units, criterion meanings, thresholds and missing-case rules; equal labels or numeric ranges do not establish the same measure. Hold the evaluator fixed to compare candidates and outputs fixed to compare evaluators. If both change and interaction matters, score both candidates with both evaluators. Compute a joint difference only on a justified common measure, retaining each evaluator's original findings.
Test changed rubric meaning under the same score label, changed case coverage and an unavailable historical output. Preserve original denominators and disclose incomplete pairs; a matched-subset result applies only to that subset. Scope retains the original artifact references and keeps a proposal that depends on an unresolved comparison pending. A separately admitted comparison that can answer its own question may proceed.
Role confusion is rejected at every step
Tests must show that a Reckon process trying to read or change Scope's store is denied; that an artifact whose candidate, configuration or data changed after preregistration is rejected before comparison; that a candidate failing parity or its numeric domain is recorded ineligible with no fallback score; that a scalar outcome without its underlying terminal and acceptance evidence is excluded; that a passing experiment produces at most a proposal while production stays byte-identical until a separate release; that a rejection, timeout or partial evaluation leaves the scorer and ledger unchanged; that a research run presented as a Scope experiment, or the reverse, is rejected; that evidence from a path with no organising owner assigned a synthetic episode, mixed real and synthetic provenance, or evaluation permission widened to training is rejected; that Reckon attempting training, candidate selection, live judgment, foreign persistence, admission, approval or release is denied; that a case with missing, stale or conflicting permission, credentials, hidden reasoning, a mutable source identity or a widened purpose is rejected before review; and that a proposal, disposition, mint, use grant, use receipt, evaluation, ruling or release is never presented as another of those states.
Part of Scope engineering.

Improvement and go-live
Scope improves offline: freeze the permitted evidence, propose a change, measure it independently, obtain the owner's decision, release the chosen bytes and activate them separately. The optimiser cannot change its own test. Scope owns changes to its scorer, retrieval policy and memory; Pale's SkillOpt owns improvements to the agent instructions for using Scope.
Scope requires the complete adaptive system and its offline rehearsal before go-live. Every learned promotion requires all three Reckon roles: evaluation, a curated case in the shared set, and preservation of the responsible owner's authenticated decision. Evidence export and Reckon defines those responsibilities. Ordinary deterministic work remains independent. The rehearsal includes release, simulated activation and forward rollback, and ends with the deterministic policy still active.
Outcome evidence is several facts, and a reward is only a projection
An owner's committed event can close an episode without anyone transcribing it, but that is capture, not a correctness oracle. Process termination, a verifier's result, the task's acceptance, the organiser's acceptance, the owner's approval and goal satisfaction stay distinct references, and no transform or universal order turns one into another. A declared evaluation may map eligible evidence to the unit interval for one declared question, recording the evidence class, the mapping version and what it excluded; missing evidence stays missing, and any derived reward must be reproducible from the complete referenced evidence. It can never outrank the evidence or promote a proposal. The source-event mapping keeps the raw terminal category, normalisation happens only in a versioned projection, and no optimisation loop ever writes episode or outbox tables; they are read-only inputs.
The scoring loop tunes exactly two artifacts
For A-MAC-lite, exactly two artifacts are tunable, both kept as configuration data on port 3309: the scoring configuration (half-lives, priors, the novelty and confidence thresholds and weights) and the feature map for terminal process categories. One cycle runs in eight steps:
Snapshot. Record the exact input roots, and optionally tag the store as opt-{cycle}-pre, an audit and replay reference and never a rollback mechanism.
Propose at most the edit budget's number of bounded edits.
Evaluate by replay on the held-out split. Inverse-propensity estimates are used only for rows whose logging-policy version and non-zero action propensity were durably recorded; deterministic logs support observed replay and bounded sensitivity analysis, never claims about unshown alternatives.
Gate the result against metrics and safety tests fixed in advance.
Record a versioned proposal together with every rejected candidate and its measured difference from the baseline on the held-out split.
Review. The responsible owner accepts or rejects; the evaluation cannot approve itself.
Apply an accepted proposal only through a separate, owner-authorised release.
Resume deterministically if the cycle was killed.
The edit budget and any decay rule belong to the immutable experiment policy and need measured justification. Every edit stays inside the scorer's full domain; an edit outside it is rejected as an invalid candidate, never clipped into a different one. The improvement loop's own settings (the edit budget, the gate metric, the split) are outside what it may edit. Keep rejected edits and their measured differences so Reckon can evaluate the edit lineage. As in SkillOpt's candidate comparison, that buffer keeps evidence of unsuccessful alternatives available rather than showing only the winning edit.
Retrieval policy has its own optimiser, and SkillOpt is not it
Scope owns a bounded offline optimiser for retrieval: affinity, which optional routes to run and with what effort, and fusion and budget. It follows the same separation:
frozen retrieval-decision evidence
  -> compare the deterministic incumbent and transparent affinity candidate
     alongside a memory-host candidate when selected
  -> Reckon corpus admission and independent evaluation
  -> Scope's retrieval-policy proposal
  -> the responsible owner's authenticated ruling
     -> reject or defer: retain the ruling and leave the active policy in place
     -> accept: Reckon preserves the responsible owner's authenticated decision
        -> Scope's policy release with a rollback anchor
        -> a separate activation decision

The optimiser cannot edit eligibility, required context, source facts, freshness or revocation, privacy or model-use limits, the evidence policy or split, hard budgets, the evaluator, the owner's decision interface or its own acceptance criteria. Every candidate binds its exact base policy, snapshot and evidence, including its rejected alternatives. A newly fetched paper, model or repository revision may suggest a candidate; compilation and evaluation use only the immutable inputs admitted for that run. Changed inputs require a separately identified run. Each owner supplies the outcome facts it controls. For the same question, an owner's observed outcome takes precedence over a labelled proxy such as reported use, follow-up or model judgment; different outcome questions remain separate. Counterfactual claims need the exact eligible set and propensity evidence.
SkillOpt is Pale's mechanism for evolving packages and Skills. It may consume minimised Scope evidence through Pale for a package or Skill target and never trains, selects, releases or activates Scope's retrieval policy. Scope does not call SkillOpt, CodeGraph or Reckon directly, none of them writes Scope, and a SkillOpt run in Pale's integrated flow receives only minimised semantic and use lineage through Pale's evaluation manifest. None of these loops may train or emit a model; a model-training hypothesis leaves only through the research export on Evidence export and Reckon.
For Pale's own coordination, Scope keeps two proposal channels apart: quantitative changes to declared numeric policy settings, and qualitative changes to doctrine, manifests, relationships or plans. Both use immutable evidence and an evaluator policy the learner cannot edit; the owner decides first; the artifact's own owner commits and releases; and Scope records only the ruling reference and the release lineage. Scope is never the owner of Pale's policy or of any artifact it did not make.
Every accepted change is released forward and can be rolled back forward
Restoring a retained policy requires a new decision, release record, cycle checkpoint and anchor advance. Recheck the old artifact against current permissions, scope, dependencies and compatibility; its historical digest alone cannot make it eligible. Stage it away from the active path, bind the recovery decision to the expected predecessor and activate under a new identity and fence. Preserve the failed generation, its outcomes, current revocations and committed history. Existing pinned work finishes only while its permissions and required inputs remain valid. Test permitted reuse, a changed predecessor, invalidated permission or dependency, interrupted activation and an ambiguous reply reconciled before retry. The optimiser never mutates live configuration, weights or memory items. Proposals and releases are separate immutable records, and Reckon preserves the owner's decision independently under the promotion rule.

Record design remains implementation work. The field sketches must be consolidated before publication while preserving the information required by this chain. Scope needs a cycle checkpoint, its scoring and memory proposals, a release and any required equivalence evidence. The checkpoint advances through snapshotted, candidate generated, evaluated, proposals persisted and complete; restart resumes the first incomplete stage without regenerating identities or timestamps. Scope's own proposals map to their releases as follows:
Proposal	What it changes	Base it binds	How it is released	
Scoring proposal	The scoring configuration or the category feature map	The exact base artifact and version	Scope commits the bytes and the release record atomically	
Memory proposal	Compaction, merge, supersession or tombstone of memory items	The sorted complete set of source items and their versions	Scope commits atomically after the semantic owner accepts	
A release must carry byte-identical candidate bytes, or an owner-signed equivalence record proving a declared deterministic transformation; changed, unevaluated bytes need a new proposal, and base drift conflicts rather than rebasing. A proposal whose evaluation did not pass cannot receive an accepting decision; one proposal takes at most one accepting decision and one decision at most one release. Proposal identity is unique over the cycle, its checkpoint and input roots, the proposal identifier and the proposer's key epoch. An edit-history export for Reckon distinguishes a proposal, a decision with its preserved record, and a release. The final names and signing domains belong to the published contract definitions.
Compaction is a proposal, never a deletion
Compaction produces a derived proposal and never destroys source lineage. Omitting or deleting an accepted item needs an owner-reviewed tombstone that keeps the minimum lineage needed for supersession, stale-use rejection and invalidating dependents; no score or model can approve that tombstone, and canonical Skills, owner statements, rulings, assignments and effect receipts are never rewritten automatically. Deletion is asymmetric: deleting a source, tombstoning an item, revoking a permission or invalidating freshness invalidates every dependent snapshot, embedding, affinity feature and cache, while deleting a snapshot or affinity creates no tombstone and changes no truth.
Output mentions are a labelled feature, and transcripts are redacted first
Mentions in an agent's output are an optional derived feature. An accepted use receipt records the admitted caller's report, and independent execution evidence is needed to establish model-visible input. Scope never scrapes another owner's transcripts. An owner-native exporter may provide a redacted, versioned derivation joined to the full episode identity. Only the subset supported by that derivation, its exact profile reference and hash, and the source digest may populate the output-reference candidates. If either that evidence or the admitted join is missing, the field stays empty; Scope never guesses. Redaction is mandatory and fails closed: it runs before any transcript is parsed, a redaction failure aborts that transcript entirely, and no raw transcript text ever reaches Scope's store, only item references and derived features. Any learned-credit experiment must test whether mentions are a valid feature at all.

The agent instructions improve through Pale's SkillOpt
SkillOpt improves Packages and Skills; Scope's optimiser improves retrieval. The Package teaching an agent to request context, read the exact bundle and report use belongs to Pale's Package improvement path. It may use permitted, minimised Scope evidence, with redaction and a complete run identity where applicable. Pattern mining, replay, staged edits, held-out comparison and owner adoption belong to that path, including the package owner's release and the checks before an agent receives it. Scope neither stages the package nor claims an atomic change across the two stores.
Validation is necessary and never sufficient
Every proposed artifact passes measured validation before the responsible owner reviews it, and passing never decides for that owner. Killing proposal generation before or after it appends to the ledger changes no live state and resumes deterministically; rejected, expired and superseded proposals cannot be replayed as accepted; base drift invalidates a proposal rather than rebasing it; compaction proposals keep source digests, information-loss reports and lineage; evaluation fixtures span controllers, organisations, relationships and task classes without leaking hidden scope through metrics; and deleted payload cannot be rebuilt from proposal caches, transcript derivations or diagnostics unless retention allows it. Ungated optimisation is not allowed at all.
One command runs the offline cycle, and one owner schedules it
The offline scoring and retrieval cycle is a Scope capability, with scope optimize as its intended command. Weave holds its schedule at a cadence the operator selects; away-work follows Weave → Pale → execution, with Pale governing and supervising execution. Standalone Scope keeps an explicit operator command. There is no default nightly run or competing cron, launchd or systemd entry. The operator may launch the go-live rehearsal explicitly; a later schedule needs its own declared capability and permission and does not approve or activate its result.
Freeze the comparison's exact case snapshot, method, workflow, model settings, validator, output schema and execution mode. Keep the assigned path, observed provider calls, fallback, raw output and evaluation result distinct, with failures and retries included in cost and coverage. Stage replay holds upstream outputs fixed; end-to-end replay regenerates them under the candidate without live effects. Scope supplies the pinned retrieval policy and snapshot, the requested mode, and the receipt for a permitted strict fallback or a refusal when full mode is required. Evaluation evidence, the rehearsal and the certificate govern acceptance.
Before starting or resuming a bounded offline optimisation, establish the target state, permitted observations and actions, and why another iteration can use new evidence. Inspect the actual process or session handle; an old record or timeout does not prove that it is still running. Give attempts, time, cost, rate, concurrency, stored state and effects separate budgets, with a no-progress rule, stale-work check, intervention owner, safe ending and recovery point. Reconcile an uncertain earlier effect before repeating it. Stop on lost permission, exhausted budget, an unreconciled effect or repeated failure from the same cause. Test progress, duplicate work, safe replay and shared errors between generation and judgment. Scope owns the run and its evidence. Scheduling and proposal adoption follow their separate gates.
Go-live is a full rehearsal through rollback, done offline
Scope's compiler and one immutable, request-pinned snapshot are required for go-live, along with an offline rehearsal of the adaptive machinery. Compare the deterministic incumbent with a transparent evidence-weighted affinity and planner candidate. Include a memory-host-assisted candidate if selected and permitted by the evidence rights. Freeze the controller-, purpose- and rights-bounded evidence set, apply the same hard budgets, splits and fixtures, and keep every rejected alternative. The adaptive rehearsal then exercises Reckon's corpus admission and use, independent evaluation, Scope's proposal, the responsible owner's authenticated ruling, custody, Scope's policy release, the compatibility and readiness handshake with Pale, simulated activation and forward rollback. Prove that a Reckon outage holds up a new learned promotion while ordinary deterministic work continues, that the baseline runs without packages or packs, and that Scope and Pale release and activate independently.
Certification also requires the integrated full retrieval path with Counsel's memory host and its declared degradation, even when the policy comparison uses only model-free candidates. Standalone strict mode has its own proof without a Pale daemon. Standalone full mode links Pale's Counsel port library and calls the host selected in Scope's configuration; it must pass the host's independent processing-permission and failure checks. Architecture fixes those two routes, and Retrieval governs artifact eligibility and fallback.
The handshake identifies both owners, deployments, immutable releases, contracts, required capabilities, scope and permitted degradation. Each owner still authorises and verifies its own activation. Bind a request to one current permitted pair through completion; a new head cannot silently replace half that pair. Test both activation orders, an old handshake reused for a new pair, activation between acceptance and reply, revocation or outage during a request, and a response from the wrong deployment or generation. Check the actual pair and separately tested standalone operation after an integration failure.
Read back the release from each intended target, checking the active identity and served bytes or behaviour separately from build status and dispatch acknowledgement. Retain the accepted starting state, intended release, attempt and independent inspection. Test a lost reply after an update, a reachable endpoint serving the predecessor and a partially inspected target set. Reconcile the original attempt before retry or rollback; a currently old state does not erase earlier success or uncertainty. Report missing targets and keep wider activation pending when required inspection is absent. The certificate below defines the evidence Scope requires.
The certificate requires deterministic rebuilds with one pinned snapshot per request; every route with stable fusion; a useful strict mode and a declared memory-host degradation; freshness and revocation fencing with no mixed heads; complete eligible-set evidence for the governed window; isolation by controller, relationship, purpose and model use; lawful deletion and explicit loss of reconstructibility; native release, handshake, independent activation and rollback; corpus admission, independent evaluation, an authenticated ruling preserved by Reckon, with no self-promotion; and the standalone and direct-owner paths intact. The learned policy stays switched off at the end, unless a later, separately authorised release and activation select it.
A single canonical, authenticated owner-ruling contract may be reached through several admitted interfaces, such as Reckon presenting the review packet or an explicit action in Buzz. Ordinary chat, task completion, a parent task being accepted and a merge in Gas Town are never rulings. Every enabled interface needs positive, negative and replay proofs, and disabled interfaces keep their fixtures so that turning one on later cannot invent semantics.
Safe endings are a deterministic bundle, an explicit no-context answer, a policy-permitted limited retrieval result with visible limitations, a refusal where context is required, a demand for a rebuild, a rejected successor, a rejected or expired proposal, a candidate waiting for Reckon, a release left switched off, a completed rollback and a decision marked unreconstructible after lawful deletion. A partial build, mixed generations, unknown authority, stale required context, a missing candidate preimage, unproved vector isolation or changed unevaluated bytes is never a successful ending. The shortcuts that stay forbidden are reading source stores or credentials from Scope; making Scope a bus, keyring, provider router, scheduler or genealogy store; ranking before eligibility or treating relevance as permission; compiling truth out of affinity or model output; treating packages, packs, SkillOpt, Reckon, Counsel or Pale as the owner of Scope's retrieval; treating a webhook, poll, Nostr delivery, watcher or cache age as truth; treating use, evaluation, a merge, a release or an event acknowledgement as settlement or activation; and claiming implementation from planning prose, filenames, research or a rehearsal.
Part of Scope engineering.
